dieu_for_elohim.french: Mon Dieu a envoyé son ange
dieu_for_elohim.form: Aramaic ʾĕlāhî, singular noun + singular verb

items.canon_french: Au commencement Elohim créa les cieux et la terre

reading_quotes.french: Elohim, injustement traduit dans certaines Bibles par Dieu, veut dire en Hébreu «ceux qui sont venus du ciel» et est bel et bien au pluriel
Ils ont «créé», découvert en réalité, la terre

items.reading_summary: Elohim is a plural = scientists from another world; 'created' the earth really means 'discovered' a suitable planet.

load_bearing.gloss: noun, plural in form
load_bearing.comment: Plural morphology is real; French keeps the word untranslated, as does the Hebrew.

load_bearing.gloss: qal perfect 3rd masc. SINGULAR, 'created/shaped'
load_bearing.comment: The verb governed by Elohim is singular in Hebrew; French 'créa' is singular too. The canon's 'découvert en réalité' overrides the verb in both languages.

load_bearing.gloss: the skies and the earth/land
load_bearing.comment: Two objects of bārāʾ; the canon's reading silently drops 'the skies' as an object of the 'discovery'.

items.analysis: The plural FORM of Elohim is in the Hebrew (hebrew-supported as far as it goes), but the predicate is singular (bārāʾ), so the verse itself gives no plural agreement; the French reproduces that faithfully. The gloss 'ceux qui sont venus du ciel' is not a lexical sense of the word (core woh-claim-0009 already labels it a canonical gloss). 'Créé = découvert' is an explicit re-definition by the canon, resting on neither the Hebrew nor the French. The project English ('the Elohim began to shape') carries a definite article not in the Hebrew of this verse (no article on ʾĕlōhîm).

items.ref_note: Quotation carries no reference; it is Gen 1:2b.
items.canon_french: Et l’esprit d’Elohim planait au-dessus des eaux

reading_quotes.french: Ils effectuèrent des voyages de reconnaissance et ce que vous pourriez appeler des satellites artificiels étaient mis en place autour de la Terre

items.reading_summary: Reconnaissance flights and artificial satellites placed around the Earth, then covered by water and thick mists.

load_bearing.gloss: breath / wind / spirit of Elohim
load_bearing.comment: rûaḥ is one word for wind, breath and spirit; French 'esprit' chooses the immaterial sense. The same Hebrew word is 'esprit' again at Gen 6:3 (TBWTT-2:52) and 'vent' at Gen 8:1 (TBWTT-2:63).

load_bearing.gloss: piel participle fem. sing., 'hovering/fluttering'
load_bearing.comment: Feminine singular participle agreeing with rûaḥ: one hovering thing, durative. 'Planait' is a fair rendering; the hovering-over-the-waters image is in the Hebrew.

load_bearing.gloss: over the face of the waters
load_bearing.comment: French drops 'face/surface'.

ellipsis.cut: The canon quotes only the last clause of v.2, omitting 'the earth was tōhû wābōhû, and darkness over the face of the deep' (its prose 'entièrement recouverte d’eau et de brumes épaisses' paraphrases that).

items.analysis: The hook is the hovering of something belonging to Elohim over the waters, and that is the Hebrew's own image (participle of continuous hovering; subject rûaḥ, grammatically feminine singular). The Hebrew word is physically broader than French 'esprit' (wind/breath), which makes a material hovering thing marginally easier to read from the Hebrew than from the French; but 'satellites' and plural 'voyages' are supplied — the Hebrew has one rûaḥ, not vehicles.

items.canon_french: Elohim vit que la lumière était bonne

reading_quotes.french: Il s’avéra que le soleil chauffait correctement la Terre sans lui envoyer de rayons nocifs

items.reading_summary: The scientists tested whether the sun's radiation was harmful; 'the light was good' = the sun's rays were safe.

load_bearing.gloss: wayyiqtol 3rd masc. SINGULAR, 'and he saw'
load_bearing.comment: Singular verb with Elohim.

load_bearing.gloss: the light, that (it was) good
load_bearing.comment: 'Good' is an evaluation after inspection in both languages; 'light' is ʾôr, not the sun.

ellipsis.cut: Skips v.3 ('Let there be light, and there was light') and v.4b ('and Elohim separated between the light and the darkness').
ellipsis.note: In the Hebrew the light is called into being by command at v.3 (GEN-WOH-1:3) before it is judged good, and the luminaries (sun included) appear only at v.14–16; the canon's reading presupposes an already-shining sun being tested.

items.analysis: The evaluative formula ('saw that … good') is in the Hebrew and is read by the canon as a test result — a possible construal of the wording. But the identification light = solar radiation is supplied: the Hebrew has ʾôr created by fiat three 'days' before the luminaries. French and Hebrew agree; nothing here is translation-dependent.

items.canon_french: Il y eut un soir, il y eut un matin : premier jour

reading_quotes.french: Le «jour» correspond à la période pendant laquelle votre soleil se lève sous le même signe le jour de l’équinoxe de printemps, soit deux mille ans terrestres environ

items.reading_summary: A creation 'day' is a precessional age of about 2,000 years.

load_bearing.gloss: 'day one' (cardinal numeral, no article)
load_bearing.comment: Hebrew has the cardinal 'one', not the ordinal 'first'; French 'premier' normalises it.

load_bearing.gloss: and there was evening and there was morning
load_bearing.comment: Same in both.

load_bearing.gloss: 'and Elohim called the light Day' (the half-verse the canon does not quote)
load_bearing.comment: The unquoted first half of the same verse defines yôm as the light period.

ellipsis.cut: v.5a: 'Elohim called the light Day and the darkness he called Night'.
ellipsis.note: The omitted half-verse is the text's own definition of 'day' as the period of light, bounded by an evening and a morning.

items.analysis: Neither Hebrew nor French carries a hook for a 2,000-year 'day'; the equation is supplied by the canon. The Hebrew is somewhat less hospitable than the isolated French clause because the same verse (first half, omitted) names the light itself 'day' and frames the unit by evening and morning. The cardinal 'day one' vs French 'premier jour' has no bearing on the reading.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] Dhorme's wording of 1:5 (whether 'premier jour' or 'jour un') was not checked against the Pléiade extract.

items.canon_french: Il sépara les eaux qui sont au-dessous du firmament d’avec les eaux qui sont au-dessus du firmament

reading_quotes.french: ils descendirent au-dessous des nuages, tout en restant au-dessus de l’eau. Entre les eaux d’en haut : les nuages, et les eaux d’en bas : l’océan recouvrant toute la Terre

items.reading_summary: The explorers descended below the clouds; waters above = clouds, waters below = the global ocean.

load_bearing.gloss: the rāqîaʿ: something beaten/spread out, an expanse or vault
load_bearing.comment: French 'firmament' (via Latin firmamentum) = a firm vault. The canon's reading never says what the 'firmament' is; it reads only the two waters.

load_bearing.gloss: hiphil wayyiqtol 3rd masc. SINGULAR, 'and he separated'
load_bearing.comment: Singular; the subject is Elohim. An act of dividing, not of moving between.

load_bearing.french: les eaux qui sont au-dessus du firmament
load_bearing.gloss: the waters which are above the rāqîaʿ
load_bearing.comment: In Gen 1:14 (quoted at TBWTT-2:17) the luminaries are set IN the rāqîaʿ, so these waters are above the level of sun and stars — not at cloud height.

ellipsis.cut: The canon drops the opening clause 'Elohim made the rāqîaʿ' (וַיַּ֣עַשׂ אֱלֹהִים֮ אֶת־הָרָקִיעַ֒) and the closing 'and it was so'.
ellipsis.note: The omitted clause makes the firmament a manufactured object that does the separating; without it the sentence reads as a positioning between two bodies of water.

items.analysis: The two-waters structure is in the Hebrew, but the agent's action there is making a rāqîaʿ and dividing — not descending. The clouds identification is supplied, and sits awkwardly with the text's own cosmography, which places the luminaries inside the rāqîaʿ and the upper waters above it. French and Hebrew agree on the quoted clause; the less-favourable element is what the canon's truncation removed.

items.canon_french: Que les eaux de dessous les cieux s’amassent en un seul lieu et qu’apparaisse la Sèche

reading_quotes.french: grâce à d’assez fortes explosions qui ont fait un peu un travail de bulldozers, fait en sorte que de la matière soit enlevée du fond des mers et qu’elle s’amasse au même endroit, ce qui forma un continent

items.reading_summary: Explosions bulldozed sea-floor matter into one heap, forming a single original continent (linked to continental drift).

load_bearing.gloss: niphal jussive 3rd masc. PLURAL, 'let the waters be gathered' — plural verb agreeing with 'waters'
load_bearing.comment: The thing gathered is the WATER. The canon's prose transfers the verb to the matter ('qu’elle s’amasse au même endroit').

load_bearing.gloss: to one place
load_bearing.comment: The 'one place' is where the waters go; the canon derives one continent from it.

load_bearing.gloss: niphal jussive, 'and let the dry (ground) be seen'
load_bearing.comment: The dry ground is exposed/seen, not built.

items.analysis: French and Hebrew say the same thing: waters are gathered into one place and dry ground becomes visible. The canon's reading inverts the grammar (matter, not water, is amassed) while reusing the verb 's’amasser' and the phrase 'au même endroit' from the verse; a single landmass is a possible inference from 'one place' for the waters and singular 'the dry', but the mechanism is supplied. Not translation-dependent.

items.actual_reference: Gen 1:11 (wording of v.11; v.12 repeats it)
items.canon_french: Que la terre produise du gazon, de l’herbe (...) des arbres (...) qui aient en eux leur semence... selon leur espèce

reading_quotes.french: Tous leurs efforts ont porté sur la reproduction
des cellules végétales à partir de rien d’autre que des produits chimiques

items.reading_summary: Laboratory synthesis of plant cells from chemicals; the design effort went into self-reproduction; teams created different plants by region.

load_bearing.french: qui aient en eux leur semence
load_bearing.gloss: 'whose seed is in it'
load_bearing.comment: Self-contained reproduction is explicit in the Hebrew.

load_bearing.gloss: according to its kind
load_bearing.comment: Kind-boundedness explicit (repeated twice in v.12).

load_bearing.gloss: hiphil jussive 3rd fem. sing., 'let the land sprout' — grammatical agent is the land
load_bearing.comment: In the Hebrew (and French) the land, not Elohim, is the producing subject; Elohim only speaks.

ellipsis.cut: Canon's (...) remove 'seed-bearing' (מַזְרִ֣יעַ זֶ֔רַע), 'fruit (trees) making fruit' and 'upon the land'.
ellipsis.note: The cuts shorten the list; the reproduction clause that carries the reading is kept.

items.analysis: The reading's textual hook — plants that carry their own seed and reproduce by kind — is squarely in the Hebrew (and doubled in v.12, including the cut 'seed-seeding' participle, which would have reinforced it). The laboratory/chemicals scenario and the regional teams are supplied. A mild counter-detail common to French and Hebrew: the earth is the grammatical producer.

items.canon_french: Qu’il y ait des luminaires au firmament des cieux pour séparer le jour de la nuit et qu’ils servent de signes pour les saisons, pour les jours et pour les années !

reading_quotes.french: Ils ont pu, en observant les étoiles et le soleil, mesurer la durée des jours, des mois et des années sur la Terre

items.reading_summary: Astronomical observation: they measured Earth's days, months and years from the stars and sun.

load_bearing.gloss: jussive 'let there be luminaries' (singular verb, plural noun)
load_bearing.comment: A coming-into-being formula, identical to 'let there be light'; the canon reads it as observation of existing bodies.

load_bearing.gloss: in the rāqîaʿ of the skies
load_bearing.comment: Luminaries are located IN the rāqîaʿ — relevant to the 'waters above' reading at TBWTT-2:12.

load_bearing.french: qu’ils servent de signes pour les saisons, pour les jours et pour les années
load_bearing.gloss: 'and let them be for signs and for appointed times and for days and years'
load_bearing.comment: Hebrew has four coordinated items (signs AND appointed times AND days and years); the French subordinates ('signes pour les saisons…'). môʿădîm = fixed/appointed times rather than 'seasons'. No word for 'months' in either.

items.analysis: The calendrical function (luminaries as markers for times, days, years) is the Hebrew's own statement, so the time-measurement hook is real. What is supplied: that the verse reports observation rather than making (v.16, unquoted, says Elohim 'made' them), and 'months'. The French follows the Hebrew closely apart from the 'signes pour les saisons' subordination.

items.canon_french: Que les eaux foisonnent d’une foison d’animaux vivants et que les volatiles volent au-dessus de la terre (...)

reading_quotes.french: Ils ont ensuite créé les premiers animaux aquatiques
Après les poissons, ils ont créé les oiseaux

items.reading_summary: Aquatic life first (plankton to large fish, with an ecological balance), then birds under the artists' influence.

load_bearing.french: Que les eaux foisonnent d’une foison
load_bearing.gloss: 'let the waters swarm (with) a swarm' — cognate verb+noun, plural verb agreeing with waters
load_bearing.comment: French 'foisonnent d’une foison' reproduces the Hebrew figura etymologica exactly.

load_bearing.gloss: living being(s) (collective singular)
'and let flyer(s) fly about' (collective singular, no article)
load_bearing.comment: Hebrew ʿôp has no article; the canon's 'les' (core records Dhorme: 'des') is slightly further from the Hebrew than Dhorme.

ellipsis.cut: The canon's (...) removes the end of the verse: 'across the face of the rāqîaʿ of the skies' (עַל־פְּנֵ֖י רְקִ֥יעַ הַשָּׁמָֽיִם).
ellipsis.note: No effect on the fish-then-birds reading; it does remove a third occurrence of the firmament in the quoted verses.

items.french_variance: Core source note: Dhorme reads «des volatiles»; the canon digitization reads «les volatiles».
items.analysis: The order waters-creatures then flyers and the swarming image are the Hebrew's own; the canon's elaborations (plankton, food chains, artists, contests) are supplied. In the Hebrew the waters are the grammatical subject of 'swarm'. The les/des variance against Dhorme is already recorded in core (dhorme-bible source note).

items.ref_note: No quotation and no reference; content of Gen 1:21 narrated.
items.canon_french: Des dragons ou ce que vous avez baptisé des Dinosaures ou autres Brontosaures

reading_quotes.french: Mais d’autres équipes de savants créèrent des animaux épouvantables

items.reading_summary: Other teams created monsters — dragons, i.e. dinosaurs — at the stage adjacent to the birds.

load_bearing.gloss: 'the great tannînîm' (definite plural)
load_bearing.comment: The canon's 'dragons' matches the Hebrew word-class (and Dhorme's rendering per core).

load_bearing.gloss: 'and Elohim created' — singular verb, same subject as the rest of the chapter
load_bearing.comment: In the Hebrew the tannînîm are made by the same subject with the same verb bārāʾ as heaven-and-earth and humankind; no separate agent is marked.

ellipsis.cut: The whole verse is passed over between the quotations of 1:20 and 1:24.
ellipsis.note: Treated in core woh-claim-0073 (dragons-passage-signature); not re-done here.

items.analysis: Already covered by core woh-claim-0073. Added observation only: the Hebrew gives no textual footing for attributing the tannînîm to 'other teams' — the verse has the ordinary singular wayyibrāʾ ʾĕlōhîm and closes with the ordinary approval formula 'Elohim saw that it was good', which sits against the canon's 'animaux épouvantables'. The dragon lexeme itself is hebrew-supported.

items.canon_french: Que la terre fasse sortir des animaux vivants selon leur espèce : bestiaux, reptiles, bêtes sauvages, selon leur espèce !

reading_quotes.french: Après les mers et les airs, ils ont créé des animaux terrestres
Ils ont ensuite créé des carnivores pour équilibrer le peuple des herbivores

items.reading_summary: Land animals next: herbivores first, then carnivores for balance.

load_bearing.gloss: hiphil jussive, 'let the land bring forth'
load_bearing.comment: Land as grammatical producer, as at v.11.

load_bearing.gloss: cattle, creeping thing, and beast of the land
load_bearing.comment: Three classes; no herbivore/carnivore sequence in the wording. 'Reptiles' for remeś ('creeping things') is narrower than the Hebrew.

items.french_variance: Core: TBWTT-2:23 reproduces Dhorme's 1:24 exactly.
items.analysis: The sequence sea – air – land and the land-animal classes are in the Hebrew. The herbivore-then-carnivore sequence is supplied; the verse's three classes are not ordered by diet.

items.canon_french: Faisons l’homme à notre image, à notre ressemblance ! Qu’il ait autorité sur les poissons de la mer

reading_quotes.french: A notre image! Vous pouvez constater que la ressemblance est frappante
chaque race humaine correspond à une équipe de créateurs

items.reading_summary: Humans were made artificially to look like their makers; the physical likeness between the speaker and the narrator is the proof; one team per human race.

load_bearing.gloss: qal cohortative 1st person PLURAL, 'let us make'
load_bearing.comment: Genuine first-person plural in the Hebrew.

load_bearing.french: à notre image, à notre ressemblance
load_bearing.gloss: 'in our ṣelem, according to our dəmût' — both with 1st person PLURAL suffix
load_bearing.comment: ṣelem is the word for a concrete image/statue; the physical-resemblance reading has a lexical basis. Two different prepositions (bə-, kə-) flattened to 'à … à' in French.

load_bearing.gloss: qal jussive 3rd masc. PLURAL, 'and let THEM rule'
load_bearing.comment: Hebrew is plural ('they'); the canon's singular 'Qu’il ait' departs from the Hebrew and (per core) from Dhorme's 'Qu’ils aient'.

load_bearing.gloss: 'and Elohim said' — verb 3rd masc. SINGULAR
load_bearing.comment: The speech-introduction, not quoted by the canon, has a singular verb; the plural is inside the speech.

ellipsis.cut: The canon omits the speech-introduction 'And Elohim said' and, in its list, the Hebrew 'and over all the land' appears as 'sur toutes les bêtes sauvages' (a known emendation following the Syriac, not the MT wording וּבְכָל־הָאָ֔רֶץ).

items.french_variance: Core source note: Dhorme «Qu’ils aient autorité»; canon «Qu’il ait autorité».
items.analysis: This is the strongest plural hook in the Genesis sequence and it is fully in the Hebrew: cohortative plural plus two plural suffixes. The image vocabulary (ṣelem) supports a concrete likeness. Counter-data in the Hebrew that the canon does not quote: the introducing verb is singular, and the fulfilment at 1:27 (GEN-WOH-1:27) switches to singular 'in HIS image' (בְּצַלְמ֔וֹ) with singular בָּרָ֣א. The canon's 'Qu’il ait' is the one place where its French is less accurate than both the Hebrew and Dhorme; it does not bear on the reading.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] That 'sur toutes les bêtes sauvages' follows the Syriac reading against MT 'over all the earth' is standard text-critical lore, not verified here against an apparatus.

items.canon_french: De tout arbre du jardin tu pourras manger, mais de l’arbre de la science du bien et du mal tu n’en mangeras pas, car du jour où tu en mangerais, tu mourrais

reading_quotes.french: tu peux apprendre tout ce que tu voudras, lire tous les livres que nous avons ici à ta disposition, mais ne touche pas aux livres scientifiques sinon tu mourrais

items.reading_summary: Trees = books; the forbidden tree = the scientific books; the first man is kept from science.

load_bearing.french: l’arbre de la science du bien et du mal
load_bearing.gloss: 'and from the tree of the knowing (of) good and bad' — daʿat is a verbal noun 'knowing' taking 'good and bad' as its object
load_bearing.comment: French 'science' (in its older sense 'knowledge') is what the canon then reads in the modern sense 'livres scientifiques'. Hebrew daʿat is general knowing/acquaintance, here specified by the object 'good and bad'.

load_bearing.gloss: infinitive absolute + imperfect, 'you shall surely die'
load_bearing.comment: Hebrew is an emphatic certainty formula; the canon's conditional 'tu mourrais' is weaker.

load_bearing.gloss: infinitive absolute + imperfect, 'you may freely eat'
load_bearing.comment: Eating vocabulary throughout; 'reading/learning' is supplied.

ellipsis.cut: Speech-introduction omitted: 'YHWH Elohim commanded the human, saying' (וַיְצַו֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֔ים, singular verb).

items.analysis: The step from the tree to 'scientific books' passes through the French word 'science'. In the Hebrew the tree is of 'knowing good and bad' (daʿat + object), a phrase about discernment, not a body of technical knowledge; the modern-French resonance science → scientifique has no counterpart in daʿat. Trees-as-books and eating-as-reading are supplied in both languages. The canon's conditional 'tu mourrais' also softens the Hebrew's emphatic death formula.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] Whether Dhorme prints 'science du bien et du mal' and 'tu mourras/mourrais' at 2:17 was not collated; core's inspected extract covers Genesis 1–3 but only selected verses are transcribed in the source note.

items.canon_french: Il amena vers l’homme les animaux pour voir comment il les appellerait

reading_quotes.french: Les créateurs lui apprirent le nom et les pouvoirs de tout ce qui vivait autour de lui : la botanique et la zoologie

items.reading_summary: The creators taught the man the names and properties of plants and animals (botany and zoology being harmless).

load_bearing.gloss: hiphil wayyiqtol 3rd masc. SINGULAR, 'and he brought'
load_bearing.comment: Singular subject YHWH Elohim.

load_bearing.french: pour voir comment il les appellerait
load_bearing.gloss: 'to see what he would call it'
load_bearing.comment: The maker observes; the human does the naming.

load_bearing.original: וְכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִקְרָא־ל֧וֹ הָֽאָדָ֛ם נֶ֥פֶשׁ חַיָּ֖ה ה֥וּא שְׁמֽוֹ
load_bearing.translit: wəkōl ʾăšer yiqrāʾ-lô hāʾādām nepeš ḥayyâ hûʾ šəmô
load_bearing.gloss: 'and whatever the human called it, each living being, that was its name' (clause not quoted by the canon)
load_bearing.comment: Confirms the direction: names originate with the human.

ellipsis.cut: Omits the beginning ('YHWH Elohim formed from the ground every beast of the field and every bird of the skies') and the end ('whatever the human called it, that was its name').
ellipsis.note: The omitted end states outright that the names come from the human, the opposite of the canon's 'lui apprirent le nom'. The omitted beginning has the animals formed AFTER the human, against the Genesis 1 order the canon has just followed.

items.analysis: The canon's gloss (the creators taught him the names) reverses the direction of naming in the verse it quotes: in Hebrew — and already in the French clause quoted ('pour voir comment il les appellerait') — the maker brings the animals to see what the human will call them, and the unquoted clause fixes the human's names as the names. An 'observational test of the created human' would be hebrew-supported (the existing library note says as much); 'taught him the names' is not. Plants ('botanique') are not in the verse.

items.ref_note: Printed 'III, I-5' (roman I for arabic 1); absent from the www citation index, so not linked. The quotation is a splice of 3:1a, 3:3a, 3:4b, 3:5.
items.canon_french: or le serpent (...) dit à la femme (...) du fruit de l’arbre qui est au milieu du jardin (...) vous n’en mourriez pas, mais Elohim sait que, le jour où vous en mangerez, vos yeux se dessilleront et vous serez comme des dieux

reading_quotes.french: Parmi tous les savants de cette équipe, quelques-uns qui aimaient profondément leurs petits hommes
ils seraient aussi forts que leurs créateurs

items.reading_summary: The 'serpent' is a subgroup of the creators who told the young humans they could study science and become equal to their creators.

load_bearing.gloss: 'and the serpent' — definite singular noun
load_bearing.comment: Singular; canon reads a group.

load_bearing.original: מִכֹּל֙ חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֑ים
load_bearing.translit: mikkōl ḥayyat haśśādeh ʾăšer ʿāśâ YHWH ʾĕlōhîm
load_bearing.gloss: '(shrewder) than every beast of the field that YHWH Elohim had made' — the words under the canon's first (...)
load_bearing.comment: The cut clause classes the serpent among the animals that YHWH Elohim made.

load_bearing.gloss: 'like Elohim' — the very same word as the subject of the chapter
load_bearing.comment: The canon's French switches to lower-case 'des dieux' here; the Hebrew has the same word it renders 'Elohim' six words earlier in the same sentence (יֹדֵ֣עַ אֱלֹהִ֔ים).

load_bearing.gloss: 'knowers of good and bad' — masculine PLURAL participle
load_bearing.comment: Not rendered in the canon's quotation (it stops at 'des dieux'). The plural participle agrees either with 'you' (plural) or with ʾĕlōhîm; if the latter, it is a plural modifier of Elohim.

load_bearing.gloss: 'Elohim knows' — participle masc. SINGULAR
load_bearing.comment: Singular agreement in the same verse.

load_bearing.gloss: 'you shall surely not die' (plural 'you')

ellipsis.cut: (1) v.1: 'was the most cunning of all the beasts of the field that YHWH Elohim had made'; (2) the serpent's question and the woman's reply vv.1b–2; (3) v.3b 'Elohim has said: you shall not eat of it nor touch it, lest you die' and the speech-change 'the serpent said to the woman' (v.4) — so that the woman's words ('du fruit de l’arbre qui est au milieu du jardin') run on into the serpent's ('vous n’en mourriez pas'); (4) v.5 end 'knowing good and bad'.
ellipsis.note: The first cut removes the statement that the serpent is one of the animals YHWH Elohim made, which is the text's own obstacle to reading the serpent as a faction of the makers. The splice also merges two speakers into one.

items.french_variance: Inconsistent with itself: the canon keeps 'Elohim' as a name everywhere else in ch. 2 (and in this very sentence) but prints 'des dieux' for the same Hebrew word at the end of 3:5.
items.analysis: Two findings pull in opposite directions. LESS favourable: the Hebrew serpent is singular and is explicitly ranked among 'the beasts of the field that YHWH Elohim had made' — exactly the words the canon's ellipsis removes (the same class-phrase is cut again at Gen 3:14, TBWTT-2:38). MORE favourable: the promise is 'you will be like ELOHIM' (kēʾlōhîm), the same word as the makers' name, which matches the canon's gloss 'aussi forts que leurs créateurs' better than the French 'comme des dieux' the canon actually prints; and the following plural participle 'knowers' may construe with Elohim. The identification serpent = dissenting scientists is supplied in either language.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] Whether 'comme des dieux' is Dhorme's own rendering at 3:5 was not collated against the Pléiade extract.

items.canon_french: Alors se dessillèrent leurs yeux, à tous deux, et ils surent qu’ils étaient nus

reading_quotes.french: Alors ils comprirent qu’ils pouvaient eux aussi devenir des créateurs et en voulurent à leurs pères

items.reading_summary: Their eyes opened = they understood they too could become creators and resented being treated as lab animals.

load_bearing.comment: Same in both.

load_bearing.comment: The content of the new knowledge in the text is nakedness; the canon substitutes 'they could become creators'.

ellipsis.cut: v.7b: 'and they sewed fig leaves and made themselves loincloths'.

items.analysis: The eye-opening/knowing vocabulary is in the Hebrew, but the text specifies what was known (their nakedness) and the canon replaces that object with another. French and Hebrew agree; nothing hangs on the translation.

items.canon_french: Iahvé Elohim dit au serpent : «(...) maudit sois-tu (...) Sur ton ventre tu marcheras et tu mangeras de la poussière tous les jours de ta vie !

items.reading_summary: The serpent = the small group of creators who told the truth; the curse = their sentence of exile on Earth by the home-planet government.

load_bearing.gloss: 'and YHWH Elohim said' — singular verb
load_bearing.comment: Double name present in Hebrew; canon reads it as 'le gouvernement de la planète originelle'.

load_bearing.gloss: 'cursed are you' — 2nd masc. SINGULAR
load_bearing.comment: Singular addressee throughout (also תֵלֵ֔ךְ, תֹּאכַ֖ל, חַיֶּֽיךָ).

load_bearing.gloss: 'above/out of all cattle and all beasts of the field' — the words under the canon's second (...)
load_bearing.comment: Again the clause that places the serpent among the animals is what the ellipsis removes.

load_bearing.gloss: 'on your belly you shall go'
load_bearing.comment: Read by the canon as confinement to the Earth.

ellipsis.cut: (1) 'Because you have done this' (כִּ֣י עָשִׂ֣יתָ זֹּאת֒); (2) 'among all cattle and all beasts of the field'.
ellipsis.note: Second removal of the serpent's animal classification (cf. A-015). With the clause present the curse is a zoological ranking; without it, the sentence can be read as a sentence on persons.

items.french_variance: Here the canon prints the double name 'Iahvé Elohim'; at Gen 3:21 (TBWTT-2:40) the same Hebrew double name is printed as 'Elohim' alone.
items.analysis: The exile reading rests on taking 'on your belly … dust' figuratively as being bound to the ground; that is supplied. The Hebrew is less hospitable than the canon's trimmed French: the addressee is grammatically one individual, and he is cursed 'out of all the cattle and all the beasts of the field' — a comparison class the canon's (...) deletes, here and at 3:1.

items.canon_french: Elohim fit pour l’homme et sa femme des tuniques de peau et les en revêtit

La Bible a conservé ici une phrase à peu près intacte du document originel

load_bearing.gloss: 'and YHWH Elohim made' — singular verb, DOUBLE name
load_bearing.comment: The canon's quotation lacks 'Iahvé': the Hebrew subject is YHWH Elohim, as in 3:14 where the canon prints both.

load_bearing.gloss: tunics of skin
load_bearing.comment: Same.

load_bearing.comment: Singular.

items.analysis: The reading stays close to the plain sense (the makers clothe the pair), so the hook is in the Hebrew. The noteworthy point is that in the one verse the canon singles out as 'à peu près intacte du document originel', its own quotation differs from the Hebrew by dropping the Tetragrammaton from the double name, and the Hebrew verbs are singular against the canon's plural 'Les créateurs'.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] Dhorme presumably prints 'Iahvé Élohim fit' at 3:21; not collated.

items.canon_french: Voici que l’homme est devenu comme l’un de nous

reading_quotes.french: il existe un moyen scientifique de la prolonger très longtemps

items.reading_summary: The makers speak as a group; the tree of life is a scientific means of extreme longevity withheld from humans.

load_bearing.gloss: 'like one of us' — 1st person PLURAL suffix
load_bearing.comment: Genuine plural self-reference; hebrew-supported.

load_bearing.gloss: 'and live forever / for a very long age'
load_bearing.comment: ʿôlām = remote/long duration; the longevity hook is in the Hebrew.

load_bearing.french: il faut éviter qu’il étende sa main
load_bearing.gloss: 'lest he send forth his hand'
load_bearing.comment: Hebrew is an unfinished 'lest…' clause (aposiopesis); the French completes it as a deliberate policy ('il faut éviter que').

load_bearing.gloss: 'and YHWH Elohim said' — singular verb (not quoted)
load_bearing.comment: Plural pronoun inside a speech introduced by a singular verb.

ellipsis.cut: Speech-introduction omitted; see A-020 for the (...) after 'science'.

items.analysis: Both hooks of the reading — a plural 'us' among whom the human now ranks, and a means of living ləʿōlām that must be kept from him — are in the Hebrew wording. 'Scientific means' is the canon's specification. The French 'il faut éviter que' makes the Hebrew's broken-off 'lest' into an explicit decision, which mildly helps the policy reading.

items.canon_french: grâce à la - science (...)

reading_quotes.french: mais ne touche pas aux livres scientifiques sinon tu mourrais
de leur avoir interdit de toucher aux livres scientifiques

items.reading_summary: Man has become like the creators 'thanks to science' — i.e. by gaining scientific knowledge.

load_bearing.gloss: lə + infinitive construct 'to know / in knowing' + object 'good and bad'
load_bearing.comment: Hebrew has a verb form ('knowing good and bad'), not a noun 'science', and no word for 'grâce à'. The canon's (...) falls exactly where the Hebrew object 'good and bad' stands.

ellipsis.cut: The object of the knowing: 'good and bad' (ט֣וֹב וָרָ֑ע) — in French presumably 'du bien et du mal'.
ellipsis.note: With the object removed, 'la science' stands absolute and can be read as science in the modern sense; with it, the phrase is 'the knowledge of good and evil'. Compare 2:17 (TBWTT-2:29) where the canon prints the phrase in full.

items.french_variance: TBWTT-2:29 'l’arbre de la science du bien et du mal' vs TBWTT-2:42 'grâce à la - science (...)' (object cut; stray hyphen in the digitization).
items.analysis: This is the clearest case in the Genesis sequence of a reading produced by the French plus an ellipsis. The Hebrew says the human has become like one of us 'in knowing good and bad' — an infinitive with its object. The canon's text has the noun 'science', a causal 'grâce à' with no Hebrew counterpart, and cuts the object. The canon is also inconsistent with itself: at 2:17 it keeps 'la science du bien et du mal'.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] Dhorme's wording of 3:22 ('grâce à la science du bien et du mal'?) was not collated; the inference that the cut words are 'du bien et du mal' is from the Hebrew.

items.canon_french: Il chassa l’homme et il installa à l’orient du jardin d’Eden les Chérubins et la flamme tournoyante de l’épée pour garder la route de l’arbre de vie

reading_quotes.french: Des militaires possédant des armes atomiques désintégrantes furent placés à l’entrée de la résidence des créateurs

items.reading_summary: Cherubim + flaming sword = soldiers with atomic disintegrating weapons guarding the creators' residence.

load_bearing.gloss: hiphil 3rd masc. SINGULAR, 'and he caused to dwell / stationed'
load_bearing.comment: A stationing verb (root škn 'dwell'): supports 'furent placés'.

load_bearing.gloss: 'the cherubim' — definite plural
load_bearing.comment: Unexplained definite plural beings; 'militaires' is supplied.

load_bearing.gloss: 'the flame of the sword that turns itself' — hithpael participle FEMININE, agreeing with ḥereb 'sword' (fem.), not with lahaṭ 'flame' (masc.)
load_bearing.comment: In Hebrew it is the sword/blade that turns itself; the French makes the flame the turning thing. The Hebrew has a self-moving blade with flame, coordinated with (not held by) the cherubim.

load_bearing.gloss: 'to guard the way'
load_bearing.comment: Guard function explicit.

items.analysis: The guard-post scenario (beings stationed, a flaming device, to guard an access route) is the Hebrew's own. The original is marginally more favourable than the French on the weapon: the participle is reflexive ('turning itself') and agrees with the blade, and the object is listed alongside the cherubim rather than in their hands — an autonomous flaming, turning blade. 'Atomic', 'désintégrantes' and 'résidence des créateurs' (for 'the way to the tree of life', east of the garden) are supplied.

items.canon_french: Il advint (...) que Caïn apporta des fruits du sol (...) à Iahvé. Abel, de son côté, apporta les premiers-nés de son petit bétail

reading_quotes.french: Les créateurs exilés, qui restaient sous surveillance militaire, poussèrent les hommes à leur amener de la nourriture afin de montrer à leurs supérieurs

items.reading_summary: The exiled creators had humans bring them food to show their superiors that the creatures were good.

load_bearing.gloss: 'a minḥâ (gift, tribute) to YHWH' — the word under the canon's second (...) is minḥâ
load_bearing.comment: minḥâ is the ordinary word for a gift or tribute brought to a superior; the canon cuts it (French presumably 'en oblation'). The recipient is YHWH.

load_bearing.gloss: hiphil 'and he brought'

load_bearing.french: les premiers-nés de son petit bétail
load_bearing.gloss: 'from the firstborn of his flock and from their fat'
load_bearing.comment: 'and from their fat' is silently dropped at the end of the canon's quotation.

ellipsis.cut: (1) 'at the end of days' (מִקֵּ֣ץ יָמִ֑ים); (2) 'a minḥâ/offering'; (3) v.4b 'and from their fat; and YHWH looked on Abel and his offering' (and v.5, not on Cain's).
ellipsis.note: The cut word minḥâ would, if anything, have supported a tribute reading.

items.analysis: Bringing produce and animals to a superior is the Hebrew's plain content, and the cut noun minḥâ ('tribute') fits the canon's provisioning reading at least as well as the French. But the recipient in the Hebrew is YHWH — whom the canon's own scheme at 3:14 places on the side of the home-planet authority, not the exiles; the reading that the food went to the exiled creators is supplied and is in tension with the name in the verse. Hebrew and French agree.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] That the canon's second (...) corresponds to Dhorme's 'en oblation' is inferred from the Hebrew, not collated.

items.canon_french: Adam neuf cent trente ans, Seth neuf cent douze ans, Énosh neuf cent cinq ans

reading_quotes.french: Ils obtinrent ainsi qu’on fasse bénéficier les chefs de ces premiers hommes de «l’arbre de vie», ce qui explique que ceux-ci vécurent si longtemps

items.reading_summary: The patriarchs' lifespans are due to their being granted the 'tree of life' (longevity treatment) as chiefs.

load_bearing.gloss: nine hundred years and thirty years
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.original: שְׁתֵּ֤ים עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה וּתְשַׁ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה
load_bearing.translit: šətêm ʿeśrê šānâ ûtəšaʿ mēʾôt šānâ
load_bearing.gloss: twelve years and nine hundred years
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.gloss: five years and nine hundred years
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

ellipsis.cut: Paraphrase, not quotation.

items.analysis: The three figures agree exactly with the Masoretic numbers in the library text. The explanation (access to the tree of life, granted to 'chiefs') is supplied: Genesis 5 gives no cause for the lifespans, calls none of the men a chief, and Gen 3:22–24 (quoted by the canon two paragraphs earlier) bars the way to the tree. The spelling 'Énosh' follows the Hebrew אֱנ֔וֹשׁ rather than the traditional French 'Énos'.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] That 'Énosh' is Dhorme's spelling is not verified.

items.canon_french: il advint que les fils d’Elohim s’aperçurent que les filles des hommes étaient belles. Ils prirent donc pour eux des femmes parmi toutes celles qu’ils avaient élues

reading_quotes.french: Les créateurs en exil prirent aux hommes leurs filles les plus belles et en firent leurs femmes

items.reading_summary: The 'sons of Elohim' are the exiled creators themselves, who took human women as wives.

load_bearing.gloss: 'the sons of THE Elohim' — with the definite article
load_bearing.comment: Hebrew has the article (hā-); French 'd’Elohim' drops it. bənê + class noun regularly means 'members of the class'.

load_bearing.gloss: 'and they saw' — 3rd masc. PLURAL
load_bearing.comment: Real plural verbs for these beings (also וַיִּקְח֤וּ 'they took', בָּחָֽרוּ 'they chose').

load_bearing.gloss: 'good' (fem. pl.)
load_bearing.comment: Same adjective ṭôb as 'the light was good'; 'belles' is interpretation, a usual one.

load_bearing.gloss: 'the daughters of the human/Adam'

items.analysis: The union of beings from the Elohim side with human women is the Hebrew's explicit content, with unambiguous plural verbs. The canon's equation 'sons of Elohim' = the creators themselves (not their offspring) is actually easier from the Hebrew than from the French: the phrase carries the article ('the Elohim') and the bənê- construction can denote membership in a class. 'En exil' and 'les plus belles' are supplied.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] The 'bənê = members of a class' idiom is standard Hebrew grammar but is stated from general knowledge, not from a library note on this verse.

items.canon_french: Mon esprit ne restera pas toujours dans l’homme, car il est encore chair. Ses jours seront de cent vingt ans

reading_quotes.french: La longévité n’est pas héréditaire et les enfants des hommes ne bénéficiaient pas automatiquement de «l’arbre de vie»

items.reading_summary: Longevity is not inherited; ordinary human lifespan is capped (120 years); the longevity secret was lost.

load_bearing.gloss: 'my rûaḥ' — breath/wind/spirit
load_bearing.comment: Same noun as 1:2 and 8:1. The project translation renders 'my breath' (life-breath), a sense closer to a lifespan statement than French 'esprit'.

load_bearing.gloss: verb of uncertain meaning (occurs only here): 'abide in' / 'contend with' / 'be strong in'
load_bearing.comment: 'Restera' follows the ancient-versions sense 'abide'.

load_bearing.gloss: 'inasmuch as he also is flesh' (difficult form)
load_bearing.comment: 'Encore' for gam ('also'); minor.

load_bearing.french: Ses jours seront de cent vingt ans
load_bearing.gloss: 'and his days shall be a hundred and twenty years'
load_bearing.comment: Explicit cap.

ellipsis.cut: Speech-introduction 'And YHWH said' (וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֗ה) omitted, so the canon's reader is not told who speaks.

items.analysis: A limit on human lifespan connected with the withdrawal of something of the speaker's from the human is what the Hebrew says. The Hebrew rûaḥ covers 'breath / animating wind', which is closer to a biological-longevity reading than French 'esprit'. 'Not hereditary' is the canon's inference from the verse's position after 6:1–2. The key verb yādôn is a hapax of uncertain sense, so any reading leans on a guess here.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] The hapax status and candidate meanings of yādôn are standard lexicon information, not taken from the library note.

items.canon_french: (...) quand les fils d’Elohim venaient vers les filles des hommes et qu’elles enfantaient d’eux, c’étaient les héros qui furent jadis des hommes de renom

reading_quotes.french: Vous avez là, la preuve que les créateurs pouvaient s’accoupler avec les filles des hommes qu’ils avaient créés à leur image et en avoir des enfants exceptionnels

items.reading_summary: Proof that creators and humans were interfertile and had exceptional children; this alarmed the home planet.

load_bearing.original: הַנְּפִלִ֞ים הָי֣וּ בָאָרֶץ֮ בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵם֒ וְגַ֣ם אַֽחֲרֵי־כֵ֗ן
load_bearing.translit: hannəpilîm hāyû bāʾāreṣ bayyāmîm hāhēm wəgam ʾaḥărê-kēn
load_bearing.gloss: 'The Nephilim were on the earth in those days, and also afterwards' — the words under the canon's (...)
load_bearing.comment: The Nephilim, subject of the verse's main clause, are cut.

load_bearing.gloss: imperfect 3rd masc. PLURAL, 'used to come (in to)'
load_bearing.comment: Iterative imperfect; French imperfect matches.

load_bearing.gloss: 'and they bore to them'
load_bearing.comment: Offspring explicit.

load_bearing.gloss: 'those were the mighty ones'
load_bearing.comment: Antecedent of 'those' is ambiguous in Hebrew: the Nephilim or the children.

load_bearing.gloss: 'men of the name'

ellipsis.cut: The first half of the verse: 'The Nephilim were on the earth in those days, and also afterwards'.
ellipsis.note: Removing the Nephilim removes (a) the name itself, which the canon never uses, and (b) the ambiguity over whether 'the heroes' are the Nephilim (present 'in those days and also afterwards', i.e. possibly independent of the unions) or the offspring. In the canon's cut the heroes can only be the offspring.

items.analysis: Interfertility and offspring are stated in the Hebrew ('they bore to them'), so the canon's 'preuve' has its hook in the original. The ellipsis, however, resolves a real ambiguity in the canon's favour by deleting the Nephilim clause: in the Hebrew, 'those were the mighty ones' may point back to the Nephilim rather than to the children. 'Exceptionnels' for gibbōrîm ('mighty/warriors') is a fair gloss.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] Dhorme's rendering of hannəpilîm at 6:4 (e.g. 'Les géants') was not collated.

items.canon_french: Iahvé vit que la malice de l’homme sur la terre était grande et que tout l’objet des pensées de son cœur n’était toujours que le mal

reading_quotes.french: Le mal, c’est-à-dire le désir de devenir un peuple égal à ses créateurs, un peuple scientifique et indépendant

items.reading_summary: 'Evil' = the human desire for scientific progress and equality with the creators, as seen from the home planet.

load_bearing.gloss: 'the badness/evil of the human'

load_bearing.french: tout l’objet des pensées de son cœur
load_bearing.gloss: 'and every yēṣer (thing formed, inclination) of the plans of his heart'
load_bearing.comment: yēṣer is from the root 'to form/shape' — what the mind forms; French 'objet' reads as 'aim'. maḥšābôt = plans, devices (also used of technical designs).

load_bearing.gloss: 'only bad, all the day'

items.analysis: The canon redefines 'evil' as scientific ambition; that is a declared re-reading, not a property of either text. One small point in the Hebrew's favour: maḥšābôt ('plans, devices') is a word of designing and contriving rather than of feeling. One point the French adds: 'objet' (aim) for yēṣer (formation), which the canon exploits at 8:21 (see A-034).

items.actual_reference: Gen 6:14–16 (the ark as a rocket; narrated)
items.ref_note: No quotation or reference; content of Gen 6:13–22 narrated.
items.canon_french: avaient demandé à Noé de construire une fusée qui devait tourner autour de la Terre durant le cataclysme

reading_quotes.french: la vie était préservée à quelques milliers de kilomètres au-dessus de la Terre

items.reading_summary: The ark was a spacecraft in orbit carrying cells of each species; the Flood was a nuclear strike and tidal wave.

load_bearing.gloss: 'a tēbâ (box, chest) of gopher-wood(s)'
load_bearing.comment: tēbâ is a box/chest, not a word for a ship; but the material is wood.

load_bearing.gloss: 'and you shall coat it inside and outside with pitch'
load_bearing.comment: Waterproofing instruction; not quoted by the canon.

ellipsis.cut: The canon quotes none of the construction specifications (wood, compartments, pitch, dimensions) except the three-level clause of 6:16 (A-029).
ellipsis.note: The unquoted specifications describe a pitched wooden box.

items.analysis: The canon itself flags part of this as figurative ('Ceci est une image' — about the animal pairs). On the vessel, the Hebrew word tēbâ ('chest, box') does not say 'boat', which leaves the vessel type more open than French 'arche' suggests to a modern reader; but the unquoted Hebrew specifications (gopher wood, coated with pitch inside and out) are those of a watertight wooden container, which is less favourable to a rocket than the canon's selective quotation.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] tēbâ as 'chest/box' (and its only other use for Moses' basket, Exod 2) is standard lexicon information.

items.canon_french: (...) l’arche (...) s’éleva au-dessus de la terre

reading_quotes.french: Vous pouvez constater qu’il est bien dit qu’elle s’éleva audessus de la Terre et non pas sur les eaux

items.reading_summary: The text itself says the ark rose above the Earth, not on the waters — i.e. it flew.

load_bearing.gloss: 'and it rose up from upon / above the earth'
load_bearing.comment: mēʿal = 'from upon, above'. The clause exists as quoted.

load_bearing.gloss: 'and the waters increased and LIFTED the tēbâ' — the words under the canon's second (...); verb 3rd PLURAL with 'waters' as subject
load_bearing.comment: The immediately preceding clause names the waters as what raised the ark.

load_bearing.gloss: 'and the tēbâ went upon the face of the waters' (next verse, not quoted)
load_bearing.comment: The next verse says in so many words what the canon says the text does not say.

ellipsis.cut: (1) 'The deluge was forty days on the earth; the waters increased and lifted' before 'l’arche'; (2) nothing substantive after it — the quotation is 'l’arche … s’éleva au-dessus de la terre' with 'les eaux … soulevèrent' removed from in front.
ellipsis.note: The ellipsis removes the grammatical agent of the lifting (the waters). The canon's argument 'il est bien dit … non pas sur les eaux' holds only for the truncated sentence.

items.analysis: The quoted words are really there (wattārom mēʿal hāʾāreṣ), so the phrase is not a translation artefact. But the canon's explicit textual argument — that the verse says the ark rose above the earth 'and not on the waters' — is contradicted by the same verse in Hebrew ('the waters increased and lifted the ark', the clause replaced by '(...)') and by the next verse ('the ark went on the face of the waters'). This is the one place in the Genesis sequence where the canon makes a claim about what the wording says and the full wording says the opposite.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] The French of the cut clause in Dhorme (e.g. 'les eaux s’accrurent et soulevèrent l’arche') was not collated.

items.canon_french: (...) les eaux grandirent au-dessus de la terre durant cent cinquante jours

reading_quotes.french: Ensuite il fallut attendre qu’il n’y ait plus de retombées dangereuses

items.reading_summary: 150 days = the wait for radioactive fallout to clear before landing.

load_bearing.gloss: 'were mighty / prevailed' (3rd pl.)
load_bearing.comment: gābar = be strong, prevail; 'grandirent' (grew) is weaker.

load_bearing.gloss: 'upon the earth'
load_bearing.comment: Plain ʿal 'upon', not mēʿal 'above' as in 7:17; the canon's French uses 'au-dessus de' for both.

load_bearing.gloss: a hundred and fifty day(s)
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

ellipsis.cut: The leading (...) corresponds to nothing in v.24, which is quoted whole (it marks the jump from 7:17).

items.analysis: The duration is in the Hebrew; the fallout explanation is supplied. Note that here 'day' (yôm) is taken at face value as a 24-hour day, whereas at Gen 1:5 the same word is read as about 2,000 years (TBWTT-2:10).

items.ref_note: Quoted in parentheses without reference; it is Gen 6:16c. Not in the citation index.
items.canon_french: tu la disposeras en étages, l’inférieur, le second et le troisième

reading_quotes.french: Et la fusée à trois étages

items.reading_summary: The ark was a three-stage rocket.

load_bearing.french: en étages, l’inférieur, le second et le troisième
load_bearing.gloss: 'lower ones, second ones and third ones you shall make it' — three plural adjectives, NO noun
load_bearing.comment: The Hebrew has no word for 'storeys/decks/stages'; the noun is supplied by every translation. French 'étages' is also the technical term for rocket stages ('fusée à trois étages'), which is the canon's hook.

ellipsis.cut: Rest of 6:16: the ṣōhar (roof/opening), 'finish it to a cubit above', and 'the door of the tēbâ you shall set in its side'.

items.analysis: The 'three-stage rocket' rests on the French noun 'étages', which does double duty in French (storeys of a building; stages of a rocket). The Hebrew has only three substantivised plural adjectives — lower, second, third — with the thing they qualify left unstated; they are plural ('lower ones'), suggesting sets of compartments per level rather than three single units. A three-level structure is hebrew-supported; the rocket-stage sense is carried by the French word.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] Whether 'tu la disposeras en étages, l’inférieur, le second et le troisième' is Dhorme verbatim was not collated.

items.canon_french: Elohim se souvint de Noé (...) (et) fit passer un vent sur la terre et les eaux s’apaisèrent

reading_quotes.french: Après avoir surveillé la radio-activité et fait disparaître celle-ci scientifiquement

items.reading_summary: The creators monitored and scientifically removed the radioactivity.

load_bearing.gloss: wind / breath / spirit
load_bearing.comment: Same noun rendered 'esprit' at 1:2 and 6:3. In Hebrew the thing that hovered over the waters at the beginning and the thing sent over the earth to end the Flood are the same word.

load_bearing.gloss: hiphil 3rd masc. SINGULAR, 'and Elohim caused to pass'
load_bearing.comment: Deliberate causative act; singular verb.

load_bearing.gloss: 'and he remembered' (singular)
'and the waters subsided'
load_bearing.comment: Water, not radiation.

ellipsis.cut: 'and every living thing and all the cattle that were with him in the tēbâ' (וְאֵ֤ת כָּל־הַֽחַיָּה֙ וְאֶת־כָּל־הַבְּהֵמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ בַּתֵּבָ֑ה). The '(et)' is the canon's own insertion.
ellipsis.note: The cut removes the live animals aboard, consistent with the canon's statement that the pairs are 'une image' for preserved cells; it does not alter the wind clause.

items.french_variance: rûaḥ → 'esprit' (TBWTT-2:6, 2:52) but 'vent' (TBWTT-2:63).
items.analysis: A deliberate agent-caused passing of a rûaḥ over the earth that makes the waters go down is the Hebrew's content; decontamination is supplied. The Hebrew is slightly more suggestive than the French because it uses for this 'wind' the same word the French translated 'esprit d’Elohim' at 1:2 — the French splits one Hebrew term into 'spirit' (1:2, 6:3) and 'wind' (8:1), and the canon's readings follow the split (hovering reconnaissance vs. a clean-up operation) without noticing the shared word.

items.canon_french: Noé bâtit un autel à Iahvé, il prit de toutes les bêtes pures et de tous les oiseaux purs, il fit monter les holocaustes sur l’autel

reading_quotes.french: Noé s’engagea à verser une part de toutes les récoltes ou élevages aux créateurs pour leur subsistance
Les créateurs furent heureux de voir que les hommes leur voulaient du bien et promirent de ne jamais essayer de les détruire à l’avenir

items.reading_summary: Noah's offering = a pledge of a share of produce for the creators' subsistence; in return they promise never to destroy again.

load_bearing.gloss: 'and he sent up ʿōlôt' — offerings that 'go up', i.e. are wholly burnt
load_bearing.comment: French 'fit monter' keeps the Hebrew verb-noun link (ʿālâ/ʿōlâ). A whole burnt offering leaves nothing to eat.

load_bearing.gloss: 'an altar (slaughter-place) to YHWH'

items.analysis: An animal offering to YHWH followed (8:21) by a promise not to strike again is the Hebrew sequence, so the gratitude-and-pledge frame has a textual basis. The 'share of harvests … for their subsistence' is supplied and fits poorly with the specific rite named in both French and Hebrew — holocausts/ʿōlôt, which are burnt entire — and no crops are mentioned. Hebrew and French agree.

items.canon_french: (...) l’objet du cœur de l’homme est le mal

reading_quotes.french: Le but de l’homme est le progrès scientifique
car ils avaient compris qu’il était normal qu’ils veuillent faire des progrès

items.reading_summary: 'The object of man's heart is evil' = man's goal is scientific progress, which the creators now accept as normal.

load_bearing.gloss: 'the yēṣer (what is formed; inclination, bent) of the heart of the human'
load_bearing.comment: French 'objet' → canon 'but' (goal). yēṣer, from yāṣar 'to form', is the shape or bent of the mind, not its target.

load_bearing.gloss: '(is) bad from his youth'
load_bearing.comment: 'From his youth' is dropped at the end of the canon's quotation without ellipsis marks.

load_bearing.original: לֹֽא־אֹ֠סִף לְקַלֵּ֨ל ע֤וֹד אֶת־הָֽאֲדָמָה֙ בַּעֲב֣וּר הָֽאָדָ֔ם כִּ֠י
load_bearing.translit: lōʾ-ʾōsip ləqallēl ʿôd ʾet-hāʾădāmâ baʿăbûr hāʾādām kî
load_bearing.gloss: 'I will not again curse the ground on account of the human, FOR…' (not quoted)
load_bearing.comment: The promise-not-to-destroy and its causal link to the yēṣer clause are in the Hebrew; this supports TBWTT-2:66's 'promirent … car ils avaient compris'.

ellipsis.cut: Before: 'YHWH smelled the soothing odour and YHWH said in his heart: I will not again curse the ground because of the human, for'; after: 'from his youth; and I will not again strike every living thing as I have done'.
ellipsis.note: The cut 'from his youth' marks the 'evil' as an inborn disposition; without it 'objet' can be read as a chosen aim.

items.french_variance: Gen 6:5 'tout l’objet des pensées de son cœur' and 8:21 'l’objet du cœur' render the same Hebrew yēṣer consistently; the inconsistency is in the canon's gloss ('mal' = desire for science at 2:57; 'objet' = 'but' at 2:68).
items.analysis: The canon's equation 'objet … est le mal' → 'le but de l’homme est le progrès scientifique' needs the French word 'objet' in the sense of 'aim'. Hebrew yēṣer is 'what is formed, inclination', and the full clause adds 'from his youth' — a statement about native bent, not about a goal. On the other hand, the logical structure the canon builds around it (the makers resolve not to destroy again BECAUSE of this trait) is exactly the Hebrew's kî-clause, which the canon paraphrases but does not quote.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] That 'objet' is Dhorme's rendering of yēṣer at 6:5 and 8:21 was not collated.

items.ref_note: Reference is attached to the continuation paragraph TBWTT-2:70; quotation text sits in TBWTT-2:69.
items.canon_french: D’elles ont essaimé les nations sur la terre après le

reading_quotes.french: Chaque race humaine fut replacée en son lieu de création
Il y avait à l’intérieur outre Noé, un couple de chaque race humaine de la Terre

items.reading_summary: After the Flood each human race (one pair of each was aboard) was put back in its original place of creation.

load_bearing.gloss: 'and from these' — antecedent: 'the families of the sons of Noah' (אֵ֣לֶּה מִשְׁפְּחֹ֧ת בְּנֵי־נֹ֛חַ, first half of the verse)
load_bearing.comment: French feminine 'elles' = 'les familles (des fils de Noé)'; the canon cuts the antecedent.

load_bearing.gloss: niphal 3rd pl., 'the nations separated / branched off'
load_bearing.comment: A branching-out from a common stock; French 'essaimé' (swarmed out) is apt.

ellipsis.cut: v.32a: 'These are the families of the sons of Noah, according to their generations, in their nations'. (The digitization also splits the quotation across TBWTT-2:69/2:70: 'après le / Déluge».')
ellipsis.note: With the antecedent restored, the verse derives ALL nations from Noah's sons' families — a single post-Flood stock — whereas the canon uses it for the return of several separately created races to their places.

items.analysis: The verse the canon cites for the redistribution of pre-existing races says, in Hebrew and in the French once the antecedent of 'D’elles' is restored, that the nations branched off from the families of Noah's sons. The canon's premise that the ark carried 'un couple de chaque race humaine' has no counterpart in the text (Gen 6–8 put only Noah's household aboard). The contradiction is with the original and with the untruncated French alike.

items.canon_french: S’ils commencent à faire cela, rien désormais ne leur sera impossible de tout ce qu’ils décideront de faire

reading_quotes.french: Les gens de la planète eurent peur en apprenant la chose
Ils construisirent donc une immense fusée : la Tour de Babel

items.reading_summary: The tower was a spaceship built by Israel with the exiles' help; the home planet feared unlimited human capability.

load_bearing.gloss: 'and this is their beginning to do' — a statement of fact (infinitive with suffix), not a condition
load_bearing.comment: Hebrew: they HAVE begun. French turns it into 'if they begin'.

load_bearing.french: rien désormais ne leur sera impossible
load_bearing.gloss: 'and now nothing will be cut off / inaccessible from them'
load_bearing.comment: bāṣar niphal = be fenced off, out of reach.

load_bearing.french: tout ce qu’ils décideront de faire
load_bearing.gloss: 'which they plan/scheme to do'
load_bearing.comment: zāmam = devise, plan.

ellipsis.cut: v.6a: 'And YHWH said: Behold, one people and one language for them all' — the unity premise and the speaker.
ellipsis.note: The cut premise ('one people, one language') is what motivates the remedy in v.7; it is consistent with the canon's reading.

items.analysis: The speaker's concern in the Hebrew is exactly unlimited capability ('nothing they plan to do will be out of their reach'), with no moral vocabulary — the existing library note makes the same observation. The Hebrew is a shade stronger than the canon's French: it states that the work has already begun ('this is their beginning to do') where the French has a conditional. Tower = rocket and builders = Israel are supplied; the Hebrew builders are 'the sons of the human' (GEN-WOH-11:5), and the unquoted 11:4 gives 'a tower with its head in the skies' (וּמִגְדָּל֙ וְרֹאשׁ֣וֹ בַשָּׁמַ֔יִם).

items.canon_french: descendons et (...) confondons leur langage, en sorte qu’ils ne comprennent plus le langage les uns des autres». Puis Iahvé les dispersa de là sur la surface de toute la terre (...)

reading_quotes.french: Ils vinrent, prirent les Juifs qui avaient le plus de connaissances scientifiques et les dispersèrent sur tout le continent, dans des peuplades primitives, dans des pays où aucun ne pouvait se faire comprendre car le langage y était différent et ils détruisirent les appareillages scientifiques

items.reading_summary: They came down, scattered the most learned among peoples whose languages they could not speak, and destroyed the equipment.

load_bearing.gloss: qal cohortative 1st person PLURAL, 'let us go down'
load_bearing.comment: Genuine plural.

load_bearing.gloss: cohortative 1st PLURAL, 'and let us confuse there their lip/speech'
load_bearing.comment: Second plural. The Hebrew action is on the speech itself; 'there' (šām) is under the canon's (...).

load_bearing.gloss: 'and YHWH scattered them' — verb 3rd masc. SINGULAR
load_bearing.comment: Plural deliberation, singular execution.

load_bearing.gloss: 'and they ceased to build THE CITY' — the words under the canon's final (...)
load_bearing.comment: What is abandoned in the Hebrew is a city, not a tower/vehicle.

ellipsis.cut: (1) Opening 'Come' (הָ֚בָה) — the canon's quotation also lacks its opening guillemet; (2) 'there' (šām); (3) v.8b 'and they ceased to build the city'.
ellipsis.note: The cut end names the abandoned project as 'the city'; the tower is not mentioned in the outcome at all.

items.analysis: The plural descent ('let us go down … let us confuse') is in the Hebrew in two unambiguous first-person-plural cohortatives, and the scattering is explicit. Two points go the other way: in the Hebrew the makers alter the builders' language ('confuse their lip') whereas the canon has the people relocated to where other languages already existed; and the cut clause shows the outcome as abandoning a city. 'Destroyed the scientific apparatus' has no counterpart.

items.canon_french: Les deux Anges arrivèrent le soir à Sodome

reading_quotes.french: Les créateurs envoyèrent deux espions pour voir ce qui se préparait

items.reading_summary: The two 'angels' are two spies sent by the creators.

load_bearing.gloss: 'the two messengers/envoys' — malʾāk = one sent on a mission
load_bearing.comment: French 'Anges' (capitalised) carries the later celestial-being sense; the Hebrew word is the ordinary noun for an envoy, also used of human messengers.

load_bearing.gloss: 'and they came' (3rd pl.)

ellipsis.cut: Rest of v.1 (Lot at the gate, rising, bowing).

items.analysis: The Hebrew malʾākîm means 'those sent' — agents on a mission — which is closer to the canon's 'envoyèrent deux espions' than the French 'Anges' it quotes. The same two are called simply 'the men' in the narrative (הָֽאֲנָשִׁים֙, GEN-WOH-19:10 and 19:16). 'Spies' specifically is the canon's inference (a fact-finding purpose).
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] A fact-finding purpose is stated at Gen 18:21 ('I will go down and see'); that verse was not pulled from the library for this audit.

items.ref_note: The reference stands alone in the next paragraph (TBWTT-2:82), the quotation in TBWTT-2:81.
items.canon_french: Ils les frappèrent de cécité, du plus petit au plus grand.

reading_quotes.french: Des hommes voulurent les tuer mais ils les aveuglèrent avec une arme atomique de poche

items.reading_summary: The envoys blinded the attackers with a pocket atomic weapon.

load_bearing.gloss: hiphil perfect 3rd PLURAL, 'they struck'
load_bearing.comment: Plural: the two envoys themselves do it.

load_bearing.gloss: 'with the sanwērîm' — a rare word (definite, plural form) for a sudden blinding/dazzling, not the ordinary Hebrew word for blindness
load_bearing.comment: French 'cécité' flattens a special term.

load_bearing.french: du plus petit au plus grand
load_bearing.gloss: from small to great

ellipsis.cut: 'the men who were at the entrance of the house' and the end 'so that they wearied themselves to find the entrance'.
ellipsis.note: The cut end shows the effect was disorientation — they still grope for the door.

items.analysis: That the two envoys themselves strike a crowd with an instantaneous blinding is the Hebrew's statement (plural active verb). The Hebrew is slightly more favourable than the French in that it uses a special term (sanwērîm) rather than ordinary 'blindness', i.e. marks the effect as something unusual; the device ('arme atomique de poche') is supplied. 'Voulurent les tuer' restates the mob's intent, which in the text is sexual assault (19:5), not killing.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] sanwērîm occurring only here and at 2 Kgs 6:18, and its sense 'dazzling', is standard lexicon information.

items.canon_french: (...) sortez de cette localité, car Iahvé va détruire la ville

reading_quotes.french: Ils prévinrent les hommes qui étaient pacifiques de quitter cette ville qu’ils allaient détruire par une explosion atomique
ils ne se pressaient pas, ne se doutant pas de ce que représentait une explosion atomique

items.reading_summary: The envoys warned the peaceful inhabitants to leave before an atomic explosion; people did not hurry.

load_bearing.gloss: 'arise, go out from this place' (imperatives pl.)
load_bearing.comment: 'Arise' is under the canon's (...).

load_bearing.gloss: 'for YHWH is destroying / about to destroy the city' — hiphil participle
load_bearing.comment: Imminent-action participle; 'va détruire' is exact.

load_bearing.gloss: 'and Lot went out and spoke to his sons-in-law' (not quoted)
load_bearing.comment: In the Hebrew the speaker of the quoted words is Lot, the audience his sons-in-law.

ellipsis.cut: 'Lot went out and spoke to his sons-in-law, who were to marry his daughters, and said: Arise' before; 'but he seemed to his sons-in-law as one jesting' after.
ellipsis.note: The canon's lead-in ('Ils prévinrent les hommes qui étaient pacifiques') assigns to the envoys, addressing the peaceable citizens, a sentence that the Hebrew gives to Lot addressing his sons-in-law, who do not believe him.

items.analysis: The warning of imminent destruction is in the Hebrew; the atomic nature is supplied. The ellipsis changes speaker and audience. The Hebrew offers an unquoted line more favourable to the canon's 'qu’ils allaient détruire': at 19:13 the envoys say 'WE are destroying this place … YHWH has sent us to destroy it' (כִּֽי־מַשְׁחִתִ֣ים אֲנַ֔חְנוּ, GEN-WOH-19:13), with a plural participle and the envoys as agents. The canon's 'ils ne se pressaient pas' matches the unquoted 19:14 end and 19:16 ('he lingered').

items.canon_french: Sauve-toi, (...) ne regarde pas derrière toi et ne t’arrête pas

reading_quotes.french: Et la bombe tomba sur Sodome et Gomorrhe

items.reading_summary: Flee without stopping or looking back — then the bomb fell.

load_bearing.gloss: 'escape for your life' (imperative sing.)
load_bearing.comment: 'for your life' under the (...).

load_bearing.gloss: 'do not look behind you'
'and do not stand still in all the kikkār (the round plain/district)'
load_bearing.comment: The canon stops before 'in all the Plain'.

ellipsis.cut: 'for your life'; and the end: 'in all the Plain; escape to the mountain, lest you be swept away' (הָהָ֥רָה הִמָּלֵ֖ט פֶּן־תִּסָּפֶֽה).
ellipsis.note: The cut end specifies an evacuation zone (the whole plain) and high ground as refuge — detail that would have suited the canon's blast reading.

items.analysis: Urgent evacuation orders are the Hebrew's content; 'la bombe' is supplied. The uncited remainder of the verse (clear the entire plain, get to the mountain or be swept away) is more specific about a destruction radius than the portion the canon quotes.

items.canon_french: Iahvé fit pleuvoir (...) du soufre et du feu provenant de Iahvé, des cieux. Il anéantit ces villes (...) et les germes du sol. La femme de Loth regarda en arrière et elle devint une statue de sel

reading_quotes.french: la brûlure occasionnée par une explosion atomique à ceux qui sont proches les fait mourir en les faisant ressembler à une statue de sel

items.reading_summary: Atomic explosion from the sky; Lot's wife died of the burn, looking like a salt statue.

load_bearing.french: du soufre et du feu provenant de Iahvé, des cieux
load_bearing.gloss: 'sulphur and fire from-with YHWH, from the skies'
load_bearing.comment: Fire delivered from the sky by an agent: in the Hebrew. YHWH is named twice (subject and source).

load_bearing.gloss: 'and he overturned those cities' — hāpak 'turn over, overthrow'
load_bearing.comment: Hebrew 'overturned' (the standing term for Sodom's fate); French 'anéantit' (annihilated) is stronger and less specific.

load_bearing.gloss: 'and the growth/vegetation of the ground'
'a nəṣîb of salt' — something set upright: pillar, post
load_bearing.comment: nəṣîb is an upright post/pillar, not a figure in human likeness; French 'statue' adds the human-figure image that the canon's 'ressembler à une statue de sel' relies on.

load_bearing.gloss: 'and his wife looked from behind him'
load_bearing.comment: Hebrew has her behind Lot, i.e. lagging — nearer the destruction.

ellipsis.cut: (1) 'upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah'; (2) 'and all the Plain and all the inhabitants of the cities'.

items.analysis: Fire and sulphur 'from YHWH, from the skies', destroying cities, a plain and its vegetation, with a straggler turned to salt: all of that is the Hebrew's wording, so the sky-delivered destruction is a real textual hook. Two French colourings help the canon slightly: 'anéantit' for 'overturned', and 'statue' for nəṣîb (pillar/upright), which makes the wife a salt effigy. One Hebrew detail helps it: 'from behind him' places her at the rear. 'Atomic' is supplied.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] That 'statue de sel' and 'anéantit' are Dhorme's wording was not collated.

items.canon_french: N’étends pas la main sur le garçon et ne lui fais rien, car maintenant je sais que tu crains Elohim (...)

reading_quotes.french: Les créateurs le mirent à l’épreuve pour voir si ses sentiments à leur égard étaient suffisamment forts

items.reading_summary: The binding of Isaac was a loyalty test set by the creators.

load_bearing.gloss: 'now I know' (1st sing. perfect)
load_bearing.comment: Knowledge gained by the test — explicit in Hebrew.

load_bearing.gloss: 'a fearer of Elohim are you'
load_bearing.comment: 'Fear' (awe/obedience); the canon paraphrases as 'bons sentiments'.

load_bearing.gloss: 'and you have not withheld your son, your only one, from ME' — the words under the (...)
load_bearing.comment: The speaker refers to Elohim in the third person and then says 'from me'.

load_bearing.gloss: 'and THE Elohim tested Abraham' — with article; verb 3rd masc. SINGULAR (v.1, not quoted)
load_bearing.comment: The chapter's first sentence states the canon's reading outright.

ellipsis.cut: End of v.12: 'and you have not withheld your son, your only one, from me'. Also unquoted: the speaker is 'the messenger of YHWH … from the skies' (מַלְאַ֤ךְ יְהוָה֙ מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם, GEN-WOH-22:11).

items.analysis: The canon's reading (a test to establish the patriarch's disposition) is the Hebrew's own framing: 22:1 says 'the Elohim tested Abraham' and 22:12 'now I know'. The original is more favourable than the fragment quoted on two counts the canon does not use: the article in hāʾĕlōhîm at 22:1, and the fact that the voice is a malʾāk ('envoy') calling 'from the skies'. Against the plural reading, nissâ is singular. 'Sentiments' softens 'fear'.

items.canon_french: «Une échelle était dressée par terre, sa tête touchant aux cieux, et voici que des Anges d'Elohim montaient et descendaient sur elle»

reading_quotes.french: se trouve une autre description de notre présence

items.reading_summary: Presented as 'another description of our presence': messengers of the Elohim going up and down between earth and sky.

load_bearing.gloss: hapax: ladder / stairway / ramp
load_bearing.comment: French 'échelle' is one of several possible senses; library EN has 'stairway'. Not load-bearing for the reading.

load_bearing.gloss: messengers of Elohim (construct plural)
load_bearing.comment: French 'Anges' (capitalised) is the traditional rendering; Hebrew malʾāḵ is the ordinary word for an envoy/messenger. ʾĕlōhîm here has no article.

load_bearing.gloss: ascending and descending (m.pl. participles)
load_bearing.comment: Matches. The Hebrew order is up first, then down, as in the French.

load_bearing.gloss: and he dreamed
load_bearing.comment: First word of the verse; absent from the canon's quotation, which starts mid-verse with no '(...)'.

ellipsis.cut: Silent cut (no '(...)' printed): the verse-opening 'And he dreamed, and behold' (wayyaḥălōm wəhinnēh).
ellipsis.note: The Hebrew frames the scene as the content of a dream; the canon introduces it as a 'description of our presence'. The cut is unmarked.

items.analysis: The traffic of malʾăḵê ʾĕlōhîm between earth and sky is in the Hebrew exactly as in the French, so the textual hook is real. But the verse's first verb, wayyaḥălōm 'he dreamed', is dropped without an ellipsis mark; in the original the stairway is dream content, not a waking observation. The French 'Anges' is less neutral than Hebrew malʾāḵ 'messenger', which is the more favourable datum for a non-supernatural reading; the dream frame is the less favourable one.

items.ref_note: The reference is printed in the following paragraph (TBWTT-3:6) after the canon's '(...)'.
items.canon_french: «Enlevez les dieux étrangers qui sont au milieu de vous

reading_quotes.french: se mettaient à adorer bêtement des morceaux de pierre et des idoles en oubliant qui les avait créés

items.reading_summary: Post-Sodom humans, fallen back into a primitive state, worship pieces of stone and idols and forget their creators.

load_bearing.gloss: the elohim of the foreign(er) — construct plural of the same noun ʾĕlōhîm
load_bearing.comment: The French distinguishes 'dieux' (lower case) here from 'Elohim' elsewhere; the Hebrew uses one and the same noun for both.

load_bearing.gloss: the foreign elohim that were in their hand
load_bearing.comment: v 4 (not quoted) shows the 'foreign elohim' are portable objects handed over with ear-rings; this is the only textual support for 'idoles', and it is outside the quotation.

ellipsis.cut: Canon '(...)' cuts 'and purify yourselves, and change your garments'; the speaker (Jacob to his household) is also not given.
ellipsis.note: The cut clauses are ritual preparation; they do not bear on the reading.

items.french_variance: The canon prints 'dieux' for ʾĕlōhê here but keeps 'Elohim' for the same noun at TBWTT-3:3 and 3:82 — the Elohim/dieux contrast exists only in the French.
items.analysis: The reading contrasts the true creators (Elohim) with stones and idols ('dieux étrangers'). In Hebrew there is no lexical contrast: the objects to be removed are ʾĕlōhê hannēḵār, the same word ʾĕlōhîm in the construct. 'Morceaux de pierre' is not in the verse; that they are objects is inferable only from v 4 (handed over, buried under the oak). The canon's claim at TBWTT-2:5 that Elohim 'means those who came from the sky' sits awkwardly with a verse where the same noun names household objects.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] Whether Dhorme prints 'dieux étrangers' here has not been collated; the core notes only cover Genesis 1–3.

items.canon_french: «L'Ange de Iahvé lui apparut dans une flamme de feu, du milieu d'un buisson (...) le buisson était embrasé par le feu, mais il n'était pas dévoré !»

reading_quotes.french: Une fusée se posa devant lui
dans cet engin dont la lumière blanche éclaire dans les arbres sans les faire brûler pour autant

items.reading_summary: A rocket landed in front of Moses; its white light shines in the trees without burning them, as a 'primitive' would describe it.

load_bearing.gloss: messenger of YHWH
load_bearing.comment: Same word as Gen 28:12; 'Ange' is the French convention.

load_bearing.french: dans une flamme de feu, du milieu d'un buisson
load_bearing.gloss: in a flame of fire from the midst of the bush
load_bearing.comment: Hebrew has the definite article ('the bush', a single shrub, səneh); the canon's reading speaks of 'les arbres' (plural trees).

load_bearing.french: le buisson était embrasé par le feu
load_bearing.gloss: the bush was burning with fire
load_bearing.comment: The Hebrew affirms that the bush burns with fire; the reading turns this into a light that does not burn.

load_bearing.gloss: it was not eaten/consumed
load_bearing.comment: Matches; this is the one clause the 'light without burning' reading leans on.

load_bearing.gloss: from the midst of the bush
load_bearing.comment: v 4 (not quoted): the Elohim calls 'from the midst of the bush' — the speaker is located inside the shrub, not in a craft standing beside it.

ellipsis.cut: Canon '(...)' cuts 'and he looked, and behold' (wayyarʾ wəhinnēh).
ellipsis.note: Trivial cut.

items.analysis: Nothing in the Hebrew describes a descent, a landing or a vehicle: the only objects are a messenger, a flame of fire, and one particular bush (hassəneh, with article). The reading's 'white light … without burning' rests on ʾênennû ʾukkāl 'it was not consumed', which is real, but the same verse says the bush was 'burning with fire' and places flame and voice inside the bush (mittôḵ, vv 2 and 4). The rocket is an addition to wording that is the same in French and Hebrew; the plural 'arbres' departs from both.

items.canon_french: «or Iahvé marchait au-devant d'eux, le jour en colonne de nuée pour les guider sur la route, et la nuit en colonne de feu pour les éclairer en sorte qu'ils marchent jour et nuit»
