reading_quotes.french: Lorsqu'ils partirent, nous les guidâmes jusqu'au pays que nous leur destinions.

items.reading_summary: The creators themselves guided Israel on the route (the column is treated as their craft/smoke in the following paragraphs).

load_bearing.gloss: in/as a pillar of cloud
load_bearing.comment: The preposition bə- can be locative ('in a pillar') or beth essentiae ('as a pillar'); the French 'en colonne' chooses the second. On the locative reading YHWH travels inside the column.

load_bearing.gloss: in/as a pillar of fire
load_bearing.comment: Same construction.

load_bearing.french: pour les guider sur la route
load_bearing.gloss: to lead them (on) the way
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.gloss: and YHWH was going before them (sg. participle)
load_bearing.comment: Singular subject and participle; the canon's commentary uses 'nous' (plural).

items.analysis: The guiding function (lanḥōṯām) and the day/night column are in the Hebrew as quoted. The Hebrew bəʿammûḏ admits 'in a pillar', i.e. YHWH located inside the column, which the French 'en colonne de' (as a column) flattens; on that point the original is marginally more open to the canon's occupant-in-a-vehicle picture than the French it quotes. The subject is singular (YHWH hōlēḵ); the canon's 'nous les guidâmes' pluralises.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] The beth essentiae vs locative analysis of bəʿammûḏ is standard grammar-book material but is not discussed in the library note; no grammar was consulted for this audit.

items.ref_note: The first quoted clause is 14:19b; the second ('la nuée était … ténèbres … éclairait la nuit') is 14:20. 14:19a is not quoted.
items.canon_french: «La colonne de nuée se déplaça de devant eux et se tint derrière eux (...) la nuée était (pour les uns) ténèbres, et (pour les autres) elle éclairait la nuit»

reading_quotes.french: La fumée émise derrière le peuple d'Israël faisait un rideau qui ralentissait les poursuivants.

items.reading_summary: Smoke emitted behind Israel formed a curtain that slowed the Egyptian pursuers.

load_bearing.french: La colonne de nuée se déplaça de devant eux et se tint derrière eux
load_bearing.original: וַיִּסַּ֞ע עַמּ֤וּד הֶֽעָנָן֙ מִפְּנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיַּֽעֲמֹ֖ד מֵאַחֲרֵיהֶֽם׃
load_bearing.translit: wayyissaʿ ʿammûḏ heʿānān mippənêhem wayyaʿămōḏ mēʾaḥărêhem
load_bearing.gloss: and the pillar of cloud set out from before them and stood behind them
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.gloss: and the messenger of the Elohim set out
load_bearing.comment: 14:19a, not quoted: a personal agent, 'the messenger of the Elohim' (with article), moves together with the column.

load_bearing.french: la nuée était (pour les uns) ténèbres, et (pour les autres) elle éclairait la nuit
load_bearing.gloss: and there was the cloud and the darkness, and it lit up the night
load_bearing.comment: The canon's bracketed '(pour les uns)…(pour les autres)' has no Hebrew counterpart; the brackets mark it honestly as a supplement.

load_bearing.original: וַיָּבֹ֞א בֵּ֣ין ׀ מַחֲנֵ֣ה מִצְרַ֗יִם וּבֵין֙ מַחֲנֵ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל
load_bearing.translit: wayyāḇōʾ bên maḥănēh miṣrayim ûḇên maḥănēh yiśrāʾēl
load_bearing.gloss: and it came between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel
load_bearing.comment: Cut by the canon's '(...)': the clause that actually states the screening position.

load_bearing.gloss: and the one did not come near the other all night
load_bearing.comment: Also cut: the clause that states the effect the canon's reading describes (pursuers kept off).

load_bearing.gloss: the cloud
load_bearing.comment: The reading says 'fumée' (smoke); the Hebrew word is ʿānān 'cloud' (smoke is ʿāšān, used at Exod 19:18). The canon's own quotation says 'nuée'.

ellipsis.cut: (1) 14:19a 'the messenger of the Elohim who went before the camp of Israel moved and went behind them' is not quoted (silently). (2) The '(...)' removes 14:20a 'it came between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel'. (3) The quotation stops before 'and the one did not come near the other all night'.
ellipsis.note: The cuts remove the clauses most favourable to the canon's own 'curtain' reading, and remove the personal messenger who moves with the column.

items.analysis: The screen function is stated more explicitly in the uncited Hebrew than in the excerpt the canon prints: the column 'came between' the two camps and 'the one did not come near the other all night'. 14:19a also pairs the column with a named agent, malʾaḵ hāʾĕlōhîm (articular Elohim), who relocates with it. Against the reading: the noun is ʿānān 'cloud', not smoke, and nothing is 'emitted'; and the bracketed 'for some … for others' is a translator's supplement to a difficult clause, not Hebrew.

items.ref_note: Reference printed in the next paragraph (TBWTT-3:17).
items.canon_french: «(...) il mit ainsi la mer à sec et les eaux se fendirent»

reading_quotes.french: Ensuite la traversée de l'eau est obtenue grâce à un rayon répulseur qui permet de dégager un passage.

items.reading_summary: The crossing of the sea was obtained with a 'repulsor ray' that cleared a passage.

load_bearing.french: il mit ainsi la mer à sec
load_bearing.gloss: and he made the sea into dry land
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.gloss: and the waters were split (Niphal)
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.original: וַיּ֣וֹלֶךְ יְהוָ֣ה ׀ אֶת־הַ֠יָּם בְּר֨וּחַ קָדִ֤ים עַזָּה֙ כָּל־הַלַּ֔יְלָה
load_bearing.translit: wayyôleḵ YHWH ʾeṯ-hayyām bərûaḥ qāḏîm ʿazzâ kol-hallaylâ
load_bearing.gloss: and YHWH made the sea go by a strong east wind all the night
load_bearing.comment: Cut by the canon's '(...)': the verse's own statement of the means (a strong east wind, blowing all night). French 'ainsi' ('thus') in the retained clause points back to it.

load_bearing.gloss: and Moses stretched out his hand over the sea
load_bearing.comment: Also cut.

ellipsis.cut: The '(...)' removes 14:21a: Moses stretching out his hand, and 'YHWH drove the sea back by a strong east wind all night'.
ellipsis.note: The removed clause is the text's own mechanism (rûaḥ qāḏîm ʿazzâ, over a whole night). The canon's reading substitutes a different mechanism in exactly that slot; its own 'ainsi' is left pointing at nothing.

items.analysis: The splitting and drying are in the Hebrew as quoted, but the instrument is named in the half-verse the canon elides: a strong east wind working all night. A 'repulsor ray' is therefore not an addition to neutral wording; it replaces a stated cause that the quotation has removed. The same holds for the French: Dhorme-type French also has the wind, so this is a selection effect, not a translation effect. v 22 ('the waters were a wall for them on their right and on their left') is the detail most compatible with a held-open passage and is not quoted.

items.canon_french: «En ce jour Iahvé sauva Israël (...)»
items.reading_summary: No technological reading; closes the sea episode.

load_bearing.gloss: and YHWH delivered
load_bearing.comment: Matches; singular verb.

ellipsis.cut: Cuts 'from the hand of Egypt; and Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the shore of the sea'.

items.analysis: Plain narrative summary; nothing rests on a particular word.

items.ref_note: Reference printed in the next paragraph (TBWTT-3:21).
items.canon_french: «(...) à la surface du désert il y eut une mince croûte (...)»

reading_quotes.french: La manne n'était qu'un aliment chimique de synthèse pulvérisé à la surface du sol et que la rosée du matin faisait gonfler.

items.reading_summary: Manna was a synthetic chemical food sprayed onto the ground, which the morning dew caused to swell.

load_bearing.gloss: on the face of the wilderness
load_bearing.comment: Matches; this is the hook for 'à la surface du sol'.

load_bearing.gloss: fine, flaky(?) — məḥuspās is a hapax of uncertain sense
load_bearing.comment: French 'croûte' (crust) is one guess at the hapax; library EN 'a fine, flaky substance'.

load_bearing.gloss: and the layer of dew went up (lifted)
load_bearing.comment: Cut by the first '(...)': the manna is seen after the dew has lifted. The reading has the dew swell the product.

load_bearing.gloss: raining down for you bread from the skies
load_bearing.comment: Not quoted: the Hebrew says the bread is 'rained' from the sky — closer to 'pulvérisé' than anything in the verse the canon cites.

load_bearing.gloss: the manna would come down upon it (the dew)
load_bearing.comment: Not quoted: manna 'descends' at night on top of the dew.

ellipsis.cut: First '(...)' cuts 'and the layer of dew lifted, and behold'; second cuts 'fine as the frost on the ground'.
ellipsis.note: The dew clause is the only link to the canon's dew mechanism, and it is elided; the frost simile is neutral.

items.analysis: The verse quoted gives only location (ʿal-pənê hammiḏbār) and texture (daq məḥuspās); 'chemical', 'synthetic' and 'swelling' are additions. The delivery-from-above element of the reading ('pulvérisé') is, however, better supported by Hebrew the canon does not quote: Exod 16:4 mamṭîr … min-haššāmāyim 'raining bread from the skies' and Num 11:9 yērēḏ hammān 'the manna came down' on the dew. The dew's role in the Hebrew is as a carrier layer that lifts, not as a swelling agent.

items.ref_note: The guillemets enclose a paraphrase ('de faire jaillir de l'eau'), not the verse's wording.
items.canon_french: Quant au bâton de Moïse qui lui permit «de faire jaillir de l'eau»

reading_quotes.french: ce n'était qu'un détecteur de nappes aquatiques souterraines
Une fois l'eau localisée, il suffit de creuser.

items.reading_summary: Moses' staff was a detector of underground water; once the water was located one only had to dig.

load_bearing.gloss: and your staff with which you struck the Nile
load_bearing.comment: The staff is in v 5, not v 6; it is identified as the striking staff of the Nile plague.

load_bearing.gloss: and you shall strike the rock, and water will come out of it
load_bearing.comment: The verb is 'strike' (hikkâ), not locate or dig; the water 'comes out of' the rock.

load_bearing.gloss: behold, I am standing before you there on the rock
load_bearing.comment: The spot is indicated by YHWH standing on it, not found by the staff.

ellipsis.cut: Not a quotation; the canon paraphrases.

items.analysis: The Hebrew gives the staff a striking role (wəhikkîṯā) and gives the locating role to YHWH, who stands 'there on the rock' in front of Moses. Neither detection nor digging is in the wording. The reading is therefore added to the text, and its division of labour (staff finds, men dig) runs against the verse's own (YHWH marks the spot, staff strikes). The French paraphrase is the canon's, not a Bible translation's.

items.canon_french: «(...) il y eut des tonnerres, des éclairs et une lourde nuée sur la montagne, un son de cor très fort (...)»

reading_quotes.french: Les créateurs vinrent dicter ces lois à Moïse sur le Mont Sinaï. Ils descendirent dans un engin volant :

items.reading_summary: The creators came down on Sinai in a flying craft to dictate the laws; thunder, lightning, heavy cloud and horn-sound describe it.

load_bearing.gloss: voices / sounds / thunders (plural of qôl)
load_bearing.comment: qôl is the general word for 'sound, voice'; 'tonnerres' is a contextual rendering. The Hebrew is the less specific term.

load_bearing.gloss: and a heavy cloud
load_bearing.comment: Matches. kāḇēḏ 'heavy' is the root of kāḇôḏ 'glory' (see Exod 24:17).

load_bearing.french: un son de cor très fort
load_bearing.gloss: and the sound of a shofar, very strong
load_bearing.comment: šōp̄ār is the ram's horn; French 'cor' is fair. The source of the sound is not stated (no one is said to blow it).

ellipsis.cut: Opening '(...)' cuts 'on the third day, when it was morning'; closing '(...)' cuts 'and all the people in the camp trembled'.

items.analysis: The phenomena listed are those of the Hebrew; none of the nouns denotes a vehicle. qōlōṯ ('sounds/voices') is less weather-specific than 'tonnerres', and the unattributed qōl šōp̄ār is a genuine oddity of the text, but both are wording the reading interprets rather than wording that says 'craft'. The plural 'Ils descendirent' is the canon's; the descent verb in this chapter (vv 18, 20) is singular with YHWH. The library note on this verse attributes the canon's engagement to 'Extra-Terrestrials Took Me To Their Planet'; the quotation is in fact at TBWTT-3:25.

items.canon_french: «or le Mont Sinaï était tout fumant, parce que sur lui était descendu Iahvé dans le feu, et sa fumée montait comme la fumée d'une fournaise : toute la montagne tremblait fort. Le son du cor allait en se renforçant de plus en plus, (...)»

reading_quotes.french: Ils descendirent dans un engin volant :

items.reading_summary: Continuation of the Sinai landing: descent in fire, furnace-like smoke, the mountain shaking, a horn-sound growing louder.

load_bearing.french: sur lui était descendu Iahvé dans le feu
load_bearing.gloss: YHWH had come down upon it in (the) fire
load_bearing.comment: Matches word for word; singular verb yāraḏ.

load_bearing.french: sa fumée montait comme la fumée d'une fournaise
load_bearing.gloss: and its smoke went up like the smoke of the kiln
load_bearing.comment: Matches; kiḇšān is a kiln/smelting furnace.

load_bearing.gloss: and the whole mountain trembled greatly
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.french: Le son du cor allait en se renforçant de plus en plus
load_bearing.original: וַיְהִי֙ ק֣וֹל הַשּׁוֹפָ֔ר הוֹלֵ֖ךְ וְחָזֵ֣ק מְאֹ֑ד
load_bearing.translit: wayhî qôl haššôp̄ār hôlēḵ wəḥāzēq məʾōḏ
load_bearing.gloss: and the sound of the shofar was going on and growing very strong
load_bearing.comment: Matches; a continuously intensifying sound.

load_bearing.gloss: Moses would speak and the Elohim would answer him with a voice/sound
load_bearing.comment: Cut by the canon's '(...)'. hāʾĕlōhîm (with article) takes a singular verb, yaʿănennû.

ellipsis.cut: The '(...)' removes 19:19b: 'Moses spoke, and the Elohim answered him by a voice'.
ellipsis.note: The cut clause would have served the canon (a spoken exchange with 'the Elohim'); its removal does not change the sense of what is kept.

items.analysis: Each physical element the reading uses — a descent (yāraḏ) onto the mountain, in fire, with kiln-like smoke, ground tremor and a sound that keeps getting louder — is in the Hebrew exactly as in the French. No noun names a vehicle, so the identification is interpretive, but the hook is textual and not translation-made. Grammatical number: yāraḏ is singular with YHWH, and in the elided v 19b hāʾĕlōhîm also governs a singular verb; the canon's plural 'Ils descendirent' is not reflected in these verses.

items.ref_note: Two speakers are spliced into one quotation: v 23 is Moses speaking to YHWH, v 24 is YHWH's reply.
items.canon_french: «Le peuple ne pourra monter au Mont Sinaï (...) que les prêtres et le peuple ne se ruent pas pour monter vers Iahvé, de peur qu'il ne les abatte»

reading_quotes.french: Mais les créateurs eurent peur d'être envahis ou bousculés par les hommes, il fallait qu'ils soient respectés, vénérés même, afin de n'être pas en danger.

items.reading_summary: The creators feared being overrun or jostled by the people and needed to be respected, even venerated, for their own safety.

load_bearing.french: ne se ruent pas pour monter vers Iahvé
load_bearing.gloss: let them not break through to go up to YHWH
load_bearing.comment: hāras is 'tear down, break through'; French 'se ruer' (rush) is close. This is the hook for 'envahis ou bousculés'.

load_bearing.french: de peur qu'il ne les abatte
load_bearing.gloss: lest he break out against them
load_bearing.comment: The stated danger runs from YHWH to the people, not from the people to YHWH.

load_bearing.gloss: set bounds around the mountain and consecrate it
load_bearing.comment: Cut by '(...)': the reason given in the text for the exclusion is that the mountain is consecrated.

load_bearing.gloss: and many of them fall
load_bearing.comment: v 21 (not quoted): the anticipated casualties are among the people.

ellipsis.cut: The '(...)' removes the rest of v 23 ('for you yourself warned us, saying: set bounds around the mountain and consecrate it') and the first half of v 24 ('And YHWH said to him: go down, and come up, you and Aaron with you'), fusing Moses' speech and YHWH's speech.
ellipsis.note: The cut removes (a) the change of speaker and (b) the text's own rationale (consecration of the mountain). What remains reads as one continuous order.

items.analysis: The crowd-surge image has a real Hebrew basis in ʾal-yehersû 'let them not break through'. But the motive the canon assigns — the creators' fear for their own safety — reverses the direction of danger in the Hebrew, where it is the people who would 'fall' (v 21) and against whom YHWH would 'break out' (vv 22, 24), and where the reason for the boundary is consecration (v 23b, elided). The canon's French still contains 'de peur qu'il ne les abatte', so the reversal is visible inside its own quotation.

items.canon_french: «Moïse s'avancera seul vers Iahvé, mais les anciens d'Israël ne s'avanceront pas et le peuple ne montera pas avec lui !»

reading_quotes.french: il fallait qu'ils soient respectés, vénérés même, afin de n'être pas en danger

items.reading_summary: Further evidence that the creators kept people at a distance.

load_bearing.gloss: and Moses alone shall draw near to YHWH
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.french: mais les anciens d'Israël ne s'avanceront pas
load_bearing.gloss: but they shall not draw near
load_bearing.comment: Hebrew has only the pronoun 'they'; 'les anciens d'Israël' is an explanatory substitution (the antecedent in v 1 is Aaron, Nadab, Abihu and seventy of the elders).

items.french_variance: The canon's French replaces the pronoun wəhēm with a noun phrase; whether this is Dhorme's wording or the canon's has not been collated.
items.analysis: Graded access (Moses alone; 'they' at a distance; the people not at all) is what the Hebrew says. The only French-side feature is the expansion of 'they' into 'the elders of Israel', which narrows the antecedent of v 1 but does not affect the reading.

items.canon_french: «Ils virent le Dieu d'Israël. Sous ses pieds il y avait comme un ouvrage en plaque de saphir et d'une pureté pareille à la substance des cieux»

reading_quotes.french: Vous avez là une description du piédestal sur lequel un des créateurs se montra et qui était fait du même alliage bleuté que le plancher de l'engin où nous sommes actuellement.

items.reading_summary: The verse describes the pedestal on which one of the creators showed himself, made of the same bluish alloy as the floor of the craft.

load_bearing.gloss: the Elohim of Israel (construct of ʾĕlōhîm)
load_bearing.comment: The canon prints 'Dieu' here although the Hebrew noun is ʾĕlōhîm; compare TBWTT-2:5, which calls 'Dieu' an unjust translation of Elohim.

load_bearing.gloss: and under his feet (3 m.sg. suffix)
load_bearing.comment: Singular possessor — consistent with the canon's 'un des créateurs' — and a figure with feet.

load_bearing.french: comme un ouvrage en plaque de saphir
load_bearing.gloss: like a work (manufacture) of brick/tile of sappîr
load_bearing.comment: maʿăśēh is 'something made'; liḇnâ is a brick or paving tile. 'Plaque' is fair. The kə- makes it a comparison. sappîr is a stone (probably lapis lazuli per the library note), not a metal.

load_bearing.french: d'une pureté pareille à la substance des cieux
load_bearing.gloss: and like the very substance (lit. bone) of the skies for clearness
load_bearing.comment: Matches; supports sky-coloured/clear.

items.french_variance: 'Dieu' for ʾĕlōhê here vs 'Elohim' elsewhere in the same chapter of the canon (TBWTT-3:3, 3:82).
items.analysis: A made surface (maʿăśēh), of tile-work (liḇnâ), blue and sky-clear, under the feet of a single visible figure: all of this is Hebrew, and the French renders it without loss. 'Alliage' is the canon's addition — the material named is a stone — and both clauses are similes (kə- … ûḵə-). The unquoted v 11 ('they beheld the Elohim, and they ate and drank') reinforces the plain visibility of the figure. The canon's French says 'Dieu' where the Hebrew has ʾĕlōhê, the reverse of its usual practice.

items.canon_french: «(...) l'aspect de la gloire de Iahvé était comme un feu dévorant au sommet de la montagne (...)»

reading_quotes.french: Vous avez là la description de la «gloire», l'engin volant en réalité, des créateurs et comme vous avez pu le remarquer, au moment du départ il prend une coloration semblable à celle d'un feu.

items.reading_summary: 'Glory' is in reality the creators' flying craft, which takes on a fire-like colour at take-off.

load_bearing.gloss: the kāḇôḏ of YHWH — from kbd 'be heavy'; weight, substance, splendour
load_bearing.comment: French 'gloire' is abstract; the Hebrew noun's root sense is weight/heaviness (cf. ʿānān kāḇēḏ 'heavy cloud', Exod 19:16).

load_bearing.gloss: and the appearance (what is seen)
load_bearing.comment: The kāḇôḏ has a visible 'appearance': it is treated as something looked at.

load_bearing.gloss: like a consuming fire
load_bearing.comment: A simile (kə-), as in the French 'comme'.

load_bearing.gloss: and the kāḇôḏ of YHWH settled/dwelt on Mount Sinai
load_bearing.comment: v 16 (not quoted): the kāḇôḏ 'settles' on the mountain and stays six days under cloud; nothing departs.

ellipsis.cut: Opening '(...)' is a nominal cut of the conjunction; closing '(...)' cuts 'before the eyes of the children of Israel'.
ellipsis.note: The cut 'before the eyes of the children of Israel' would have reinforced visibility.

items.analysis: That the kāḇôḏ is a localized, visible thing with an 'appearance' that 'settles' on a mountain (v 16) is Hebrew, and the Hebrew noun (root kbd, weight) is more concrete than French 'gloire' — on the noun the original is the more favourable. On the event it is less favourable: the context has the kāḇôḏ dwelling on the mountain for days (wayyiškōn), with no departure, whereas the reading ties the fire colour to 'le moment du départ'. The fire is a comparison in both languages. The equation gloire = craft is not made by any word of the verse.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] The derivation of kāḇôḏ from kbd 'be heavy' is standard lexicon material (BDB/HALOT) but is not stated in the library note for this verse.

items.canon_french: «De tout homme (...) vous prendrez un prélèvement pour moi (...) or, argent et cuivre, pierres (précieuses), etc.»

reading_quotes.french: avait envie de nourriture fraîche, voici pourquoi elle demanda que le peuple d'Israël lui en donne régulièrement, ainsi que des richesses à ramener ensuite sur sa planète. C'était un peu de la colonisation si vous voulez.

items.reading_summary: The resident team of creators wanted fresh food and asked Israel to supply it regularly, together with riches to take back to their planet — 'a bit of colonisation'.

load_bearing.french: De tout homme (...) vous prendrez un prélèvement pour moi
load_bearing.original: מֵאֵ֤ת כָּל־אִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִדְּבֶ֣נּוּ לִבּ֔וֹ תִּקְח֖וּ אֶת־תְּרוּמָתִֽי׃
load_bearing.translit: mēʾēṯ kol-ʾîš ʾăšer yiddəḇennû libbô tiqḥû ʾeṯ-tərûmāṯî
load_bearing.gloss: from every man whose heart moves him (to give freely) you shall take my contribution
load_bearing.comment: The canon's first '(...)' removes exactly the relative clause 'whose heart makes him willing'.

load_bearing.gloss: gold and silver and copper/bronze
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.gloss: šōham stones and stones for setting, for the ephod and for the breastpiece
load_bearing.comment: The Hebrew states the stones' purpose (priestly vestments); the canon's bracketed '(précieuses)' and 'etc.' replace it.

load_bearing.gloss: and let them make me a sanctuary
load_bearing.comment: v 8 (not quoted here): the stated destination of the materials.

ellipsis.cut: (1) 'whose heart makes him willing' (v 2); (2) vv 4–6: dyed yarns, linen, goat hair, skins, acacia wood, lamp oil, spices for anointing oil and incense; (3) the purpose clauses of v 7 ('for the ephod and the breastpiece'), replaced by 'etc.'.
ellipsis.note: The first cut turns a freewill contribution into a levy; the others remove the items and purpose clauses that show the list to be building and vestment materials.

items.analysis: The reading needs a compulsory levy of food and exportable wealth. The Hebrew list contains no foodstuff (the only consumables are lamp oil and spices for anointing oil and incense), the giving is explicitly voluntary (ʾăšer yiddəḇennû libbô), and v 8 states the use: a sanctuary to be built on the spot. The French the canon quotes would say the same if quoted in full; the effect is produced by the three elisions. The canon's next paragraph (TBWTT-3:36) itself goes on to the residence, which is the Hebrew's stated purpose.

items.stated_reference: chapitre XXVI de l'Exode (prose reference, no quotation)
items.actual_reference: Exod 26 (tabernacle instructions); the governing statement is Exod 25:8–9
items.ref_note: Exod 26 is not in the library; the command to build is at 25:8–9, which is.
items.canon_french: Ils avaient également décidé de s'installer plus confortablement et demandèrent aux hommes de leur confectionner une résidence suivant leurs plans.

reading_quotes.french: Dans cette résidence ils devaient rencontrer les représentants des hommes : c'est la tente du rendez-vous où les hommes apportaient nourriture et présents en gage de soumission.

items.reading_summary: The creators had men build them a residence to their own plans, where they would meet men's representatives: the Tent of Meeting.

load_bearing.gloss: the dwelling-place (from šāḵan 'dwell')
load_bearing.comment: The Hebrew technical term for the tabernacle literally means 'dwelling'; 'résidence' is its plain sense.

load_bearing.gloss: and I will dwell in their midst
load_bearing.comment: The purpose clause, not quoted by the canon.

load_bearing.gloss: the pattern/model of the dwelling
load_bearing.comment: taḇnîṯ (from bānâ 'build') is a construction model or plan, shown to Moses ('according to all that I show you').

ellipsis.cut: No quotation.

items.analysis: This is a case where the canon cites a chapter without quoting and the unquoted Hebrew is closer to its reading than any French it prints: the structure is called miškān 'dwelling', its purpose is 'that I may dwell (wəšāḵantî) in their midst', and it is to be made after a taḇnîṯ 'plan/model' shown to Moses. The speaker and the dweller are singular ('I'); the canon's plural 'ils' is its own. 'More comfortably' and 'in token of submission' are additions.

items.actual_reference: Not a verse as worded; nearest is Exod 33:8–9 (Moses entering the tent)
items.ref_note: Printed in guillemets as if a quotation, with no reference; no verse of Exod 33 has this wording. Its subject ('Il') is ambiguous.
items.canon_french: «Il entrerait dans la tente du rendez-vous»

reading_quotes.french: c'est la tente du rendez-vous où les hommes apportaient nourriture et présents en gage de soumission

items.reading_summary: The Tent of Meeting is the residence in which the creators met men's representatives.

load_bearing.gloss: tent of appointed meeting (môʿēḏ from yāʿaḏ 'appoint, meet by appointment')
load_bearing.comment: 'Rendez-vous' renders môʿēḏ accurately; the meeting sense is Hebrew, not a French colouring.

load_bearing.original: וּמֹשֶׁה֩ יִקַּ֨ח אֶת־הָאֹ֜הֶל וְנָֽטָה־ל֣וֹ ׀ מִח֣וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֗ה
load_bearing.translit: ûmōšeh yiqqaḥ ʾeṯ-hāʾōhel wənāṭâ-lô miḥûṣ lammaḥăneh
load_bearing.gloss: and Moses would take the tent and pitch it for himself outside the camp
load_bearing.comment: In Exod 33 the 'tent of meeting' is a tent Moses himself pitches outside the camp — not the miškān built to plan in Exod 25–26, which the canon identifies with it.

items.analysis: ʾōhel môʿēḏ does mean a tent of (appointed) meeting, so the 'rendez-vous' sense the canon relies on is in the Hebrew. Two cautions: the guillemeted sentence is not locatable as a verse, and in Exod 33:7 the tent of meeting is Moses' own tent outside the camp, a different object in the narrative from the planned 'résidence' of Exod 26 with which TBWTT-3:36 merges it. Nothing in 33:7–11 mentions food or gifts brought there.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] That the ʾōhel môʿēḏ of Exod 33:7–11 and the priestly miškān are distinct traditions is a commonplace of Pentateuch scholarship; no source was consulted here.

items.canon_french: «Dès que Moïse entrait dans la tente, la colonne de nuée descendait et s'arrêtait à l'entrée de la tente. Alors Il parlait avec Moïse»

reading_quotes.french: Dans cette résidence ils devaient rencontrer les représentants des hommes

items.reading_summary: The column of cloud comes down to the tent door and 'He' speaks with Moses: a meeting between a creator and men's representative.

load_bearing.french: la colonne de nuée descendait et s'arrêtait à l'entrée de la tente
load_bearing.original: יֵרֵד֙ עַמּ֣וּד הֶֽעָנָ֔ן וְעָמַ֖ד פֶּ֣תַח הָאֹ֑הֶל
load_bearing.translit: yērēḏ ʿammûḏ heʿānān wəʿāmaḏ peṯaḥ hāʾōhel
load_bearing.gloss: the pillar of cloud would come down and stand at the entrance of the tent
load_bearing.comment: Matches; a descent verb (yāraḏ) with the column as subject.

load_bearing.gloss: and (it/he) would speak with Moses
load_bearing.comment: No subject is expressed. The only expressed subject of the three consecutive verbs (come down, stand, speak) is the pillar of cloud. The canon's capitalised 'Il' supplies a person.

items.french_variance: The capital 'Il' is a French-side disambiguation of a subjectless Hebrew verb.
items.analysis: Descent and stationing of the column at the door are Hebrew. On the speaker the Hebrew is more favourable to the canon's picture than the French: grammatically it is the column itself that descends, stands and 'speaks with Moses', i.e. the voice is not separated from the object, whereas French 'Alors Il' introduces a distinct divine person. v 11 then names YHWH as the speaker, so the ambiguity is resolved by context, but v 9 on its own attaches speech to the column.

items.canon_french: «Alors Iahvé parlait à Moïse, face à face, comme parle un homme à son prochain...»

reading_quotes.french: Comme aujourd'hui je peux vous parler et vous pouvez me parler, d'homme à homme.

items.reading_summary: YHWH spoke to Moses as the speaker now speaks to Raël, man to man.

load_bearing.gloss: face to face
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.french: comme parle un homme à son prochain
load_bearing.gloss: as a man speaks to his companion
load_bearing.comment: Matches; ʾîš 'man' is in the Hebrew, in a comparison (kaʾăšer).

ellipsis.cut: The canon's '...' drops 'and he would return to the camp; but his attendant Joshua … would not depart from the tent'.

items.analysis: The wording the reading rests on (pānîm ʾel-pānîm; ʾîš ʾel-rēʿēhû) is Hebrew and is rendered exactly. It is a comparison ('as a man speaks'), which the canon takes as a description of the manner of the encounter. The verse stands nine verses before 33:20 ('you cannot see my face'), a tension the canon itself addresses at LWTE-1:4.

items.canon_french: «Tu ne peux voir ma Face car l'homme ne peut me voir et vivre !»

reading_quotes.french: Vous avez là l'allusion à la différence d'atmosphère existant entre nos planètes. Un homme ne peut voir ses créateurs sans que ces derniers soient protégés par un scaphandre
«Tu ne peux voir ma face, car l'homme ne peut voir ma face et vivre »

items.reading_summary: An allusion to the difference in atmosphere between the two planets: men can see the creators only when the latter wear a protective suit; a man on their planet would see them bare-faced but die.

load_bearing.french: Tu ne peux voir ma Face
load_bearing.gloss: you are not able to see my face
load_bearing.comment: Matches; pānîm 'face' is literal.

load_bearing.french: car l'homme ne peut me voir et vivre
load_bearing.gloss: for the human shall not see me and live
load_bearing.comment: Hebrew has 'see me' (yirʾanî), as TBWTT prints; LWTE-1:4 re-quotes the verse with 'voir ma face' in the second clause too.

load_bearing.gloss: and they beheld the Elohim, and they ate and drank
load_bearing.comment: Exod 24:11 (quoted context of TBWTT-3:30): seventy-four people see 'the Elohim' and survive.

items.french_variance: The canon quotes this verse twice with different French: TBWTT-3:41 '…ne peut me voir et vivre', LWTE-1:4 '…ne peut voir ma face et vivre'. The Hebrew agrees with the TBWTT form.
items.analysis: The verse states a prohibition/impossibility and a lethal consequence; it names no cause. Atmosphere and protective suits are supplied by the canon to wording that is identical in sense in Hebrew and French. The specific object is the face (pānāy), which fits a reading about an uncovered face, but the same book has Moses addressed 'face to face' (33:11) and the elders seeing the Elohim and living (24:10–11), both of which the canon also quotes.

items.ref_note: Introduced as an example from 'tout le début du Lévitique', but chapter 21 is not at the beginning of the book.
items.canon_french: «Car tout homme qui a en lui une tare n'approchera pas pour offrir l'aliment de son Dieu»

reading_quotes.french: afin d'éviter que des hommes malades ou difformes, symboles d'un échec et insupportables aux yeux des créateurs, ne se présentent devant eux
comment les aliments offerts aux créateurs doivent être amenés pour leur ravitaillement

items.reading_summary: Leviticus regulates how food is to be brought for the creators' provisioning; the sick or deformed, symbols of failure, are kept out of their sight.

ellipsis.cut: Cannot be determined: Leviticus 21 is not in the library.

items.analysis: Leviticus 21 is not held in the library in Hebrew (leviticus-woh has only chapters 17 and 25), so the load-bearing phrase 'l'aliment de son Dieu' cannot be compared against library data. The introductory claim places the passage at 'the beginning' of Leviticus, which chapter 21 is not.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] The Hebrew of Lev 21:17 is commonly cited as leḥem ʾĕlōhāyw 'the bread/food of his God'; if so the 'aliment' wording would be Hebrew-supported. Not verified against a text for this audit.

items.canon_french: «La manne était comme de la graine de coriandre et son aspect comme l'aspect du bdellium (...) son goût était comme le goût d'une friandise à l'huile»

reading_quotes.french: la description très exacte de la manne que vos chimistes pourraient reconstituer
Mais cette manne n'était qu'une nourriture chimique à laquelle les créateurs préféraient les fruits et légumes frais.

items.reading_summary: A description exact enough for chemists to reconstitute the manna, which was only a chemical food.

load_bearing.french: comme de la graine de coriandre
load_bearing.gloss: like seed of gaḏ (traditionally coriander)
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.gloss: like the look (lit. eye) of bəḏōlaḥ
load_bearing.comment: Matches; bəḏōlaḥ is itself an uncertain substance (resin or stone).

load_bearing.french: le goût d'une friandise à l'huile
load_bearing.gloss: like the taste of the ləšaḏ of oil (ləšaḏ uncertain: moisture/richness)
load_bearing.comment: 'Friandise' (a confection) follows the LXX-type reading ('cake with oil') per the library note; the MT word does not mean a prepared dainty.

ellipsis.cut: The '(...)' removes 11:8a: the people went about, gathered it, ground it in mills or pounded it in a mortar, boiled it in pots and made cakes of it.
ellipsis.note: The cut removes the processing steps (a hard, millable material); it does not change the comparison terms.

items.analysis: All three descriptors are comparisons (kə-) to things that are themselves uncertain (gaḏ, bəḏōlaḥ, ləšaḏ), so 'very exact description' overstates what the Hebrew offers; the uncertainty is smoothed by the French ('coriandre', 'bdellium', 'friandise'). In particular 'friandise à l'huile' is a versional reading, not the MT's lexical sense. 'Chemical' is an addition.

items.canon_french: «Les primeurs de tout ce qui sera en leur pays et qu'ils apporteront à Iahvé»

reading_quotes.french: les créateurs préféraient les fruits et légumes frais

items.reading_summary: The creators preferred fresh fruit and vegetables to the manna, hence the first-fruits brought to YHWH.

load_bearing.french: Les primeurs de tout ce qui sera en leur pays
load_bearing.gloss: the first-ripe produce of all that is in their land
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.gloss: which they bring to YHWH
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.gloss: shall be yours (2 m.sg. — Aaron)
load_bearing.comment: The main clause of the sentence, absent from the quotation with no ellipsis mark.

load_bearing.gloss: every clean person in your house shall eat it
load_bearing.comment: Also absent: the produce is eaten by the priest's household.

ellipsis.cut: Silent truncation (no '(...)'): the quotation ends before the predicate 'shall be yours; everyone who is clean in your house shall eat of it'.
ellipsis.note: What the canon prints is a subject with its relative clauses; the predicate, which says who gets and eats the produce, is dropped without notice.

items.analysis: The quoted words are accurate but form only the subject of the Hebrew sentence. Its predicate assigns the first-fruits to Aaron ('ləḵā yihyeh') and has his household eat them. The verse therefore says the opposite of what it is cited for: the fresh produce 'brought to YHWH' is consumed by the human priesthood. The effect comes from the truncation, not from the French.

items.canon_french: «Fais-toi un serpent brûlant et place-le sur une hampe : quiconque aura été mordu et le verra, il vivra !»

reading_quotes.french: Plus loin les créateurs apprennent aux hommes à faire des piqûres contre les morsures de serpents.
Dès qu'un homme était mordu, il «regardait» le «serpent d'airain», on approchait de lui une seringue, et on lui faisait une piqûre de sérum.

items.reading_summary: The creators taught men to give injections against snakebite: the bitten man 'looked at' the bronze serpent, a syringe was brought and serum injected.

load_bearing.gloss: a śārāp̄ — 'burning one' (root śrp 'burn')
load_bearing.comment: Hebrew has the single noun śārāp̄, without 'serpent'; 'serpent brûlant' expands it.

load_bearing.gloss: on a standard/signal-pole
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.gloss: and (he) sees it, and lives
load_bearing.comment: Seeing is the only stated means.

load_bearing.gloss: a serpent of bronze/copper
load_bearing.comment: v 9, quoted as a phrase in the reading paragraph; matches.

load_bearing.gloss: and he looked toward the serpent of bronze
load_bearing.comment: v 9 uses a different, more deliberate verb (hibbîṭ 'gaze at') than v 8 (rāʾâ 'see').

items.analysis: The Hebrew says a bitten person who sees (v 8) or gazes at (v 9) the bronze figure lives; no instrument, substance or operator is mentioned. Injection and serum are added to wording that is neutral in both languages; the canon marks the distance itself by putting 'regardait' in scare-quotes. The pole-mounted serpent as a sign at which treatment is given is compatible with the text but not derivable from it.

items.canon_french: «Vous détruirez toutes leurs statues de métal fondu (...) vous posséderez le pays»

reading_quotes.french: Ils détruisent, sur les conseils des créateurs, les idoles des peuplades primitives et occupent leurs territoires.

items.reading_summary: On the creators' advice the chosen people destroy the idols of the primitive tribes and occupy their territories.

load_bearing.french: toutes leurs statues de métal fondu
load_bearing.gloss: all their cast (molten) images
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.gloss: and you shall take possession of the land
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.gloss: and you shall dispossess/drive out all the inhabitants of the land from before you
load_bearing.comment: Opening clause of v 52, not quoted: the expulsion of the inhabitants.

ellipsis.cut: Not quoted: 'you shall drive out all the inhabitants of the land' and 'destroy all their figured stones' (before the quoted clause, silently); the '(...)' covers 'and demolish all their high places'.
ellipsis.note: The reading paragraph states the occupation anyway; the omission softens but does not alter.

items.analysis: A historical, not technological, reading, and the Hebrew says what the canon says: a divine order to destroy cast images and take the land. 'Sur les conseils' understates a command (the verbs are 2nd-person plural perfect-consecutives in a speech of YHWH, v 50–51).

items.canon_french: «Parce qu'il a aimé tes pères, il a choisi leur race après eux (...)»

reading_quotes.french: Le peuple élu avait enfin son pays promis :

items.reading_summary: The chosen people at last has its promised country.

load_bearing.gloss: and he chose
load_bearing.comment: Matches; the basis of 'peuple élu'.

load_bearing.gloss: his seed after him (singular suffixes)
load_bearing.comment: MT is singular ('his seed after him'); the canon's plural is the versional reading (Samaritan, LXX) per the library note.

load_bearing.gloss: and he brought you out with his face/presence, with his great power
load_bearing.comment: Cut by '(...)': 'with his face' (in person).

ellipsis.cut: Cuts 'and brought you out with his presence, with his great power, out of Egypt'.
ellipsis.note: The elided bəp̄ānāyw ('in person') would have suited the canon's reading of the Exodus.

items.french_variance: 'leur race après eux' follows the plural versions against the MT singular.
items.analysis: The election statement is Hebrew (wayyiḇḥar). The plural 'leur … eux' is a translation-layer feature (it follows the versions, not the MT), but nothing in the canon's reading depends on the number of the suffix.

items.canon_french: «(...) dès que les porteurs de l'arche furent arrivés (...) les eaux qui descendent d'en haut s'arrêtèrent, elles se figèrent en un seul bloc à une très grande distance (...) les eaux furent entièrement coupées et le peuple traversa (...)»

reading_quotes.french: Les créateurs firent passer le «peuple élu» à pied sec, comme lors de la fuite devant les Egyptiens, en utilisant le même rayon répulseur.

items.reading_summary: The creators took the people across the Jordan dry-shod with the same repulsor ray as at the sea.

load_bearing.french: dès que les porteurs de l'arche furent arrivés
load_bearing.gloss: and when the bearers of the ark came to the Jordan
load_bearing.comment: Matches; the trigger in the text is the arrival of the ark.

load_bearing.french: elles se figèrent en un seul bloc
load_bearing.gloss: they rose up, one heap
load_bearing.comment: qûm is 'rise, stand up'; nēḏ is 'heap, dam'. French 'se figèrent … bloc' (congealed into a block) suggests solidification, which the Hebrew verb does not say.

load_bearing.gloss: very far off
load_bearing.comment: Matches, but the Hebrew continues with a place-name.

load_bearing.gloss: the city that is beside Zarethan
load_bearing.comment: Cut: the stoppage is located at/from Adam, a named town upstream (Ketiv 'at Adam', Qere 'from Adam').

load_bearing.gloss: were completely cut off
load_bearing.comment: Matches; said of the downstream water draining to the Dead Sea.

ellipsis.cut: Cuts: the priests' feet dipping in the water's edge and the note that the Jordan floods at harvest (v 15b); the location 'at/from Adam, the city beside Zarethan'; 'those going down to the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea'; 'opposite Jericho'.
ellipsis.note: With the place-names removed the stoppage reads as occurring at the crossing; in the Hebrew the water piles up far upstream at a named town and the bed downstream simply drains.

items.analysis: The Hebrew describes a river dammed 'very far off' at a named upstream location, with the lower reach running dry — a different geometry from the sea crossing (wind; walls of water to right and left, Exod 14:21–22) to which the canon assimilates it ('le même rayon'). The mechanism is unstated in Hebrew, so the ray is an addition; the elision of the upstream place-name and the French 'se figèrent en un seul bloc' (for qāmû 'rose') both nudge the excerpt toward an on-the-spot, solid-wall picture the Hebrew does not give.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] Whether 'se figèrent en un seul bloc' is Dhorme's wording has not been collated.

items.canon_french: «... je suis le chef de l'armée de Iahvé, je viens d'arriver !»

reading_quotes.french: il y a un contact entre un militairecréateur et le peuple élu devant la résistance d'une ville : Jéricho
un conseiller militaire est envoyé au peuple juif

items.reading_summary: A military member of the creators makes contact with Joshua before Jericho, as a military adviser.

load_bearing.french: le chef de l'armée de Iahvé
load_bearing.gloss: commander of the army of YHWH
load_bearing.comment: śar ṣāḇāʾ is the ordinary title of a human army commander; the French is literal.

load_bearing.gloss: now I have come
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.original: וְהִנֵּה־אִישׁ֙ עֹמֵ֣ד לְנֶגְדּ֔וֹ וְחַרְבּ֥וֹ שְׁלוּפָ֖ה בְּיָד֑וֹ
load_bearing.translit: wəhinnēh-ʾîš ʿōmēḏ ləneḡdô wəḥarbô šəlûp̄â bəyāḏô
load_bearing.gloss: and behold, a man standing opposite him, his sword drawn in his hand
load_bearing.comment: v 13 (not quoted): the narrator calls the figure ʾîš 'a man', armed.

ellipsis.cut: The '...' drops the opening 'No' (lōʾ, answering 'Are you for us or for our adversaries?'); the quotation stops before Joshua falls on his face and bows.

items.analysis: The reading — a military officer of YHWH's forces arriving in person — is the literal sense of śar-ṣəḇāʾ-YHWH ʿattâ ḇāʾṯî. The Hebrew context is more favourable than the excerpt: the narrator introduces him as ʾîš, 'a man', with a drawn sword (v 13), which the canon does not quote. 'Conseiller' is the canon's inference; the figure gives no military advice in the preserved verses (v 15 is about removing sandals on holy ground).

items.canon_french: «Lorsqu'on traînera (sur la note) de la corne de bélier, dès que vous entendrez le son de la trompette (...) la muraille de la ville tombera»

reading_quotes.french: en utilisant les ultra-sons très amplifiés, on peut faire s'écrouler n'importe quelle muraille en béton. C'est ce qui fut fait grâce à un instrument très compliqué que la Bible nomme «trompette».
A un moment précis, les ultra-sons sont émis d'une façon synchronisée et la muraille s'effondre.

items.reading_summary: The walls fell to greatly amplified ultrasound from a very complicated instrument 'that the Bible calls trumpet', emitted in a synchronised way.

load_bearing.gloss: with the horn of the ram
load_bearing.comment: The instrument is first named as an animal's horn; the canon's own quotation keeps this.

load_bearing.gloss: the sound of the shofar
load_bearing.comment: šôp̄ār is the ram's-horn; 'trompette' (a manufactured metal instrument) is the French/English Bible convention. Hebrew has a separate word for the metal trumpet (ḥăṣōṣərâ) which is not used here.

load_bearing.gloss: all the people shall shout a great shout
load_bearing.comment: Cut by the canon's '(...)': the action that immediately precedes the wall's fall is the people's shout.

load_bearing.french: la muraille de la ville tombera
load_bearing.gloss: and the wall of the city shall fall in its place (lit. under itself)
load_bearing.comment: Matches; taḥtêhā 'beneath itself' (collapse in place) is not in the canon's French.

ellipsis.cut: The '(...)' removes 'all the people shall shout with a great shout'; the end of the verse ('and the people shall go up, each straight before him') is also dropped.
ellipsis.note: In the Hebrew sequence (6:5 and its fulfilment 6:20) the wall falls when the people shout on hearing the horn; the cut leaves the horn as the only sound.

items.analysis: The reading turns on the name of the instrument: 'un instrument très compliqué que la Bible nomme «trompette»'. The Hebrew Bible does not name it so; it calls it qeren hayyôḇēl 'ram's horn' and šôp̄ār, i.e. the simplest of wind instruments, and reserves another word for the metal trumpet. 'Trompette' is a translation convention, and the canon's own quotation contains 'corne de bélier' alongside it. The elision further removes the people's great shout, which in Hebrew stands between the horn-blast and the collapse. The synchronised timing ('when you hear … then') is Hebrew.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] The contrast šôp̄ār / ḥăṣōṣərâ is stated in the library note at Judg 7:22; the claim that the French and English Bibles conventionally print 'trompette/trumpet' here is from the library note at Josh 6:5, not from a collation of Dhorme.

items.canon_french: «Iahvé lança des cieux contre eux de grandes pierres (...). Ceux qui moururent par les pierres de grêle furent plus nombreux que ceux que les fils d'Israël tuèrent par l'épée»

reading_quotes.french: Un bombardement en règle qui tua plus de gens que les armes blanches du peuple d'Israël.

items.reading_summary: A regular bombardment from the sky that killed more than Israel's swords.

load_bearing.french: Iahvé lança des cieux contre eux de grandes pierres
load_bearing.original: וַֽיהוָ֡ה הִשְׁלִ֣יךְ עֲלֵיהֶם֩ אֲבָנִ֨ים גְּדֹל֧וֹת מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֛יִם
load_bearing.translit: waYHWH hišlîḵ ʿălêhem ʾăḇānîm gəḏōlôṯ min-haššāmayim
load_bearing.gloss: and YHWH threw down on them great stones from the skies
load_bearing.comment: hišlîḵ is 'throw, hurl' — a verb of projection, not of precipitation; the French 'lança' is exact.

load_bearing.gloss: by the stones of hail
load_bearing.comment: The narrator identifies the stones as hail; the canon keeps this in its quotation but not in its reading.

ellipsis.cut: The '(...)' removes 'as far as Azekah, and they died'; the opening 'as they fled before Israel, on the descent of Beth-horon' is not quoted.

items.analysis: 'Hurled great stones from the skies' is the literal Hebrew (hišlîḵ … min-haššāmayim), and the casualty comparison is as quoted, so the hook for 'bombardment' is textual. The same verse, also in the canon's own French, calls the stones ʾaḇnê habbārāḏ 'hailstones'; the reading passes over that identification. No difference between Hebrew and French on either point.

items.canon_french: «Le soleil s'arrêta et la lune stationna, jusqu'à ce que la nation se fût vengée de ses ennemis»

reading_quotes.french: Un des passages les plus déformés est celui où il est dit

la guerre fut une guerre éclair qui ne dura qu'une journée puisqu'il est dit plus loin qu'elle dura «presque un jour entier». Cette guerre fut si courte par rapport à l'importance du terrain conquis que les hommes crurent que le soleil s'était arrêté...

items.reading_summary: One of the 'most distorted' passages: it simply means a lightning war lasting about one day; because so much ground was taken so fast, men believed the sun had stopped.

load_bearing.french: Le soleil s'arrêta et la lune stationna
load_bearing.gloss: and the sun was still/silent, and the moon stood
load_bearing.comment: dāmam is 'be still, be silent, cease'; ʿāmaḏ 'stand'. The first verb is less specifically 'stop moving' than French 's'arrêta'.

load_bearing.gloss: and (it) did not hasten to set, about a whole day
load_bearing.comment: In Hebrew 'about a whole day' measures how long the sun did not hasten to set. Its subject is the sun, not the war.

load_bearing.gloss: and the sun stood in the middle of the skies
load_bearing.comment: The clause immediately before 'about a whole day'; not quoted.

ellipsis.cut: The quotation stops before 'Is this not written in the Book of Yashar?' and before 'the sun stood in the midst of the skies and did not hasten to set for about a whole day'.
ellipsis.note: The canon cites 'presque un jour entier' detached from its clause; in the Hebrew the phrase belongs to the sun's delay, and the intervening source-citation (Book of Yashar) marks the first half as quoted poetry.

items.analysis: The canon's argument is that the text 'says further on that it [the war] lasted almost a whole day'. In the Hebrew, kəyôm tāmîm is the adverbial of wəlōʾ-ʾāṣ lāḇôʾ: it is the sun that 'did not hasten to go down for about a whole day'. The text thus says the opposite of a short day's fighting mistaken for a miracle: it asserts a day-long delay of sunset and adds that there was no day like it (v 14). The canon signals this itself by calling the passage 'déformé' — its reading is a correction of the text, not a reading of it. One point for the canon: wayyiddōm (dmm 'be still/silent') is less unambiguously astronomical than 's'arrêta'.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] That dmm here may mean 'cease (shining)' rather than 'stop moving' is a known scholarly proposal; no source was consulted.

items.canon_french: «(...) l'Ange de Iahvé tendit le bout de la canne qui était dans sa main et toucha la viande et les azymes. Alors le feu monta de la roche, dévora la viande et les azymes ; puis l'Ange de Iahvé disparut (...)»

reading_quotes.french: un des créateurs se trouve encore au contact d'un homme nommé Gédéon qui lui remet de la nourriture

les créateurs, qui ne peuvent pas «manger» à l'air libre à cause de leurs scaphandres, peuvent en cas de besoin se servir des «offrandes» diverses pour en extraire l'essentiel qui, au moyen d'un tuyau flexible, une «canne», parvient à les alimenter. Cette opération dégage des flammes

items.reading_summary: The creators, unable to eat in the open because of their suits, extract the essentials of offerings through a flexible tube ('canne'); the operation gives off flames that men take for sacrifice.

load_bearing.gloss: the staff (something to lean on, from šʿn 'lean')
load_bearing.comment: A support staff — by etymology rigid. 'Canne' (walking-stick) is accurate; 'tuyau flexible' departs from both.

load_bearing.french: toucha la viande et les azymes
load_bearing.gloss: and touched the meat and the unleavened cakes
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.french: le feu monta de la roche
load_bearing.gloss: and the fire went up from the rock
load_bearing.comment: The fire's source is the rock, not the staff or the visitor.

load_bearing.gloss: and it ate/consumed
load_bearing.comment: The Hebrew verb is ʾāḵal 'eat' — it is the fire that 'eats' the food. French 'dévora' keeps this.

load_bearing.gloss: went from his eyes (walked out of his sight)
load_bearing.comment: Hebrew has the ordinary verb 'go/walk'; 'disparut' (vanished) is a French colouring.

load_bearing.gloss: and pour out the broth
load_bearing.comment: v 20 (not quoted): the visitor has the broth poured away and the solids laid on a rock.

ellipsis.cut: Opening '(...)' covers the transition from v 20 (instructions to lay the food on the rock and pour out the broth); closing '(...)' drops 'from his sight'.

items.french_variance: 'disparut' for hālaḵ mēʿênāyw is noted in the library as the French canon's wording.
items.analysis: The Hebrew has a staff-tip touching food laid on a rock, fire rising from the rock and 'eating' the food, and the messenger walking away. The feeding-tube reading requires the staff to be flexible and to convey matter to the visitor; mišʿeneṯ is a leaning-staff, the fire comes from the rock, and the liquid part of the meal is poured out on the ground (v 20). Two minor points the other way: the fire's verb is literally 'ate', and the visitor leaves on foot (hālaḵ), which the French 'disparut' turns into a vanishing.

items.canon_french: les 300 hommes qui encerclent un camp ennemi avec des «trompettes» et sonnent tous ensemble pour rendre fous les hommes, se servent d'instruments émettant des ultra-sons très amplifiés

reading_quotes.french: Effectivement, le peuple encerclé devient fou, les soldats s'entretuent et prennent la fuite.

items.reading_summary: Gideon's 300 used instruments emitting amplified ultrasound that drove the encircled army mad, so that the soldiers killed one another and fled.

load_bearing.gloss: shofars (ram's horns)
load_bearing.comment: Same convention as Josh 6:5: Hebrew names horns, the French Bible 'trompettes'.

load_bearing.gloss: and empty jars, and torches inside the jars
load_bearing.comment: Not mentioned by the canon: each man also carries a jar and a torch.

load_bearing.gloss: and they broke the jars
load_bearing.comment: The night attack combines horn-blasts, smashed jars, sudden torchlight and a war-cry.

load_bearing.original: וַיָּ֣שֶׂם יְהוָ֗ה אֵ֣ת חֶ֥רֶב אִ֛ישׁ בְּרֵעֵ֖הוּ
load_bearing.translit: wayyāśem YHWH ʾēṯ ḥereḇ ʾîš bərēʿēhû
load_bearing.gloss: and YHWH set each man's sword against his companion
load_bearing.comment: The mutual killing is in the Hebrew, attributed to YHWH; no madness is mentioned.

ellipsis.cut: Paraphrase, not quotation: jars, torches and the war-cry ('A sword for YHWH and for Gideon') are omitted.
ellipsis.note: The omission leaves the horns as the only agent of panic.

items.analysis: As at Jericho the technological reading is hung on the word 'trompettes', printed in scare-quotes; the Hebrew instrument is the šôp̄ār, a ram's horn. The Hebrew account gives the panic several ordinary causes at once — horns, smashed jars, torches suddenly uncovered at the change of watch, a shouted war-cry — and attributes the mutual slaughter to YHWH's action, without the motif of madness. The mutual killing and flight are textual.

items.canon_french: «L'Ange de Iahvé apparut à la femme et lui dit : «voici donc que tu es stérile (...). Mais tu vas concevoir et enfanter un fils»

reading_quotes.french: Quant aux accouplements entre les créateurs et les femmes des hommes vous en avez encore un exemple en Juges, XIII :
Il était nécessaire que le fruit de cette union soit sain afin d'observer son comportement

items.reading_summary: Judges 13 is another example of matings between creators and human women; the child of the union had to be healthy so its behaviour could be observed.

load_bearing.french: L'Ange de Iahvé apparut à la femme
load_bearing.gloss: and the messenger of YHWH appeared to the woman
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.french: tu vas concevoir et enfanter un fils
load_bearing.gloss: and you shall conceive and bear a son
load_bearing.comment: Matches; no begetter is named.

load_bearing.gloss: a man of the Elohim came to me
load_bearing.comment: v 6 (not quoted): the woman's own report. She calls the visitor ʾîš 'a man', and uses bôʾ ʾel 'come to', the verb-plus-preposition that is also the Hebrew idiom for sexual approach.

load_bearing.gloss: the sons of the Elohim came in to the daughters of the human
load_bearing.comment: Gen 6:4, which the canon quotes at TBWTT-2:54 for the same theme, uses the same bôʾ ʾel construction with 'the Elohim'.

ellipsis.cut: The '(...)' removes 'and have not borne' (wəlōʾ yālaḏt).

items.analysis: The quoted verse says only that a messenger appeared and announced a conception; 'union' is supplied by the canon. The Hebrew of the chapter is nevertheless more suggestive than the French excerpt: the woman reports 'ʾîš hāʾĕlōhîm bāʾ ʾēlay' — 'a man of the Elohim came to me' (v 6) — where bôʾ ʾel is the same idiom Gen 6:4 uses for the sons of the Elohim 'coming in to' the daughters of men, and the visitor is repeatedly called 'the man' (vv 6, 8, 10, 11). French 'vint vers' cannot carry the double sense. bôʾ ʾel is also the everyday expression for 'come to', so the Hebrew permits the insinuation without stating it.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] That Judg 13:6 bāʾ ʾēlay has been read by some commentators as a deliberate double entendre is recalled from secondary literature; no source was consulted and none is cited in the library notes.

items.ref_note: The quotation is spread over TBWTT-3:79–81.
items.canon_french: Le rasoir ne passera pas sur sa tête, car le garçon sera, dès le sein maternel, (voué) à Dieu»

reading_quotes.french: Les antennes, ce sont les cheveux et la barbe. D'où l'importance de ne pas raser le système pileux d'un être qui aura à s'en servir.
Il pouvait communiquer avec «Dieu» directement par télépathie grâce à ses «antennes» naturelles : ses cheveux.

items.reading_summary: The ban on wine keeps the child of the union healthy; the unshaven hair serves as antennas for telepathic communication with the creators.

load_bearing.french: Garde-toi bien de boire du vin et de la boisson enivrante
load_bearing.gloss: and do not drink wine or strong drink
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.gloss: and do not eat anything unclean
load_bearing.comment: Cut by the canon's '(...)' (TBWTT-3:80): the dietary rule is paired with ritual uncleanness.

load_bearing.french: car voici que tu vas (...) enfanter un fils
load_bearing.gloss: for behold, you are pregnant (hārâ, adjective) and about to bear a son
load_bearing.comment: v 3 has the verb wəhārîṯ 'you will conceive'; v 5 has the adjective hārâ 'pregnant' after hinnāḵ. The canon's '(...)' sits exactly on this word.

load_bearing.french: Le rasoir ne passera pas sur sa tête
load_bearing.gloss: and a razor shall not come up on his head
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.gloss: a nazirite (one set apart) of Elohim
load_bearing.comment: The canon prints 'Dieu' for ʾĕlōhîm here and 'Elohim' four lines later (TBWTT-3:82) for the same noun.

ellipsis.cut: (1) 'and eat nothing unclean' (v 4b); (2) the word 'pregnant/conceive' in v 5a; (3) 'and he shall begin to save Israel from the hand of the Philistines' (v 5b).
ellipsis.note: Cut (1) removes the ritual framing of the wine ban; cut (3) removes the stated purpose of the child.

items.french_variance: 'Dieu' (TBWTT-3:81) and 'Elohim' (TBWTT-3:82) for the same Hebrew noun within one quoted passage.
items.analysis: The uncut hair and the wine ban are Hebrew; the reasons the canon gives (antennas; a healthy experimental subject) replace the reason the Hebrew gives in the same clause, kî nəzîr ʾĕlōhîm — because he is a nazirite, a consecrated status that also explains the 'nothing unclean' rule the canon elides. One Hebrew detail is of interest to the canon's reading of the chapter and is hidden by its ellipsis: at the first visit the messenger already says hinnāḵ hārâ, formally 'you are pregnant'.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] hinnāḵ hārâ wəyōlaḏt can be parsed as present ('you are pregnant') or as imminent future; the library EN has 'you shall conceive'. The parse is the auditor's, not checked against a grammar.

items.ref_note: Quotation split across TBWTT-3:82–83.
items.canon_french: «(...) l'Ange d'Elohim vint encore vers la femme, alors

reading_quotes.french: son mari n'était pas avec elle
Vous imaginez facilement ce qui a pu se passer en l'absence du mari...
Le fait pour les créateurs de s'accoupler à une fille des hommes était magnifique.

items.reading_summary: The husband's absence at the second visit is the occasion of the conception of Samson by one of the creators.

load_bearing.french: l'Ange d'Elohim vint encore vers la femme
load_bearing.gloss: and the messenger of the Elohim came again to the woman
load_bearing.comment: Hebrew has the article (hāʾĕlōhîm); the verb + preposition is again bôʾ ʾel (see Judg 13:6; Gen 6:4).

load_bearing.french: son mari n'était pas avec elle
load_bearing.gloss: and Manoah her husband was not with her
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.gloss: and the Elohim listened to the voice of Manoah
load_bearing.comment: Cut by the opening '(...)': the second visit is the answer to the husband's own request (v 8) that the man come again.

load_bearing.gloss: and the woman hurried and ran and told her husband
load_bearing.comment: v 10 (not quoted): she immediately runs to fetch him.

load_bearing.gloss: and he came to the man
load_bearing.comment: v 11: the same bôʾ ʾel, of Manoah coming to the visitor — the everyday sense of the idiom.

ellipsis.cut: Opening '(...)': 'And the Elohim listened to the voice of Manoah'; middle '(...)': 'as she was sitting in the field'; middle '(...)': the name Manoah.
ellipsis.note: The cut removes the fact that the return visit was requested by the husband; the following verse, unquoted, has the woman run at once to bring him.

items.analysis: The clause the canon leans on — 'her husband was not with her' — is Hebrew, and bôʾ ʾel ('came to the woman') can carry a sexual sense. But the narrative the Hebrew builds around it points the other way: the visitor returns because the husband prayed for him to (vv 8–9a, elided), the woman's only action is to hurry off and fetch her husband (v 10), and v 11 uses the same bôʾ ʾel for Manoah approaching 'the man'. By v 5 the messenger has already said hinnāḵ hārâ, so the Hebrew does not place the conception at this second visit, where the canon puts it.

items.ref_note: No reference is given; Judges 16 is not in the library.
items.canon_french: Mais quand Dalila lui eut coupé les cheveux, il ne put plus appeler à l'aide.

reading_quotes.french: il retrouva sa «force», c'est-à-dire qu'il put appeler à l'aide les créateurs qui firent s'abattre le temple dont il touchait les colonnes

items.reading_summary: Samson's 'strength' was his ability to call the creators telepathically through his hair; they, not he, brought down the temple.

ellipsis.cut: Paraphrase; chapter not in library.

items.analysis: Judges 16 is not held in Hebrew in the library, so the wording behind 'force', the cutting of the hair and the collapse of the building cannot be compared.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] In Judg 16:28 Samson is usually read as calling on YHWH before pushing the pillars, which would be a textual hook for 'appeler à l'aide'; and in 16:19 it is a man, not Delilah herself, who is usually read as doing the shaving. Neither was checked.

items.canon_french: «Va te coucher et, si l'on t'appelle, tu diras : Parle, Iahvé, car ton serviteur écoute»

reading_quotes.french: vous avez une véritable initiation à la télépathie de Eli sur Samuel : les créateurs cherchent à entrer en rapport avec Samuel et ce dernier croit que c'est Eli qui lui parle. Il «entend des voix» :
Un peu comme des radio-amateurs dont l'un dirait : parlez, je vous entends cinq sur cinq.

items.reading_summary: Eli initiates Samuel into telepathy: the creators try to reach him and he takes the voice for Eli's.

load_bearing.gloss: if he calls to you
load_bearing.comment: Hebrew has a 3 m.sg. verb ('if he calls'); French 'on' is impersonal. qārāʾ is the ordinary verb for calling aloud.

load_bearing.french: Parle, Iahvé, car ton serviteur écoute
load_bearing.gloss: speak, YHWH, for your servant is listening
load_bearing.comment: Matches; šōmēaʿ is 'hearing/listening' (participle).

load_bearing.gloss: that YHWH was calling the boy
load_bearing.comment: v 8: Eli infers the caller's identity; the call is treated throughout as an audible summons Samuel answers by getting up and walking to Eli.

ellipsis.cut: Not quoted: 'And Eli said to Samuel' and 'So Samuel went and lay down in his place'.

items.analysis: The Hebrew vocabulary is that of ordinary speech and hearing (qārāʾ 'call', dibber 'speak', šāmaʿ 'hear'). That the voice is mistaken for a person in the next room is in the text; that it is received mentally rather than acoustically is not said in either language. 'Initiation' has a basis in Eli's coaching (vv 8–9).

items.ref_note: The quotation begins in TBWTT-3:90 («Samuel, Samuel !»).
items.canon_french: «(...) Parle, Iahvé, car ton serviteur écoute.»

reading_quotes.french: Et la conversation télépathique s'engage :
La télépathie comme moyen de communication entre les créateurs et les hommes n'était possible que quand les Elohim étaient à proximité de la Terre.

items.reading_summary: The telepathic conversation begins.

load_bearing.french: Parle, Iahvé, car ton serviteur écoute
load_bearing.gloss: speak, for your servant is listening
load_bearing.comment: In the Hebrew of v 10 Samuel does NOT say the name: he says only 'Speak'. The canon's French repeats 'Iahvé' from v 9.

load_bearing.gloss: Samuel, Samuel
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.gloss: and YHWH came and stationed himself (took his stand)
load_bearing.comment: Cut by the canon's '(...)': before calling, YHWH 'came and stood'.

ellipsis.cut: The '(...)' (with the paragraph break after TBWTT-3:90) removes 'And YHWH came and stood, and called as at the other times' and 'Then Samuel said'.
ellipsis.note: The removed clause describes a local, bodily arrival ('came and took his stand') immediately before the call.

items.french_variance: The canon's v 10 has 'Parle, Iahvé' where the MT has only 'Speak' (dabbēr); the divine name is carried over from v 9. Whether the insertion is Dhorme's or the canon's is not collated.
items.analysis: For a telepathic reading the Hebrew is less favourable than the excerpt: the elided words say that YHWH 'came and stationed himself' (wayyāḇōʾ … wayyiṯyaṣṣaḇ) and then called — a presence in the room, not a transmission. (The same clause is, by contrast, favourable to the canon's general picture of a bodily visitor.) The French also differs from the MT in a small way: Samuel's reply in v 10 omits the name YHWH, which the canon's quotation supplies.

items.canon_french: «Qui (...) insulte les troupes du Dieu vivant ?»

reading_quotes.french: Ce qui montre bien la réalité de la présence à cette époque d'un «Dieu» tout à fait palpable...

items.reading_summary: 'Living God' shows the reality, at that time, of a quite tangible 'God'.

load_bearing.gloss: battle-lines, ranks
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.gloss: living Elohim — ḥayyîm is a masculine PLURAL adjective agreeing with ʾĕlōhîm
load_bearing.comment: French 'Dieu vivant' is singular noun + singular adjective, and the canon prints 'Dieu', not 'Elohim'. The Hebrew phrase is one of the places where ʾĕlōhîm takes a plural modifier.

ellipsis.cut: The '(...)' removes 'is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should'; the first half of the verse (David's question about the reward) is not quoted.

items.french_variance: The canon prints 'Dieu' for ʾĕlōhîm here, against its own rule at TBWTT-2:5.
items.analysis: The reading rests on the adjective 'living', which is Hebrew (ḥayyîm). The original is more favourable to the canon's wider thesis than the French it quotes, on a point the canon does not notice: the adjective is plural (ʾĕlōhîm ḥayyîm), one of the minority of cases where Elohim is construed with a plural modifier, and the French singular 'Dieu vivant' erases it. (Core claim 0009 lists the parallel Deut 5:26 among the plural-adjective cases; this verse has the same phrase.) 'Palpable' is an inference from 'living'; the phrase is a fixed epithet.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] That ʾĕlōhîm ḥayyîm is a fixed epithet contrasted with lifeless idols is the common commentary view; not sourced here.

items.canon_french: leur idole, Dagon, gisait face contre terre devant l'arche de Iahvé, consécutivement à une décharge électrique occasionnée par une mauvaise manipulation

reading_quotes.french: ils installèrent un émetteur-récepteur qui était transporté dans l'»arche de Dieu», émetteur-récepteur qui possédait sa propre pile atomique

items.reading_summary: The ark carried a transmitter-receiver with its own atomic pile; Dagon's statue was thrown down by an electrical discharge caused by mishandling.

load_bearing.french: Dagon, gisait face contre terre devant l'arche de Iahvé
load_bearing.original: דָג֗וֹן נֹפֵ֤ל לְפָנָיו֙ אַ֔רְצָה לִפְנֵ֖י אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֑ה
load_bearing.translit: dāḡôn nōp̄ēl ləp̄ānāyw ʾarṣâ lip̄nê ʾărôn YHWH
load_bearing.gloss: Dagon fallen on his face to the ground before the ark of YHWH
load_bearing.comment: Matches (a paraphrase of the verse's wording).

load_bearing.gloss: and the Ashdodites rose early on the next day
load_bearing.comment: The statue is found fallen in the morning; no one is handling the ark when it falls.

load_bearing.original: וְרֹ֨אשׁ דָּג֜וֹן וּשְׁתֵּ֣י ׀ כַּפּ֣וֹת יָדָ֗יו כְּרֻתוֹת֙ אֶל־הַמִּפְתָּ֔ן
load_bearing.translit: wərōʾš dāḡôn ûšətê kappôṯ yāḏāyw kəruṯôṯ ʾel-hammip̄tān
load_bearing.gloss: and Dagon's head and both palms of his hands cut off, on the threshold
load_bearing.comment: The second fall: head and hands severed (kəruṯôṯ 'cut off') and lying at the threshold.

ellipsis.cut: Paraphrase of 5:1–5; the second fall with severed head and hands (v 4) is not mentioned.

items.analysis: The position of the statue is as the Hebrew gives it. The cause is unstated in the text; 'mauvaise manipulation' is contradicted in detail by it, since both falls are discovered at dawn after an unattended night, and the second leaves the head and hands 'cut off' at the threshold, a detail a discharge reading does not address. ʾărôn means 'chest, box' — a container — which is as far as the Hebrew goes toward 'apparatus'.

items.canon_french: «Il les affligea de bubons»

reading_quotes.french: D'autre part les radiations dangereuses des produits radio-actifs leur occasionnèrent des brûlures.

items.reading_summary: Radiation from the radioactive material in the ark burned the Philistines.

load_bearing.gloss: and he struck them with swellings (Ketiv ʿŏp̄ālîm 'swellings, mounds'; Qere ṭəḥōrîm 'tumours/haemorrhoids')
load_bearing.comment: 'Bubons' (buboes) is one identification of the swellings; the canon's English edition has 'emerods'. Hebrew verb is 'struck' (hikkâ), not 'afflicted'.

load_bearing.gloss: and the hand of YHWH was heavy on the Ashdodites
load_bearing.comment: Opening clause, not quoted.

ellipsis.cut: Only one clause of the verse is quoted, without ellipsis marks: 'the hand of YHWH was heavy on the Ashdodites and he devastated them' and 'Ashdod and its territory' are omitted.

items.french_variance: The reading ('brûlures') does not match the canon's own French ('bubons').
items.analysis: Hebrew, French and reading are three different things here: the Hebrew has 'swellings' (with a Ketiv/Qere alternation), the French 'bubons', the canon's commentary 'burns'. Neither the Hebrew nor the French says burns; the reading is not derived from the wording it quotes. The affliction is also not limited to those who handled the chest: it strikes 'Ashdod and its territory'.

items.canon_french: «ouzza étendit (la main) vers l'Arche de Dieu qu'il retint, parce que les bœufs se relâchaient. La colère de Iahvé s'enflamma contre ouzza et Dieu le frappa là pour cette erreur : il mourut là près de l'Arche de Dieu»

reading_quotes.french: L'arche avait failli se renverser et ouzza, essayant de la retenir, avait touché une partie dangereuse de l'appareil. Il avait été électrocuté.

items.reading_summary: The ark nearly tipped over; Uzzah, steadying it, touched a dangerous part of the apparatus and was electrocuted.

load_bearing.french: ouzza étendit (la main) vers l'Arche de Dieu qu'il retint
load_bearing.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח עֻזָּ֜א אֶל־אֲר֤וֹן הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ וַיֹּ֣אחֶז בּ֔וֹ
load_bearing.translit: wayyišlaḥ ʿuzzāʾ ʾel-ʾărôn hāʾĕlōhîm wayyōʾḥez bô
load_bearing.gloss: and Uzzah reached out to the chest of the Elohim and grasped it
load_bearing.comment: Matches; the bracketed '(la main)' correctly marks a word the Hebrew lacks. 'Dieu' renders hāʾĕlōhîm (with article).

load_bearing.french: parce que les bœufs se relâchaient
load_bearing.gloss: for the oxen let (it) drop / stumbled
load_bearing.comment: Matches in sense; supports 'avait failli se renverser'.

load_bearing.french: Dieu le frappa là pour cette erreur
load_bearing.gloss: and the Elohim struck him there for the šal (hapax; 'error'?)
load_bearing.comment: The agent is 'the Elohim' (article, singular verb). šal occurs only here; 'erreur' is the traditional guess.

load_bearing.french: il mourut là près de l'Arche de Dieu
load_bearing.gloss: and he died there, beside the chest of the Elohim
load_bearing.comment: Matches; 'there' twice — death on the spot.

ellipsis.cut: The verse-opening 'when they came to the threshing-floor of Nakhon' is not quoted.

items.french_variance: 'Dieu' three times for hāʾĕlōhîm, in a paragraph whose commentary says 'l'»arche de Dieu»'.
items.analysis: The physical sequence the reading uses is exactly the Hebrew's: the load shifts, a man grasps the chest, and he dies on the spot beside it (šām … šām). What the Hebrew adds, and the reading sets aside, is an agent and a motive: YHWH's anger, and 'the Elohim struck him'. The reason-word (šal) is a hapax of uncertain sense, so 'erreur' — which the canon turns into mishandling — is itself a conjectural rendering. No divergence between French and Hebrew apart from Dieu/hāʾĕlōhîm.

items.canon_french: «Il saisit les cornes de l'Autel»

reading_quotes.french: ce qui est la description de la manipulation des manettes de l'émetteur-récepteur pour essayer de rentrer en rapport avec les créateurs

items.reading_summary: Seizing the horns of the altar describes working the levers of the transmitter-receiver to try to contact the creators.

load_bearing.french: Il saisit les cornes de l'Autel
load_bearing.gloss: and he held fast to the horns of the altar
load_bearing.comment: ḥāzaq (Hiphil) is 'grip, hold on to' — holding, not operating. mizbēaḥ is 'place of slaughter/sacrifice' (root zbḥ).

load_bearing.gloss: and Adonijah was afraid because of Solomon
load_bearing.comment: The stated motive: fear of the king (asylum).

load_bearing.gloss: and Joab fled to the tent of YHWH
load_bearing.comment: Second instance: flight, again from Solomon.

ellipsis.cut: A generalised sentence, not a verse quotation.

items.analysis: Both verses give the action a stated cause — fear of Solomon and flight — and the verb is 'hold on to', which suits a suppliant clinging and not an operator at controls. The object is also the altar (mizbēaḥ), whereas the canon has just located the transmitter-receiver in the ark (ʾărôn, TBWTT-3:96); the two are different objects in the Hebrew and the reading moves the device from one to the other. 'Cornes' is literal (qarnôṯ).

items.canon_french: «Iahvé a dit qu'il réside dans un nuage. J'ai donc bâti vraiment une Maison pour ta demeure»

reading_quotes.french: Le grand roi Salomon fit construire sur la Terre une résidence somptueuse pour accueillir les créateurs quand ils venaient en visite.
Qu'il réside dans un nuage, c'est-à-dire dans un engin en orbite autour de la Terre, au-dessus des nuages...

items.reading_summary: Solomon built a sumptuous residence to receive the creators on their visits; 'dwelling in a cloud' means a craft in orbit above the clouds.

load_bearing.gloss: to dwell in the ʿărāp̄el — thick darkness, dark storm-cloud
load_bearing.comment: Not the ordinary word for cloud (ʿānān, used in vv 10–11). The canon's French has 'nuage' here and 'nuée' in v 10, so two French words track two Hebrew words, but 'nuage' loses the darkness.

load_bearing.original: בֵּ֥ית זְבֻ֖ל לָ֑ךְ מָכ֥וֹן לְשִׁבְתְּךָ֖ עוֹלָמִֽים׃
load_bearing.translit: bêṯ zəḇul lāḵ māḵôn ləšiḇtəḵā ʿôlāmîm
load_bearing.gloss: a house of zəḇul (exalted dwelling) for you, a fixed place for your sitting/dwelling for ever
load_bearing.comment: 'Demeure' is Hebrew-supported; ʿôlāmîm 'for ever' is not in the canon's French.

load_bearing.original: הַשָּׁמַ֜יִם וּשְׁמֵ֤י הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ לֹ֣א יְכַלְכְּל֔וּךָ אַ֕ף כִּֽי־הַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּ֖ה
