load_bearing.translit: haššāmayim ûšəmê haššāmayim lōʾ yəḵalkəlûḵā ʾap̄ kî-habbayiṯ hazzeh
load_bearing.gloss: the heavens and the heavens of the heavens cannot contain you; how much less this house
load_bearing.comment: Same speech, v 27 (not quoted): Solomon denies that the house can literally hold its occupant.

ellipsis.cut: Not marked: 'Then Solomon said' is dropped and the two verses are run together; 'a place for you to dwell in for ever' is shortened to 'pour ta demeure'.
ellipsis.note: Dropping ʿôlāmîm lets the canon speak of occasional visits ('quand ils venaient en visite'); the Hebrew speaks of a permanent seat.

items.french_variance: 'nuage' (8:12, ʿărāp̄el) vs 'nuée' (8:10, ʿānān) — the canon's French is consistent with a source that distinguishes the two Hebrew nouns.
items.analysis: The 'residence' half of the reading is solidly Hebrew (liškōn, ləšiḇtəḵā, bêṯ). The 'cloud = orbiting craft above the clouds' half depends on French 'nuage': the Hebrew word is ʿărāp̄el, the dense darkness of the Sinai theophany, not the common noun for cloud, so the gloss 'au-dessus des nuages' plays on a word the original does not use. The Hebrew also says the house is for dwelling 'for ever', against 'visits', and in the same prayer (v 27, unquoted) Solomon says no house can contain the one addressed.

items.ref_note: The two verses are quoted in reverse order.
items.canon_french: «La gloire de Iahvé avait rempli la maison de Iahvé». (I Rois, VIII-11) «La nuée remplit la maison de Iahvé».

reading_quotes.french: Qu'il réside dans un nuage, c'est-à-dire dans un engin en orbite autour de la Terre, au-dessus des nuages... mais allez donc faire comprendre cela à des primitifs.
Vous avez là la description de la «gloire», l'engin volant en réalité, des créateurs

items.reading_summary: Cloud and glory in the Temple are read with the 'cloud = craft' and 'glory = craft' equations.

load_bearing.french: La gloire de Iahvé avait rempli la maison de Iahvé
load_bearing.gloss: the kāḇôḏ of YHWH filled the house of YHWH
load_bearing.comment: Matches. The kāḇôḏ fills the interior of a building.

load_bearing.french: La nuée remplit la maison de Iahvé
load_bearing.gloss: and the cloud filled the house of YHWH
load_bearing.comment: Matches; ʿānān, the ordinary word for cloud.

load_bearing.original: וְלֹֽא־יָכְל֧וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֛ים לַעֲמֹ֥ד לְשָׁרֵ֖ת מִפְּנֵ֥י הֶֽעָנָ֑ן
load_bearing.translit: wəlōʾ-yāḵəlû hakkōhănîm laʿămōḏ ləšārēṯ mippənê heʿānān
load_bearing.gloss: and the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud
load_bearing.comment: Not quoted: the cloud is inside, among the priests, and v 11 gives 'the kāḇôḏ filled the house' as the explanation (kî) of the cloud.

ellipsis.cut: 8:10a ('when the priests came out of the holy place') and 8:11a ('the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for') are not quoted; no ellipsis marks.
ellipsis.note: The omitted clauses place the cloud inside the building and equate it with the kāḇôḏ.

items.analysis: The French is exact for both clauses. The difficulty is for the canon's own equations: at TBWTT-3:33 'gloire' is the flying craft and at 3:107 the cloud is a craft in orbit above the clouds, but in these verses both kāḇôḏ and ʿānān 'fill the house' — they are inside a building, at floor level, driving the priests out. The Hebrew makes that explicit in the half-verses the canon leaves out. The reading is thus an addition which the surrounding Hebrew resists.

items.ref_note: Quoted after 8:10–13, out of order.
items.canon_french: «J'y résiderai au milieu des fils d'Israël»

reading_quotes.french: une résidence somptueuse pour accueillir les créateurs

items.reading_summary: The Temple as the creators' residence among Israel.

load_bearing.french: J'y résiderai au milieu des fils d'Israël
load_bearing.gloss: and I will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel
load_bearing.comment: The Hebrew has no 'y' (there/in it): the dwelling is 'in the midst of the children of Israel', not explicitly 'in the house'. Singular 'I'.

ellipsis.cut: Not quoted: the conditional of v 12 ('if you walk in my statutes …') on which the promise depends, and 'and I will not forsake my people Israel'.
ellipsis.note: The promise is conditional in the Hebrew; the condition is in the preceding verse.

items.french_variance: The adverbial 'y' has no counterpart in the MT; not collated against Dhorme.
items.analysis: šāḵan 'dwell' is the verb of the miškān (Exod 25:8) and supports 'résider' fully. The one French-side feature is 'J'y': it ties the dwelling to the building, whereas the Hebrew says only 'among the children of Israel'. The canon's plural 'les créateurs' corresponds to a first-person singular in the Hebrew.

items.canon_french: «(...) par ordre de Iahvé, un homme de Dieu arriva de Juda à Béthel (...) il dit (...) voici que l'autel va se fendre (...) Jéroboam étendit sa main (...) en disant : «Saisissez-le !» mais la main qu'il avait étendue (...) se dessécha et il ne put la ramener à lui, l'autel se fendit (...)»

reading_quotes.french: Grâce à un désintégrateur atomique, un des créateurs détruit l'autel et brûle la main d'un des hommes qui ne respectaient pas les créateurs.

items.reading_summary: One of the creators destroys the altar with an atomic disintegrator and burns the hand of a man who did not respect the creators.

load_bearing.french: un homme de Dieu arriva de Juda à Béthel
load_bearing.gloss: a man of Elohim came from Judah
load_bearing.comment: ʾîš ʾĕlōhîm is the title of a human prophet; he comes 'from Judah'. The canon prints 'Dieu' for ʾĕlōhîm.

load_bearing.gloss: by the word of YHWH
load_bearing.comment: He acts under orders — an envoy, not the principal.

load_bearing.gloss: the altar is (about to be) torn
load_bearing.comment: qāraʿ is 'tear' (normally of cloth); 'se fendre' (split) is fair.

load_bearing.gloss: and his hand dried up / withered
load_bearing.comment: 'Dry up, wither' — not 'burn'; the reading's 'brûle la main' departs from Hebrew and French alike.

load_bearing.gloss: this is the sign that YHWH has spoken
load_bearing.comment: Cut: the splitting is announced beforehand as a sign (môp̄ēṯ).

load_bearing.gloss: and the king's hand returned to him and became as at first
load_bearing.comment: v 6 (not quoted): the hand is restored at once when the man of God intercedes.

load_bearing.gloss: and a lion met him on the way and killed him
load_bearing.comment: v 24: the 'man of Elohim' is killed by a lion later in the same chapter.

ellipsis.cut: Seven '(...)': Jeroboam standing at the altar to burn incense; the oracle about Josiah (v 2); the announcement 'this is the sign which YHWH has spoken' and the spilling of the ashes (vv 3, 5); 'when the king heard the word of the man of God … from the altar' (v 4); 'according to the sign … by the word of YHWH' (v 5).
ellipsis.note: The cuts remove the oracle the episode exists to authenticate and the labelling of the splitting as a pre-announced sign.

items.french_variance: 'homme de Dieu' for ʾîš ʾĕlōhîm (Elohim not preserved).
items.analysis: The canon identifies the actor as 'un des créateurs'. The Hebrew calls him ʾîš ʾĕlōhîm, 'a man of Elohim' — the standing title of a human prophet, which the canon itself accepts for Elijah three paragraphs later — who comes from Judah under orders (biḏḇar YHWH), is invited to dinner by the king, and is killed by a lion in v 24. The effects are 'torn' (altar) and 'dried up' (hand, restored in v 6); neither Hebrew nor French says 'burned', and no instrument is mentioned.

items.ref_note: The closing guillemet falls mid-sentence, leaving 'par où tu seras allé' and v 10a outside the quotation marks.
items.canon_french: «Tu ne reviendras pas par le chemin» par où tu seras allé. (...) Il s'en alla donc par un autre chemin.

reading_quotes.french: Il repart vers l'un des camps terrestres des Elohim par un chemin différent afin que les hommes ne puissent les découvrir :

items.reading_summary: He leaves for one of the Elohim's terrestrial camps by a different road so that men cannot discover them.

load_bearing.french: Tu ne reviendras pas par le chemin» par où tu seras allé
load_bearing.gloss: and you shall not return by the way that you went
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.french: Il s'en alla donc par un autre chemin
load_bearing.gloss: and he went by another way
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.gloss: you shall not eat bread and you shall not drink water
load_bearing.comment: Not quoted: the route rule is the third of three prohibitions, the first two about food and drink.

ellipsis.cut: Not quoted: 'for so I was commanded by the word of YHWH: you shall eat no bread nor drink water'; the '(...)' covers the verse boundary; v 10b 'and did not return by the way he came to Bethel' is dropped.
ellipsis.note: The route rule is detached from the fasting rules it belongs with.

items.analysis: The prohibition and its execution are quoted accurately. The text gives no reason for it and no destination; 'camp terrestre des Elohim' and concealment are additions. In the Hebrew the rule is one of a set of three (no bread, no water, no return by the same road) laid on the prophet himself.

items.stated_reference: I Rois, XVII-6 (prose reference in TBWTT-3:111)
items.canon_french: «Et les corbeaux lui apportaient du pain et de la viande le matin (...) et (...) le soir»

reading_quotes.french: Un exemple de téléguidage des animaux par électrode
comme cette façon de ravitailler Elie par des «corbeaux voyageurs»

items.reading_summary: Remote guidance of animals by electrode: Elijah is supplied by 'carrier ravens'.

load_bearing.french: les corbeaux lui apportaient du pain et de la viande
load_bearing.gloss: and the ravens were bringing him bread and meat
load_bearing.comment: Matches (participle: a repeated delivery).

load_bearing.gloss: and the ravens I have commanded to feed you there
load_bearing.comment: v 4 (not quoted): YHWH says he has 'commanded' the ravens — the textual statement of directed animal behaviour.

ellipsis.cut: The two '(...)' remove the repetition 'bread and meat' in the evening clause; 'and he drank from the brook' is dropped.

items.analysis: Birds delivering food twice daily is the plain Hebrew. The element of external control that the canon's 'téléguidage' needs is not in the verse it quotes but is in v 4, which it does not: ṣiwwîṯî 'I have commanded the ravens to feed you there'. 'Par électrode' is an addition. (The library note records that the reading takes the MT's 'ravens' at face value.)

items.canon_french: «Vois ! Ton fils est vivant»

reading_quotes.french: Elie avait soigné et guéri un jeune enfant mourant.

items.reading_summary: Elijah had treated and cured a dying child (a 'miracle' = scientific means not understood at the time).

load_bearing.gloss: see, your son lives
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.gloss: until no breath was left in him
load_bearing.comment: The Hebrew describes the illness worsening 'until no breath remained in him' — it does not use the verb 'die' in v 17.

load_bearing.gloss: and the nep̄eš (breath/life) of the child returned into him, and he lived
load_bearing.comment: v 22: the cure is described as the return of nep̄eš after Elijah calls to YHWH.

ellipsis.cut: Only the last four words of the verse are quoted.

items.analysis: The canon says 'mourant' (dying), not dead. The Hebrew of v 17 in fact stops short of saying the child died: his sickness grew severe 'until no breath was left in him', and v 22 has his nep̄eš 'return'. That wording is at least as compatible with a resuscitation reading as with a resurrection, and it is not in the excerpt the canon prints. (The mother's words in v 18, and the library note at 2 Kgs 4:32, take the boy as dead.) The means — Elijah stretching himself on the child three times and calling on YHWH (v 21) — are not quoted.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] Whether 1 Kgs 17:17 describes death or cessation of breathing short of death is debated in commentaries; none was consulted.

items.ref_note: The book number is missing ('Rois' for 'I Rois').
items.canon_french: «A présent je sais que tu es un homme de Dieu (...)»

reading_quotes.french: au moment convenu à l'avance entre Elie et les créateurs, le bûcher qui leur était destiné s'alluma, même inondé, grâce à un puissant rayon se rapprochant du laser et émis d'un vaisseau caché dans les nuages

items.reading_summary: Carmel: at a moment agreed in advance between Elijah and the creators, their pyre was lit, though soaked, by a powerful laser-like beam from a vessel hidden in the clouds.

load_bearing.french: tu es un homme de Dieu
load_bearing.gloss: you are a man of Elohim
load_bearing.comment: 'Dieu' for ʾĕlōhîm; here the canon accepts the title as that of a human.

load_bearing.gloss: and it came to pass at the (time of the) offering-up of the minḥâ
load_bearing.comment: The fire comes at a fixed, publicly known hour (the regular afternoon offering) — a real textual peg for 'a moment agreed in advance'.

load_bearing.gloss: behold, a small cloud like a man's palm rising from the sea
load_bearing.comment: After the fire, Elijah's servant looks seven times before a first small cloud appears: the narrative presupposes a cloudless sky during the contest.

ellipsis.cut: The '(...)' removes 'and that the word of YHWH in your mouth is truth'.

items.french_variance: 'Dieu' for ʾĕlōhîm.
items.analysis: The Carmel paraphrase has one Hebrew-supported peg — the fire falls at a set hour (baʿălôṯ hamminḥâ, 18:36) — and one detail the Hebrew works against: 'hidden in the clouds'. The story is set at the end of a three-year drought, and only after the fire does a servant, on the seventh look, report a first cloud 'like a man's palm' (18:44). The 'laser' is an addition (see the next item for the fire itself).

items.canon_french: «Et le feu de Iahvé tomba, il dévora l'holocauste et le bois, les pierres et la poussière, puis il lampa l'eau qui était dans la rigole»

reading_quotes.french: grâce à un puissant rayon se rapprochant du laser et émis d'un vaisseau caché dans les nuages

items.reading_summary: The 'fire of YHWH' was a laser-like beam fired from a hidden vessel.

load_bearing.gloss: and the fire of YHWH fell
load_bearing.comment: nāp̄al 'fall': the fire comes down from above. Matches.

load_bearing.gloss: and the stones and the dust/soil
load_bearing.comment: The fire consumes stone and earth as well as wood and flesh — more than a wood fire does.

load_bearing.gloss: and the water that was in the trench it licked up
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

items.analysis: The Hebrew describes a fire that falls from above (wattippōl) and consumes offering, wood, stones, soil and water. Directionality and intensity — the two things a beam reading needs — are in the wording, identically in French and Hebrew. The source ('vaisseau') and nature ('laser') of the fire are additions; the text names it only as ʾēš-YHWH.

items.canon_french: «(...) un Ange le toucha et lui dit «Lève-toi, mange !». (...) à son chevet il y avait une galette (...) et une jarre d'eau.»

reading_quotes.french: Elie fut l'objet de soins empressés de la part des créateurs.
Ceci se passe en plein désert...

items.reading_summary: The creators looked after Elijah attentively, feeding him in the middle of the desert.

load_bearing.gloss: a messenger touching him
load_bearing.comment: Physical contact (nāḡaʿ 'touch'); malʾāḵ is also the word for the human messenger Jezebel sends in 19:2.

load_bearing.gloss: a cake (baked on) hot stones/coals
load_bearing.comment: The canon's '(...)' removes rəṣāp̄îm: the cake is freshly baked on coals.

load_bearing.gloss: and a flask of water
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

ellipsis.cut: Cuts: 'he lay down and slept under a broom tree'; 'he looked, and behold'; 'baked on hot stones'; 'and he ate and drank and lay down again'.

items.analysis: A messenger who touches the sleeper and leaves bread and water is exactly what the Hebrew says; the reading adds only the identification of the messenger. 'Ange' is the French convention for malʾāḵ, the same noun used three verses earlier for a human courier.

items.canon_french: «Et voici que Iahvé passe. Un vent très fort secoue les montagnes et brise les rochers par devant Iahvé ; mais Iahvé n'est pas dans le vent. Et après le vent, un tremblement de terre (...) Et après le tremblement de terre, un feu ; mais Iahvé n'est pas dans le feu. Et après le feu, le son d'une brise légère»

reading_quotes.french: Vous avez là, la description exacte de l'atterrissage d'un engin comparable à vos fusées actuelles.

items.reading_summary: An exact description of the landing of a craft comparable to present-day rockets.

load_bearing.gloss: YHWH is passing by
load_bearing.comment: Matches (participle).

load_bearing.french: Un vent très fort secoue les montagnes et brise les rochers
load_bearing.original: וְר֣וּחַ גְּדוֹלָ֡ה וְחָזָ֞ק מְפָרֵק֩ הָרִ֨ים וּמְשַׁבֵּ֤ר סְלָעִים֙
load_bearing.translit: wərûaḥ gəḏôlâ wəḥāzāq məp̄ārēq hārîm ûməšabbēr səlāʿîm
load_bearing.gloss: and a great and strong wind tearing apart mountains and shattering rocks
load_bearing.comment: Hebrew məp̄ārēq 'tearing apart' is stronger than 'secoue' (shakes).

load_bearing.gloss: quaking, shaking, rumbling
load_bearing.comment: raʿaš is 'shaking/commotion' and also 'rumbling noise'; 'de terre' is supplied.

load_bearing.gloss: a sound of thin stillness/silence
load_bearing.comment: Dhorme's 'brise légère' follows the LXX; the Hebrew dəmāmâ is 'stillness, silence'.

ellipsis.cut: Opening: 'Go out and stand on the mountain before YHWH' is not quoted; the '(...)' removes 'but YHWH was not in the earthquake'.
ellipsis.note: One of the three parallel denials is dropped; the other two are kept.

items.french_variance: 'le son d'une brise légère' is identified in the library note as Dhorme's rendering, with LXX support, against the MT's lexical sense.
items.analysis: The sequence the reading uses — a passing presence preceded by rock-breaking wind, then shaking, then fire, then quiet — is Hebrew. On two words the Hebrew fits a landing sequence somewhat better than the French: raʿaš is general 'shaking/rumbling' (not specifically an earthquake), and the final term is qôl dəmāmâ ḏaqqâ, 'a sound of thin silence', i.e. stillness after the noise, where the French (after the LXX) has a light breeze. Against 'exact description': the text three times denies that YHWH is 'in' the wind, shaking or fire, and names no object that lands.

items.canon_french: «J'ai vu Iahvé siégeant sur son trône et toute l'armée des cieux se tenant près de lui (...)»

reading_quotes.french: Plus loin, il décrit la vision des créateurs.

items.reading_summary: A vision of the creators (plural): YHWH enthroned with the whole army of the skies around him.

load_bearing.gloss: YHWH sitting on his seat/throne
load_bearing.comment: Matches; kissēʾ is 'seat, chair, throne'.

load_bearing.gloss: and all the army of the skies
load_bearing.comment: ṣāḇāʾ is the ordinary word for an army (as in Josh 5:14); 'armée' is literal.

load_bearing.gloss: standing over/beside him
load_bearing.comment: Singular participle agreeing with the collective ṣāḇāʾ.

ellipsis.cut: The '(...)' removes 'on his right hand and on his left'; the opening 'Therefore hear the word of YHWH' is not quoted. The canon's 'il' has no antecedent: the speaker is Micaiah, not Elijah.
ellipsis.note: The preceding paragraphs are about Elijah, so 'il décrit' misattributes the vision by context.

items.analysis: A plurality of beings around a presiding, seated YHWH is the Hebrew's own picture, in military vocabulary (ṣəḇāʾ haššāmayim), and the French is literal. This is one of the passages where the canon's plural 'créateurs' does correspond to a plural entity in the text, though as a collective noun distinct from YHWH and not as a plural verb with Elohim. By position the canon's 'il' reads as Elijah; the speaker in the Hebrew is Micaiah son of Imlah (1 Kgs 22:8ff.).

items.canon_french: «(...) je deviendrai un esprit de mensonge dans la bouche de tous ses prophètes»

reading_quotes.french: Les créateurs font encore usage de la télépathie, mais d'une télépathie de groupe, pour qu'aucun des prophètes ne prédise la vérité au roi.

items.reading_summary: The creators used group telepathy so that none of the prophets would tell the king the truth.

load_bearing.gloss: a rûaḥ (breath, wind, spirit) of falsehood
load_bearing.comment: French 'esprit' selects one sense of rûaḥ.

load_bearing.french: dans la bouche de tous ses prophètes
load_bearing.gloss: in the mouth of all his prophets
load_bearing.comment: Matches: one influence acting on a whole group at once — the hook for 'de groupe'. The locus is the mouth (speech), not the mind.

load_bearing.gloss: and the rûaḥ came forward and stood before YHWH
load_bearing.comment: v 21 (not quoted): 'the rûaḥ' (with article) is a member of the assembly who steps forward, stands and speaks.

ellipsis.cut: The '(...)' removes 'And he said: I will go forth'; YHWH's reply ('you shall entice him and prevail; go and do so') is not quoted.

items.analysis: The Hebrew has a volunteer from the council, called 'the rûaḥ', who undertakes to become a rûaḥ of falsehood in the mouths of all the king's prophets simultaneously. A single agent producing the same false speech in many people is textual; 'telepathy' as the means is an addition, and the Hebrew locates the effect in the mouth. The plural 'les créateurs' matches the council setting (v 19–21), where the plan is deliberated among several speakers.

items.stated_reference: II Rois, I-12 (prose reference in TBWTT-3:125)
items.ref_note: The wording 'le feu de Dieu' fits v 12 (ʾēš-ʾĕlōhîm), not the first occurrence in v 10 (ʾēš).
items.canon_french: «Si je suis un homme de Dieu, que le feu descende des cieux et qu'il te dévore, toi et tes cinquante hommes» et le feu de Dieu descendit des cieux ; il le dévora, lui et ses cinquante hommes»

reading_quotes.french: vous avez encore la preuve de la protection que les créateurs accordent à Elie

items.reading_summary: Proof of the protection the creators gave Elijah.

load_bearing.gloss: a man of the Elohim (with article)
load_bearing.comment: 'Dieu' for hāʾĕlōhîm.

load_bearing.french: le feu de Dieu descendit des cieux
load_bearing.gloss: and fire of Elohim came down from the skies
load_bearing.comment: 'Dieu' for ʾĕlōhîm. The Hebrew has 'fire of Elohim … from the skies'; v 10 has plain 'fire'.

items.french_variance: 'Dieu' twice for (hā)ʾĕlōhîm in a quotation, where the canon's stated principle (TBWTT-2:5) would require 'Elohim'.
items.analysis: Fire descending from the sky on request, on Elijah's behalf, is the Hebrew as quoted. On the canon's own terms the Hebrew is the stronger text: it reads ʾēš-ʾĕlōhîm, 'fire of Elohim', and ʾîš hāʾĕlōhîm, 'man of the Elohim', where the French the canon prints has 'Dieu' both times.

items.canon_french: «(...) l'Ange de Iahvé dit à Elie : «Descends avec lui, ne crains rien de sa part !»

reading_quotes.french: Cette opération se reproduisit encore mais la troisième fois :

items.reading_summary: No separate technological reading; continues the protection of Elijah.

load_bearing.french: l'Ange de Iahvé dit à Elie
load_bearing.gloss: and the messenger of YHWH spoke to Elijah
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

ellipsis.cut: Drops 'and he arose and went down with him to the king'.

items.analysis: Quoted as narrative continuation; nothing depends on the wording.

items.ref_note: Reference printed in TBWTT-3:131.
items.canon_french: «Quand Iahvé fit monter Elie aux cieux dans un tourbillon

reading_quotes.french: Elie est l'invité des créateurs dans un vaisseau spatial qui décolle et l'emmène

items.reading_summary: Elijah is the creators' guest in a spaceship that takes off and carries him away.

load_bearing.gloss: when YHWH caused Elijah to go up
load_bearing.comment: Causative (Hiphil) of 'go up': Elijah is taken up by an agent.

load_bearing.gloss: in the storm-wind, to the skies
load_bearing.comment: səʿārâ is 'storm, tempest'; the Hebrew has the definite article ('the storm'), French 'un tourbillon'.

ellipsis.cut: The canon's '(...)' removes 'that Elijah and Elisha went from Gilgal'.

items.analysis: A bodily ascent to the sky, caused by another party, in a violent wind, is the Hebrew. No vessel is named in this verse; 'vaisseau spatial' comes from the canon's reading of v 11. The article on səʿārâ ('the storm', as something known) is lost in 'un tourbillon'.

items.canon_french: «(...) voici qu'un char de feu et des chevaux de feu s'interposèrent entre eux deux (entre Elie et Elisée) : Elie monta aux cieux dans le tourbillon»

reading_quotes.french: C'est le décollage d'un engin volant et le feu des tuyères fait que le narrateur parle de chevaux de feu.

items.reading_summary: The take-off of a flying craft; the nozzle flames make the narrator speak of horses of fire.

load_bearing.gloss: a chariot (or chariotry; from rkb 'ride') of fire
load_bearing.comment: reḵeḇ is the general word for a ridden vehicle and is often collective; 'char' is its normal rendering.

load_bearing.gloss: and horses of fire
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.gloss: and they separated the two of them
load_bearing.comment: The chariot and horses separate the two men; the bracketed gloss '(entre Elie et Elisée)' is the canon's.

load_bearing.french: Elie monta aux cieux dans le tourbillon
load_bearing.gloss: and Elijah went up in the storm-wind to the skies
load_bearing.comment: The ascent is 'in the storm', not explicitly in the chariot — in Hebrew and French alike.

ellipsis.cut: The '(...)' removes 'as they were still going on and talking'.

items.analysis: A fiery vehicle (reḵeḇ-ʾēš), fiery draught animals, and an ascent to the sky in a tempest are the Hebrew's own terms, rendered literally. The identification with a craft is the canon's, but it is an interpretation of vocabulary that is itself vehicular. One precision that holds in both languages: the text has the chariot separate the two men and has Elijah go up 'in the storm', so that boarding the vehicle is inferred, not stated.

items.canon_french: Elisée, comme son père, procède à une «résurrection». Il soigne et ramène à la vie un enfant mort.

reading_quotes.french: où l'on fait le bouche à bouche et les massages du cœur régulièrement pour ramener à la vie un être dont le muscle cardiaque s'est arrêté

items.reading_summary: Elisha's 'resurrection' of a dead child is comparable to mouth-to-mouth resuscitation and heart massage.

load_bearing.gloss: and he put his mouth on his mouth
load_bearing.comment: The Hebrew literally describes mouth placed on mouth.

load_bearing.gloss: and he crouched/bent over him, and the child's flesh grew warm
load_bearing.comment: gāhar 'crouch, bend over' — body pressed on body, repeated in v 35; warming is the first sign.

load_bearing.gloss: and behold, the boy was dead
load_bearing.comment: Here the Hebrew says 'dead' outright (contrast 1 Kgs 17:17).

load_bearing.gloss: my father, my father
load_bearing.comment: Elisha addresses Elijah as 'my father' (2 Kgs 2:12); he is his disciple, not his son. The canon's 'son père' takes the address literally or loosely.

load_bearing.gloss: and he prayed to YHWH
load_bearing.comment: Not mentioned by the canon.

load_bearing.gloss: and the boy sneezed (hapax) seven times
load_bearing.comment: The revival is marked by a respiratory reflex.

ellipsis.cut: No quotation.

items.analysis: This is the canon's best-supported medical reading in the slice: the Hebrew itself narrates mouth on mouth, the adult's body bent over the child's, the flesh warming, and a sevenfold sneeze before the eyes open. The French 'bouche à bouche' is the literal content of wayyāśem pîw ʿal-pîw. Unmentioned by the canon: the prayer (v 33) and the eyes-on-eyes, palms-on-palms contact, which is not a resuscitation gesture. 'Comme son père' is inaccurate as kinship.

items.canon_french: «Un homme (...) apporta à l'homme de Dieu (...) vingt pains d'orge (...). Mais son serviteur dit : «Comment serviraije cela à cent personnes ?» «on en mangera et il en restera». Il les servit, ils en mangèrent et laissèrent des restes, suivant la parole de Iahvé»

reading_quotes.french: Les créateurs apportent ici un aliment synthétique et déshydraté, qui, ajouté d'eau correspond à cinq fois plus de volume. Avec vingt petits «pains», il y a suffisamment de nourriture pour cent hommes.

items.reading_summary: The creators bring a synthetic dehydrated food which swells fivefold with water: twenty small 'loaves' feed a hundred men.

load_bearing.french: Un homme (...) apporta à l'homme de Dieu
load_bearing.original: וְאִ֨ישׁ בָּ֜א מִבַּ֣עַל שָׁלִ֗שָׁה וַיָּבֵא֩ לְאִ֨ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֜ים
load_bearing.translit: wəʾîš bāʾ mibbaʿal šālišâ wayyāḇēʾ ləʾîš hāʾĕlōhîm
load_bearing.gloss: and a man came from Baal-shalishah and brought to the man of the Elohim
load_bearing.comment: The bringer is 'a man' from a named village; the canon's first '(...)' removes the place-name, and its commentary makes 'les créateurs' the bringers.

load_bearing.gloss: bread of the first-fruits, twenty loaves of barley
load_bearing.comment: The canon's second '(...)' removes 'bread of the first-fruits': the loaves are the first of the new barley harvest.

load_bearing.gloss: and fresh ears of grain in his sack
load_bearing.comment: Removed by the third '(...)': fresh grain accompanies the loaves.

load_bearing.gloss: before a hundred men
load_bearing.comment: Matches; the 20:100 ratio the canon computes from is textual.

load_bearing.french: on en mangera et il en restera
load_bearing.gloss: eating and leaving over (infinitives absolute)
load_bearing.comment: Matches; a surplus is promised and (v 44) obtained.

ellipsis.cut: The three '(...)' in the first sentence remove: 'came from Baal-shalishah'; 'bread of the first-fruits'; 'and fresh ears of grain in his sack. And he said: Give to the people, that they may eat'. Also dropped: 'for thus says YHWH'.
ellipsis.note: The removed words identify the bringer as a villager and the food as first-fruits of the harvest.

items.french_variance: 'homme de Dieu' for ʾîš hāʾĕlōhîm.
items.analysis: The numbers (twenty loaves, a hundred men, a surplus) are Hebrew and the canon's arithmetic follows from them. Its account of what the food was and who brought it does not: the Hebrew says a man from Baal-shalishah brought leḥem bikkûrîm — first-fruits bread of barley — with fresh ears of grain in his sack. Each of those three identifying details falls inside one of the canon's ellipses. The text presents ordinary agricultural produce offered to a prophet, not a product delivered by the creators.

items.canon_french: «(...) et Israël fut déporté loin de son sol (...)»

reading_quotes.french: C'est là le début de la dispersion du peuple d'Israël
Mais le peuple d'Israël adora des idoles en métal, fut anthropophage et devint complètement immoral, dégoûtant ceux qui l'avaient créé.

items.reading_summary: The beginning of the dispersion of Israel, after idolatry, cannibalism and immorality disgusted its creators.

load_bearing.french: Israël fut déporté loin de son sol
load_bearing.gloss: and Israel went into exile from upon its soil
load_bearing.comment: Matches.

load_bearing.gloss: to Assyria
load_bearing.comment: Cut by the closing '(...)': the destination — a deportation of the northern kingdom to one place, not a general dispersion.

load_bearing.original: עַ֠ד אֲשֶׁר־הֵסִ֨יר יְהוָ֤ה אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵעַ֣ל פָּנָ֔יו
load_bearing.translit: ʿaḏ ʾăšer-hēsîr YHWH ʾeṯ-yiśrāʾēl mēʿal pānāyw
load_bearing.gloss: until YHWH removed Israel from before his face
load_bearing.comment: Cut by the opening '(...)': the Hebrew makes YHWH the agent of removal.

ellipsis.cut: Opening '(...)': 'until YHWH removed Israel from his sight, as he had spoken by all his servants the prophets'; closing '(...)': 'to Assyria, unto this day'.
ellipsis.note: 'To Assyria' narrows the event to the fall of the northern kingdom.

items.analysis: A historical reading and the Hebrew supports its core (exile as the consequence of the conduct listed in 2 Kgs 17:7–22). 'Anthropophage' has no counterpart in this verse; chapter 17's own charges are idolatry, divination and passing children through fire (vv 16–17), which the library holds but which were not individually checked for this item. 'Dispersion' generalises a deportation 'to Assyria'.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] The cannibalism motif may derive from 2 Kgs 6:28–29 (siege of Samaria); that chapter is not in the library and the link is a guess.

items.canon_french: «L’année de la mort du roi ozias, je vis Adonaï assis sur un trône élevé (...). Des séraphins se tenaient au-dessus de lui. Chacun avait six ailes, deux dont il couvrait sa face, deux dont il couvrait ses pieds et deux pour voler».

reading_quotes.french: la description des créateurs revêtus d’un scaphandre autonome muni de six petits réacteurs : deux dans le dos, deux aux mains et deux aux pieds, directionnels ceux-ci

items.reading_summary: The seraphim are creators in self-contained suits with six small jets: two on the back, two at the hands, two (steerable) at the feet.

load_bearing.gloss: plural noun from śrp "burn": "burning ones"
load_bearing.comment: The French transliterates and so hides the transparent Hebrew sense "burners"; the Hebrew noun itself carries the fire/combustion idea the jet reading wants.

load_bearing.gloss: six wings (dual form kənāp̄ayim)
load_bearing.comment: Number six is in the Hebrew.

load_bearing.french: deux dont il couvrait sa face, deux dont il couvrait ses pieds et deux pour voler
load_bearing.original: בִּשְׁתַּ֣יִם ׀ יְכַסֶּ֣ה פָנָ֗יו וּבִשְׁתַּ֛יִם יְכַסֶּ֥ה רַגְלָ֖יו וּבִשְׁתַּ֥יִם יְעוֹפֵֽף׃
load_bearing.translit: bištayim yəḵasseh p̄ānāyw ûḇištayim yəḵasseh raḡlāyw ûḇištayim yəʿôp̄ēp̄
load_bearing.gloss: with two he covers his face, with two he covers his feet, with two he flies
load_bearing.comment: French = Hebrew. The text distributes the pairs face / feet / flight; the canon redistributes them back / hands / feet.

load_bearing.gloss: standing above him
load_bearing.comment: Beings stationed above a seated figure: literal in both.

ellipsis.cut: v.1b "high and lifted up, and the hem of his robe filled the temple" (וְשׁוּלָיו מְלֵאִים אֶת־הַהֵיכָל): the temple setting and the robe.
ellipsis.note: The cut removes the temple (hêḵāl) location; the canon does not locate the scene.

items.analysis: The hooks that are in the Hebrew are the number six, flight (yəʿôp̄ēp̄) and position above. The placement of the six "reactors" (back, hands, feet) is not what either the French or the Hebrew says (face, feet, flying); only the feet pair coincides, and there the verb is "cover". The one point where the original is more favourable than the French is lexical: śərāp̄îm is a transparent derivative of śrp "to burn", which the transliteration "séraphins" conceals.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] śārap̄ "burn" as the root of śərāp̄îm and the link to the "fiery (śārāp̄) serpents" of Num 21:6-8 are standard lexicon statements, not taken from the library note for this verse.

items.canon_french: «Sur les montagnes, un bruit de tumulte ! Quelque chose comme un peuple nombreux ! Le bruit du vacarme des royaumes ! Les nations rassemblées ! Iahvé des armées passe en revue l’armée du combat. Ils viennent d’un pays lointain, des confins du ciel, Iahvé et les instruments de son courroux, pour détruire tout le pays».

reading_quotes.french: Toute la vérité est décrite ici. Il fallait lire entre les lignes et comprendre. «Ils viennent d’un pays lointain, des confins du ciel». on ne pouvait être plus clair.
L’armée des cieux est décrite ici à cette époque, au moment où elle vient, avec les instruments de son courroux, pour détruire tout le pays

items.reading_summary: The host that comes "from a far country, from the ends of heaven" is the creators' army arriving from their planet with its weapons to destroy Sodom and Gomorrah.

load_bearing.french: Ils viennent d’un pays lointain, des confins du ciel
load_bearing.gloss: coming from a land of distance, from the end of the skies
load_bearing.comment: French = Hebrew word for word, plural participle included. The same phrase miqṣēh haššāmayim is the sun's rising-point in Ps 19:7 (C-046), where the canon's French renders it differently ("à un bout des cieux").

load_bearing.gloss: the implements / vessels / weapons of his indignation
load_bearing.comment: kəlî is the general word for a made implement; "instruments" is a fair and non-inflated rendering.

load_bearing.french: Iahvé des armées passe en revue l’armée du combat
load_bearing.gloss: YHWH of hosts is mustering a host of war
load_bearing.comment: Literal in both.

ellipsis.cut: No marked ellipsis; the chapter heading 13:1 ("oracle concerning Babylon") and 13:17 ("I am stirring up the Medes") are outside the quotation.
ellipsis.note: Context, not ellipsis: the chapter itself names the target (Babylon) and the army (Medes).

items.analysis: The load-bearing sentence is literally in the Hebrew and Dhorme's French adds nothing: a plural host "coming from a distant land, from the end of the skies", with YHWH and "implements of his wrath". What the Hebrew context does not support is the identification: 13:1 heads the oracle "concerning Babylon" and 13:17 names the Medes, and miqṣēh haššāmayim is a horizon idiom (library note; the same phrase is the sun's starting point in Ps 19:7). One unquoted verse is favourable to the canon's Sodom link: 13:19 itself compares the coming overthrow to "Elohim's overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah" (כְּמַהְפֵּכַת אֱלֹהִים אֶת־סְדֹם וְאֶת־עֲמֹרָה), as a comparison, not an identification.

items.canon_french: «C’est toi qui disais dans ton cœur: je monterai aux cieux, au-dessus des étoiles de Dieu».

reading_quotes.french: Allusion aux savants disparus qui avaient acquis suffisamment de connaissances scientifiques pour entreprendre d’aller sur la planète des créateurs et furent détruits à Sodome et Gomorrhe
Ce sont les hommes de Sodome et Gomorrhe qui disaient

items.reading_summary: The boast is that of the human scientists of Sodom and Gomorrah who planned to travel to the creators' planet.

load_bearing.gloss: to the skies I will ascend
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

load_bearing.gloss: above the stars of El I will raise my throne
load_bearing.comment: In Hebrew "above the stars of El" modifies "I will raise my throne"; the canon's quotation drops the throne clause without an ellipsis mark, so the phrase attaches to "je monterai". The divine name is ʾēl, not ʾĕlōhîm.

load_bearing.french: C’est toi qui disais dans ton cœur
load_bearing.gloss: and you (m. sg.) said in your heart
load_bearing.comment: Second person singular in Hebrew and in the French; the canon's commentary makes the speakers plural ("les hommes de Sodome et Gomorrhe").

ellipsis.cut: Unmarked: "I will raise my throne" (אָרִים כִּסְאִי) and "I will sit on the mount of assembly, in the far reaches of Zaphon" (וְאֵשֵׁב בְּהַר־מוֹעֵד בְּיַרְכְּתֵי צָפוֹן).
ellipsis.note: The cut turns a throne-above-the-stars boast into a journey statement, and removes har-môʿēḏ "mount of assembly", a council image that the canon could have used.

items.analysis: The hook "I will ascend to the skies" is literally Hebrew. Three things are not: (a) the journey sense depends partly on the silent omission of "I will raise my throne", which is what "above the stars of El" modifies; (b) the addressee is one man, singular in Hebrew and French, whom 14:4 identifies as "the king of Babylon" (עַל־מֶלֶךְ בָּבֶל), whereas the canon makes the speakers the men of Sodom and Gomorrah; (c) the unquoted "mount of assembly" clause shows the aim is a seat in the divine assembly.

items.canon_french: «Je monterai sur les hauteurs de la Nuée, je m’égalerai au

reading_quotes.french: Mais la destruction a empêché l’homme de s’égaler aux créateurs, «au Très-Haut»

items.reading_summary: Humanity (the Sodom scientists) wanted to equal the creators, "the Most High"; the destruction prevented it.

load_bearing.gloss: the heights (lit. backs) of cloud
load_bearing.comment: The Hebrew noun is ʿāḇ "(dark) cloud, cloud-mass", not ʿānān, the word of the Exodus pillar and of Ezek 1:4. The French capitalised singular "la Nuée" makes it look like the same named object as the Exodus "nuée".

load_bearing.gloss: I will make myself like the Most High
load_bearing.comment: ʿelyôn is singular; the canon glosses it as plural "créateurs".

ellipsis.note: The quotation is split across two dump paragraphs (3:150-151); no cut.

items.french_variance: "Nuée" capitalised here; "nuée" lower-case at Ezek 1:4 (TBWTT-3:159) for a different Hebrew word.
items.analysis: The wish to be "like" (dmh) the Most High is the Hebrew text. Two details are French-side: the capitalised "la Nuée" suggests the craft-cloud of the Exodus quotations, but the Hebrew word here (ʿāḇ) differs from the Exodus/Ezekiel ʿānān; and ʿelyôn is a singular title which the commentary pluralises.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] That Dhorme printed "la Nuée" with a capital has not been checked against the Pléiade volume.

items.canon_french: «Il a mis le monde à l’état de désert (...)».

reading_quotes.french: Mais la destruction a empêché l’homme de s’égaler aux créateurs
L’explosion nucléaire est décrite plus loin

items.reading_summary: Quoted as the result of the destruction (Sodom and Gomorrah) that stopped the scientists: the world turned to desert, followed by "the nuclear explosion".

load_bearing.french: Il a mis le monde à l’état de désert
load_bearing.gloss: (who) made the world like a wilderness
load_bearing.comment: In Hebrew the participle/verb continues the onlookers' question of v.16, "Is this the man who shook the earth ... who made the world like a wilderness?": the subject is the fallen boaster, not his destroyer. Hebrew has a simile ("like a wilderness"); the French "à l'état de" makes it a resulting state.

ellipsis.cut: "and overthrew its cities, who did not let his prisoners go home" (וְעָרָיו הָרָס אֲסִירָיו לֹא־פָתַח בָּיְתָה).
ellipsis.note: The prisoners clause shows the subject is a conquering king.

items.analysis: As placed in the canon the sentence reads as what the destroying force did. In the Hebrew (and in any continuous translation of vv.16-17) the one who "made the world like a wilderness" is the man being taunted, the same person who said "I will ascend" in v.13: on the canon's own identification that would be the Sodom scientists, not the army from the sky. The quotation works only as an isolated clause with an unspecified "Il".

items.canon_french: «La clameur a encerclé le territoire de Moab, son écho va jusqu’à Eglaïm, son écho va jusqu’à Beër Eylim. Les eaux de Dimôn sont pleines de sang !».

reading_quotes.french: L’explosion nucléaire est décrite plus loin

items.reading_summary: A description of the nuclear explosion that destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.

load_bearing.french: La clameur a encerclé le territoire de Moab
load_bearing.gloss: the outcry has gone round the border of Moab
load_bearing.comment: zəʿāqāh is a human cry of distress; "son écho" renders yilәlāṯāh "its wailing" — a wail, not a blast.

load_bearing.gloss: her/its wailing
load_bearing.comment: "écho" is weaker and more acoustic than the Hebrew "howling"; the French makes a sound-propagation reading easier than the Hebrew does.

load_bearing.french: Les eaux de Dimôn sont pleines de sang
load_bearing.gloss: the waters of Dimon are full of blood
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

ellipsis.cut: Unmarked: v.9b "for I will bring yet more upon Dimon: a lion for those of Moab who escape" (כִּי־אָשִׁית עַל־דִּימוֹן נוֹסָפוֹת ... אַרְיֵה).
ellipsis.note: The continuation is a future threat with a lion; the chapter heading 15:1 is "oracle concerning Moab".

items.analysis: Nothing in the Hebrew wording describes an explosion: the verses report a cry and a wailing spreading through named Moabite towns and water full of blood, inside an oracle headed "Moab" (15:1). The French "écho" for "wailing" is slightly more event-like than the Hebrew. An unquoted verse offers a closer hook than the ones chosen: 15:1 says Ar and Kir of Moab were laid waste "in a night" (בְּלֵיל שֻׁדַּד).
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] Moab's territory lies east of the Dead Sea, the traditional region of Sodom; and Gen 19:37 makes Moab a descendant of Lot — neither is used by the canon here.

items.canon_french: «Va mon peuple, entre dans tes chambres et ferme tes deux battants sur toi ; cache-toi juste un instant, jusqu’à ce que le courroux soit passé».

reading_quotes.french: Certains furent pourtant sauvés en s’abritant dans des « blockhaus»

items.reading_summary: Some were saved from the (nuclear) destruction by sheltering in bunkers.

load_bearing.french: entre dans tes chambres et ferme tes deux battants sur toi
load_bearing.gloss: enter your inner rooms and shut your doors (ketiv plural/dual; qere singular "door")
load_bearing.comment: "tes deux battants" follows the ketiv (plural); ḥeḏer is an inner room.

load_bearing.french: cache-toi juste un instant, jusqu’à ce que le courroux soit passé
load_bearing.gloss: hide for a little moment
load_bearing.comment: Literal; the wrath-word zaʿam at the end of the verse is the same noun as in Isa 13:5 ("instruments de son courroux"), a real lexical link in Hebrew that the French preserves with "courroux" in both places.

ellipsis.note: Context: 26:19 (resurrection of the dead) precedes and 26:21 (YHWH comes out of his place to punish) follows; the verse is future and addressed to "my people".

items.analysis: The textual hook — take shelter indoors, shut the doors, hide briefly until the wrath has passed — is exactly the Hebrew; "blockhaus" is the canon's modernisation of ḥăḏārîm "inner rooms". The link to the Sodom event is supplied: the Hebrew is an imperative to "my people" about a coming judgement (26:21), not a report of a past one. The zaʿam link with 13:5 is in the Hebrew.

items.canon_french: «(...) une grande nuée avec un feu fulgurant et une clarté autour, tandis qu’au milieu il y avait comme le scintillement du vermeil (...). Et au milieu, la forme de quatre êtres dont l’aspect était le suivant : ils avaient une forme humaine. Chacun avait quatre faces et chacun avait quatre ailes. Quant à leurs jambes : la jambe était droite et la plante de leurs pieds était comme la plante de la patte du veau et brillait comme le scintillement de l’airain poli. […] Ils allaient là où l’esprit devait aller.

reading_quotes.french: La grande nuée, c’est la trace que laissent les avions à très haute altitude actuellement, apparaît ensuite l’engin et sa lampe clignotante, le «feu fulgurant» et le «scintillement du vermeil». Quatre créateurs évoluent ensuite avec des combinaisons antigravitationnelles et de petits réacteurs directionnels. Des «ailes» sur leurs scaphandres métalliques : «leurs jambes... brillaient comme le scintillement de l’airain poli»
Le scaphandre est également décrit avec ses quatre hublots comparables à ceux de vos premiers scaphandres marins

items.reading_summary: Great cloud = contrail; flashing fire and "vermeil" gleam = the craft and its flashing light; the four beings = four creators in metallic antigravity suits with small directional jets ("wings"); the four faces = four portholes of the helmet.

load_bearing.french: une grande nuée avec un feu fulgurant
load_bearing.gloss: a great cloud and fire taking hold of itself / flashing continually
load_bearing.comment: ʿānān is the Exodus pillar-word. miṯlaqqaḥaṯ (hitpael of lqḥ) is a self-catching, recurrent fire; "fulgurant" is adequate; the canon's "lampe clignotante" (intermittent) is closer to the Hebrew reflexive-iterative than to the French adjective.

load_bearing.gloss: like the eye/look of the ḥašmal
load_bearing.comment: ḥašmal is of uncertain meaning (library keeps it untranslated); "vermeil" (silver-gilt) is Dhorme's choice for a gleaming metal/amber. A metallic gleam is a possible, not a certain, sense.

load_bearing.gloss: a likeness of four living creatures (fem. pl. of ḥayyāh "living thing, animal")
load_bearing.comment: "êtres" is neutral where the Hebrew noun is the ordinary word for animals/living creatures; "êtres" is easier to read as "creators" than ḥayyôṯ is.

load_bearing.gloss: they had a likeness of a human
load_bearing.comment: Literal: the human form is the Hebrew text.

load_bearing.gloss: four faces to each
load_bearing.comment: pānîm "faces"; v.10 (quoted by the canon) specifies them as human, lion, ox and eagle faces, which the porthole reading does not account for.

load_bearing.french: brillait comme le scintillement de l’airain poli
load_bearing.gloss: and (they were) sparkling like the look of burnished bronze
load_bearing.comment: nōṣәṣîm is a masculine PLURAL participle: it cannot agree with the feminine singular kap̄ "sole" (French "brillait", singular) and is most naturally "they sparkled". The canon's own re-quotation at 3:163 has the plural "brillaient", which matches the Hebrew better than the verse as first quoted.

load_bearing.french: Ils allaient là où l’esprit devait aller
load_bearing.gloss: the rûaḥ (wind / spirit / breath) to go
load_bearing.comment: rûaḥ with article; French "l'esprit" selects one of three senses.

ellipsis.cut: First "(...)": v.4a "I looked, and behold, a stormy wind was coming from the north" (רוּחַ סְעָרָה בָּאָה מִן־הַצָּפוֹן). Second "(...)": v.4 end "from the middle of the fire" (מִתּוֹךְ הָאֵשׁ). Chapter frame 1:1 "the skies were opened and I saw visions of Elohim" (מַרְאוֹת אֱלֹהִים) is outside the quotation.
ellipsis.note: The storm-wind from the north and the vision frame are removed; the first changes the meteorological setting of the "cloud", the second the genre.

items.french_variance: TBWTT-3:159 "la plante de leurs pieds ... brillait" (sg.) vs the re-quotation at TBWTT-3:163 "leurs jambes... brillaient" (pl., with the calf's-hoof clause dropped).
items.analysis: Several hooks are original and Dhorme is close: a great cloud with self-renewing fire and a ḥašmal-gleam at its centre, four figures of human likeness, gleam "like burnished bronze", wings, hands under the wings, movement without turning. Against the reading in the Hebrew: the figures are ḥayyôṯ ("living creatures/animals"), each with lion, ox and eagle faces (v.10) and a calf's hoof (v.7), details the canon quotes but does not interpret; the opening storm-wind is cut; and the whole is framed as "visions of Elohim" (1:1). One point favours the canon against its own French: nōṣәṣîm is plural, so "they gleamed" (the figures or their legs) rather than "the sole gleamed".
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] The grammatical analysis of nōṣәṣîm (masc. pl. participle not agreeing with feminine kap̄/regel) is my own parsing of the library text, not from a library note.
[outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] Dhorme's exact wording for this passage has not been collated; "êtres"/"vermeil" are assumed to be his.

items.canon_french: «Je regardai alors les êtres et voici qu’il y avait une roue à terre, à côté des quatre êtres».

reading_quotes.french: Quand à la «soucoupe volante», la «roue», leur aspect et leur fonctionnement ne sont pas trop mal décrits sachant que c’est un primitif qui parle

items.reading_summary: The "wheel" on the ground beside the beings is a flying saucer.

load_bearing.gloss: one wheel on the earth/ground
load_bearing.comment: ʾôp̄an is the ordinary word for a (chariot) wheel; "one" is explicit in Hebrew.

load_bearing.gloss: beside the living creatures, for its/his four faces
load_bearing.comment: Hebrew "for each of its four faces" (one wheel per face/creature); the French smooths this to "the four beings".

items.analysis: A separate disc-shaped object resting "on the earth" beside the figures is what the Hebrew says (ʾôp̄an "wheel", bāʾāreṣ). The French follows it closely. The identification with a craft is the canon's; in Ezek 10:13 the wheels are called haggalgal ("the whirling/rolling thing") — a second Hebrew term for the same objects that the canon does not use.

items.canon_french: «L’aspect des roues était comme le scintillement de la chrysolite ; les quatre avaient la même forme ; leur aspect et leur fonctionnement étaient comme si une roue se trouvait au milieu de l’autre. Dans leur marche, elles allaient suivant leurs quatre côtés, elles ne pivotaient pas dans leur marche. Quant à leurs jantes - elles avaient de la hauteur et un aspect effrayant - (...) elles étaient couvertes d’yeux qui étaient autour de toutes les quatre. […] car l’esprit des êtres était dans les roues».

reading_quotes.french: Au centre des «soucoupes volantes», très proches en aspect de celle où nous nous trouvons, est située la partie habitable : la «jante»
nos engins étaient munis de hublots, les «yeux» des «jantes»
D’autres créateurs, à l’intérieur des engins, les dirigent : «(...) l’esprit des êtres était dans les roues.»

items.reading_summary: The wheels are saucers; "a wheel within a wheel" describes their look and working; the "rim" is the habitable central part and the "eyes" are portholes; "the spirit of the beings was in the wheels" = other creators inside piloting.

load_bearing.gloss: their appearance and their make/workmanship
load_bearing.comment: maʿăśeh is "work, make, construction" (library: "workmanship"); "fonctionnement" (operation) is a mechanising choice — the canon's comment "leur aspect et leur fonctionnement ne sont pas trop mal décrits" leans on it.

load_bearing.french: comme si une roue se trouvait au milieu de l’autre
load_bearing.gloss: the wheel in the midst of the wheel
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

load_bearing.gloss: their backs / rims (gab "back, convex surface, rim/felloe")
load_bearing.comment: A rim is the outer edge of a wheel; the canon places the "jante" at the centre of the saucer. Hebrew gab ("back, boss, curved surface") is less tied to the outer edge than French "jante".

load_bearing.gloss: full of eyes all around
load_bearing.comment: ʿayin is "eye" and also "look, gleam" (the same noun is "scintillement" in kәʿên, v.4, 7, 16); "eyes all around" on a rim is the Hebrew text.

load_bearing.french: l’esprit des êtres était dans les roues
load_bearing.gloss: the rûaḥ of the living creature (SINGULAR) was in the wheels
load_bearing.comment: Hebrew haḥayyāh is singular with article ("the living creature", or "the spirit of life"); French "des êtres" is plural. The canon's "other creators inside" needs persons; the Hebrew gives one rûaḥ of one ḥayyāh.

ellipsis.cut: The "(...)" inside v.18 covers only the resumptive "and their rims" (וְגַבֹּתָם). In the […] I elide vv.19-21a, which the canon quotes in full.
ellipsis.note: No sense-changing cut in this block.

items.french_variance: TBWTT-3:164 re-quotes v.18 without "elles avaient de la hauteur et un aspect effrayant" and without the ellipsis mark; and re-quotes vv.16-17 with a new "(...)".
items.analysis: Wheel-shaped objects that rise from the ground with the figures (v.19, 21: וּבְהִנָּשֵׂא ... יִנָּשְׂאוּ הָאוֹפַנִּים), a wheel-in-wheel structure, a tarshish-stone gleam and rims "full of eyes all round" are all in the Hebrew. Three load-bearing French words are stronger than the original: "fonctionnement" for maʿăśeh ("make"), "jantes" for gab, and the plural "l'esprit des êtres" for the singular rûaḥ haḥayyāh. The canon's placing of the "rim" at the centre contradicts the word in both languages.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] That gab can mean "boss/convex surface" as well as "rim" is a lexicon statement not checked against the library glossary.

items.canon_french: «Au-dessus de la tête des êtres était une sorte de plateforme ; c’était comme l’éclat imposant du cristal ; elle s’étendait sur leurs têtes dans la partie supérieure. […] c’était, pareille à l’aspect d’une pierre de saphir, la forme d’un trône et sur la forme de trône une forme pareille à l’aspect d’un homme (qui était) dessus, dans la partie supérieure».

reading_quotes.french: Plus haut attend le gros véhicule interplanétaire
Ce dernier, sur le grand vaisseau, surveillait et coordonnait le travail des créateurs

items.reading_summary: The "platform" above the beings is the large interplanetary vehicle; the man-like form on the throne is the one supervising the work from the big ship.

load_bearing.gloss: beaten-out expanse; the "firmament" of Gen 1:6-8
load_bearing.comment: Same Hebrew noun as the Genesis "firmament" and as Dan 12:3 ("l'éclat du firmament", C-034). The French uses "plateforme" here and "firmament" there, so the reader of the French cannot see that Ezekiel's object is called by the name of the sky-vault. "une sorte de" renders dәmûṯ "likeness".

load_bearing.gloss: like the look of the awesome ice/crystal
load_bearing.comment: qeraḥ is "ice, frost" (crystal by extension).

load_bearing.gloss: the heads of the living creature (sg.)
load_bearing.comment: Hebrew singular collective again; French plural.

load_bearing.french: une forme pareille à l’aspect d’un homme
load_bearing.gloss: a likeness like the appearance of a human
load_bearing.comment: Literal, including the double hedge (likeness / like appearance).

load_bearing.gloss: likeness of a throne/seat
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

ellipsis.cut: No "(...)" in 3:162 (my […] elides vv.23-25, quoted in full by the canon). The quotation stops before v.27-28: the figure's fire/ḥašmal appearance and "This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of YHWH" (מַרְאֵה דְּמוּת כְּבוֹד־יְהוָה).
ellipsis.note: Stopping at v.26 leaves out the text's own identification of the enthroned figure as the kāḇôḏ of YHWH — which the canon elsewhere (3:193) says is the name of the large ship; quoting v.28 would have tied the two together.

items.french_variance: "plateforme" (twice) / "plate-forme" (three times) within 3:162; 3:166 re-quotes with "pareil" (masc.) for "pareille" and without "(qui était)". rāqîaʿ = "plateforme" here, "firmament" at Dan 12:3 and in Genesis 1.
items.analysis: A solid surface above the figures, gleaming like ice, with a seat on it and a human-like figure on the seat, is the Hebrew text. The French "plateforme" is a flat, engineered word for rāqîaʿ; the Hebrew term is the cosmic "firmament" (a hammered-out vault), which is both stronger (a rigid made thing — the rqʿ root recurs for metal in Job 37:18) and more awkward (it is the sky-dome, not a vehicle) than "plateforme". The Hebrew goes further than the canon's quotation in v.28, where the scene is named "the likeness of the kāḇôḏ of YHWH" — the canon's own term for the ship.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] Whether Dhorme printed "plate-forme" for rāqîaʿ in Ezekiel has not been collated.

items.ref_note: No reference printed; re-quotes Ezek 1:7 from TBWTT-3:159 with altered number.
items.canon_french: «leurs jambes... brillaient comme le scintillement de l’airain poli»

reading_quotes.french: Des «ailes» sur leurs scaphandres métalliques
Vous avez pu remarquer que les combinaisons de vos cosmonautes sont très brillantes

items.reading_summary: The gleaming legs show metallic suits, like the shiny suits of modern cosmonauts.

load_bearing.original: וְרַגְלֵיהֶ֖ם רֶ֣גֶל יְשָׁרָ֑ה וְכַ֣ף רַגְלֵיהֶ֗ם כְּכַף֙ רֶ֣גֶל עֵ֔גֶל וְנֹ֣צְצִ֔ים
load_bearing.translit: wәraḡlêhem reḡel yәšārāh wәḵap̄ raḡlêhem kәḵap̄ reḡel ʿēḡel wәnōṣәṣîm
load_bearing.gloss: and their legs: a straight leg; and the sole of their feet like the sole of a calf's foot; and (they were) sparkling
load_bearing.comment: The canon's "..." removes "straight" and the calf's hoof and changes the verb from singular ("brillait", 3:159) to plural — which is the number of the Hebrew participle nōṣәṣîm.

ellipsis.cut: "la jambe était droite et la plante de leurs pieds était comme la plante de la patte du veau".
ellipsis.note: The calf's-hoof clause is the non-human detail of the verse.

items.french_variance: "brillait" (TBWTT-3:159) vs "brillaient" (TBWTT-3:163).
items.analysis: The re-quotation differs from the canon's own first quotation of the verse (plural for singular) and in doing so comes closer to the Hebrew, whose participle is masculine plural and most naturally says that "they" gleamed like burnished bronze. The elision also removes the calf's hoof.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] Parsing of nōṣәṣîm is mine, as in C-013.

items.ref_note: No reference printed; re-quotes Ezek 1:16-18 from TBWTT-3:161.
items.canon_french: «quant à leurs jantes, elles étaient couvertes d’yeux qui étaient autour de toutes les quatre»

reading_quotes.french: nos engins étaient munis de hublots, les «yeux» des «jantes», car nous n’avions pas encore trouvé le moyen de voir à travers les parois métalliques

items.reading_summary: The "eyes" on the "rims" are portholes of the saucers.

load_bearing.gloss: and their rims were full of eyes all round, for the four of them
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

load_bearing.original: וְכָל־בְּשָׂרָם֙ וְגַבֵּהֶ֔ם וִֽידֵיהֶ֖ם וְכַנְפֵיהֶ֑ם וְהָאֽוֹפַנִּ֗ים מְלֵאִ֤ים עֵינַ֙יִם֙ סָבִ֔יב
load_bearing.translit: wәḵol-bәśārām wәḡabbēhem wîḏêhem wәḵanp̄êhem wәhāʾôp̄annîm mәlēʾîm ʿênayim sāḇîḇ
load_bearing.gloss: and all their flesh and their backs and their hands and their wings and the wheels were full of eyes all round
load_bearing.comment: Ezek 10:12 (unquoted): in the parallel vision the eyes cover the cherubim's bodies, hands and wings as well as the wheels.

ellipsis.cut: Relative to 3:161 the re-quotation drops "elles avaient de la hauteur et un aspect effrayant" and the "(...)".

items.french_variance: Wording differs from TBWTT-3:161 (clause dropped).
items.analysis: Eyes all round the rims is the Hebrew of 1:18. The parallel in 10:12, which the canon does not cite although it quotes 10:8 and 10:19, spreads the same eyes over the cherubim's flesh, backs, hands and wings — hard to read as portholes of a craft.

items.canon_french: «(...) l’esprit des êtres était dans les roues.»

reading_quotes.french: D’autres créateurs, à l’intérieur des engins, les dirigent

items.reading_summary: Other creators inside the craft pilot them.

load_bearing.french: l’esprit des êtres était dans les roues
load_bearing.gloss: the rûaḥ of the living creature (sg.) in the wheels
load_bearing.comment: See C-015: Hebrew singular haḥayyāh; the wheels move because the creature's rûaḥ is in them — i.e. the wheels are animated by the same rûaḥ as the creatures outside, not by further occupants.

ellipsis.cut: The rest of v.21.

items.analysis: The step from "the spirit of the beings was in the wheels" to "other creators inside" is easier from the French plural "des êtres" than from the Hebrew, where a single rûaḥ of "the living creature" (the collective already seen outside the wheels) is in them. The Hebrew explains co-ordinated motion by a shared rûaḥ; it does not put additional persons in the wheels.

items.ref_note: Sentence 1 = Ezek 1:6a; sentence 2 = Ezek 1:9b. Only v.9 is cited.
items.canon_french: «Chacun d’eux avait quatre faces. Leurs faces ne tournaient pas quand ils avançaient.»

reading_quotes.french: Le scaphandre est également décrit avec ses quatre hublots comparables à ceux de vos premiers scaphandres marins

items.reading_summary: Four faces that do not turn = the four fixed portholes of a diving-helmet-like suit.

load_bearing.gloss: and four faces to each
load_bearing.comment: This clause is v.6, not v.9.

load_bearing.french: Leurs faces ne tournaient pas quand ils avançaient
load_bearing.gloss: they did not turn when they went
load_bearing.comment: In the Hebrew of v.9 the subject of "did not turn" is "they" (the creatures; the preceding noun is "their wings"); "faces" is not the subject. "Leurs faces" comes from attaching the last words of v.8 (וּפְנֵיהֶם וְכַנְפֵיהֶם לְאַרְבַּעְתָּם) to v.9.

ellipsis.note: Not an ellipsis but a conflation of two verses under one reference.

items.french_variance: TBWTT-3:159: "Chacun avait quatre faces" / "Leurs faces ne se tournaient pas quand ils avançaient"; TBWTT-3:165: "Chacun d’eux avait quatre faces" / "Leurs faces ne tournaient pas quand ils avançaient".
items.analysis: The reference is partial: the first sentence is 1:6 and the second 1:9. "Faces that do not turn" — the porthole hook — depends on a French sentence-division that makes "leurs faces" the subject; the Hebrew verb in v.9 has the creatures as subject ("they did not turn as they went; each went straight ahead"). The wording also differs from the canon's own full quotation six paragraphs earlier.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] The claim that the French sentence division attaches the end of v.8 to v.9 is inferred from the French word order, not checked against Dhorme.

items.canon_french: «Au-dessus de la tête des êtres était une sorte de plate-forme ; c’était comme l’éclat imposant du cristal (...). Par-dessus la plate-forme qui était sur leurs têtes, c’était, pareil à l’aspect d’une pierre de saphir, la forme d’un trône et sur la forme de trône une forme pareille à l’aspect d’un homme dessus, dans la partie supérieure.»

reading_quotes.french: Les petites «soucoupes» sont un peu des «Lems» de service
Plus haut attend le gros véhicule interplanétaire

items.reading_summary: Re-quotation of C-016: the platform is the big interplanetary vehicle with its supervisor.

load_bearing.gloss: and a likeness over the heads of the living creature: a rāqîaʿ
load_bearing.comment: See C-016.

load_bearing.french: pareil à l’aspect d’une pierre de saphir
load_bearing.gloss: like the appearance of sapphire/lapis stone
load_bearing.comment: Same stone as the "sapphire" pavement of Exod 24:10 (other slice): a real Hebrew cross-link (sappîr) between the two scenes.

ellipsis.cut: vv.23-25 (wings under the platform, sound of the wings, voice above).
ellipsis.note: Already quoted at 3:162.

items.french_variance: Differs from 3:162 in "pareil" for "pareille", "plate-forme" for "plateforme", and the dropped "(qui était)".
items.analysis: Same assessment as C-016. The platform is "over the heads" of the figures in Hebrew as in French; that it is a separate, larger vehicle "waiting higher up" is added. The sapphire (sappîr) link to Exod 24:10 is in the Hebrew.

items.canon_french: «Fils d’homme, tiens-toi sur tes jambes et je te parlerai (...) écoute ce que je vais te dire (...) et mange ce que je vais te donner».

reading_quotes.french: mais un des créateurs lui dit
Il s’agit en fait d’une «nourriture» intellectuelle

items.reading_summary: One of the creators speaks to Ezekiel; the eating is intellectual nourishment, like "eating" of the tree of knowledge.

load_bearing.gloss: son of a human
load_bearing.comment: Literal; a term that distinguishes the addressee as human from a speaker who is not classed so.

load_bearing.french: mange ce que je vais te donner
load_bearing.gloss: and eat what I am giving you
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

ellipsis.cut: vv.2-7 (the rûaḥ enters him and sets him on his feet; the mission to the "rebellious house") and, inside v.8, "do not be rebellious like the rebellious house; open your mouth".
ellipsis.note: The cuts remove the commission to Israel but not the sense of the quoted clauses.

items.analysis: That the eating is figurative is the text's own device (the thing eaten is a written scroll, 2:9-3:3), so the canon's "intellectual food" is a reading the Hebrew invites; the comparison with the tree of knowledge is added. The speaker in Hebrew is the voice from the enthroned kāḇôḏ figure of 1:26-28 (a single figure of human appearance), compatible with "one of the creators" only by interpretation.

items.canon_french: «(...) voici qu’une main était étendue vers moi et (...) il y avait dedans le rouleau d’un livre (...) il était rédigé sur la face et au revers».

reading_quotes.french: Il était écrit recto-verso, chose surprenante à lire, à l’époque où l’on n’écrivait que d’un côté des parchemins
ce qu’il apprend, ce que vous apprenez sur l’origine des hommes, est tellement excitant et réconfortant

items.reading_summary: A book written on both sides — remarkable for the period — whose content is what Raël is now learning about human origins, exciting and comforting.

load_bearing.french: rédigé sur la face et au revers
load_bearing.gloss: written front and back
load_bearing.comment: Literal: the two-sided writing is the Hebrew text.

load_bearing.gloss: a scroll of a book/document
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

ellipsis.cut: The quotation ends before v.10b: "and written on it were laments, and mourning, and woe" (וְכָתוּב אֵלֶיהָ קִנִים וָהֶגֶה וָהִי).
ellipsis.note: The verse itself states the content of the scroll.

items.analysis: The physical detail (opisthograph scroll) is original. The content the canon assigns to the scroll — the comforting truth about the origin of humankind — is contradicted by the half-verse it stops short of: the Hebrew says what was written on it was "laments, mourning and woe". The canon's closing "(...)" stands before "il était rédigé", not after, so the omission of the content clause is unmarked.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] The canon's statement that at that period only one side of parchments was written on is a historical claim not assessed here.

items.canon_french: «Je le mangeai donc et il fut dans ma bouche comme du miel pour la douceur».

reading_quotes.french: Le rouleau est ensuite «mangé» ; c’est-à-dire qu’Ezéchiel en prend connaissance

items.reading_summary: Eating the scroll = taking in its knowledge, which is sweet (exciting, comforting).

load_bearing.french: comme du miel pour la douceur
load_bearing.gloss: like honey for sweetness
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

ellipsis.cut: Unmarked: v.3a "Son of human, feed your belly and fill your innards with this scroll".

items.analysis: Sweetness on eating the scroll is the Hebrew text and the figurative sense of eating is internal to it. The inference from sweetness to comforting content sits against 2:10b (laments, mourning, woe; see C-021) and 3:14 ("I went bitter", מַר).

items.ref_note: Reference lists the verses in the order quoted (14 then 12).
items.canon_french: «L’esprit m’avait soulevé ; il m’emporta (...) j’entendis derrière moi le bruit d’une grande rumeur».

reading_quotes.french: Puis Ezéchiel est transporté par le vaisseau des créateurs jusqu’au lieu où il doit répandre la nouvelle

items.reading_summary: Ezekiel is carried by the creators' vessel; the great noise behind him accompanies the lift.

load_bearing.gloss: and (a) rûaḥ lifted me and took me
load_bearing.comment: rûaḥ has no article and takes feminine verbs: "a wind / a spirit lifted me". The French definite "L'esprit" personalises; the Hebrew is equally "a wind", an impersonal lifting force.

load_bearing.gloss: the sound of a great quaking / rumbling
load_bearing.comment: raʿaš is "shaking, earthquake, rumble"; "rumeur" is much weaker. The same noun is "branle-bas" at 37:7 (C-029).

load_bearing.original: וְק֥וֹל הָאוֹפַנִּ֖ים לְעֻמָּתָ֑ם וְק֖וֹל רַ֥עַשׁ גָּדֽוֹל׃
load_bearing.translit: wәqôl hāʾôp̄annîm lәʿummāṯām wәqôl raʿaš gāḏôl
load_bearing.gloss: and the sound of the wheels beside them, and the sound of a great rumbling
load_bearing.comment: v.13, not quoted by the canon, attributes the great rumbling to the wings of the creatures and to the wheels.

ellipsis.cut: Order inverted (v.14 then v.12). Cut: v.12b "Blessed be the glory of YHWH from his place", all of v.13 (sound of the wings and of the wheels), v.14b "and I went bitter in the heat of my spirit, and the hand of YHWH was strong upon me".
ellipsis.note: The omitted v.13 is the verse that connects the noise of the lift-off with the "wheels" the canon calls saucers.

items.analysis: A lifting-and-carrying agent and a great rumbling noise behind the prophet are the Hebrew text. The original is stronger than the French on two points: raʿaš is a quake-like roar, not a "rumeur", and v.13 (skipped) says the roar is the sound of the wings and of the wheels (ʾôp̄annîm) — the canon's craft. On the agent, the Hebrew is more open than the French: anarthrous rûaḥ is "a wind" as readily as "the spirit".

items.canon_french: «(...) l’esprit me souleva entre ciel et terre et m’amena à

reading_quotes.french: Plus loin, le «prophète» est encore emmené dans un engin volant

items.reading_summary: Ezekiel is again taken in a flying craft, lifted between sky and earth to Jerusalem.

load_bearing.french: l’esprit me souleva entre ciel et terre
load_bearing.original: וַתִּשָּׂ֣א אֹתִ֣י ר֣וּחַ ׀ בֵּֽין־הָאָ֣רֶץ וּבֵ֣ין הַשָּׁמַ֡יִם
load_bearing.translit: wattiśśāʾ ʾōṯî rûaḥ bên-hāʾāreṣ ûḇên haššāmayim
load_bearing.gloss: and (a) rûaḥ lifted me between the earth and the skies
load_bearing.comment: Literal apart from the article on "esprit" (Hebrew rûaḥ is anarthrous).

load_bearing.gloss: and brought me to Jerusalem in visions of Elohim
load_bearing.comment: The words immediately after "Jérusalem" in Hebrew are bәmarʾôṯ ʾĕlōhîm "in visions of Elohim"; the canon's closing "(...)" begins exactly there.

ellipsis.cut: Before: "He stretched out the form of a hand and took me by a lock of my head" (וַיִּקָּחֵנִי בְּצִיצִת רֹאשִׁי). After: "in visions of Elohim, to the entrance of the gate ...".
ellipsis.note: Both cuts bear on the mode of transport: seized by the hair by a hand-like form, and "in visions of Elohim".

items.analysis: Lifting "between earth and sky" and transport to Jerusalem are the Hebrew wording. The ellipses remove the two qualifiers that the Hebrew attaches to the journey: the grasp by a lock of hair and, directly after "to Jerusalem", "in visions of Elohim" (bәmarʾôṯ ʾĕlōhîm). The same phrase is cut from the canon's quotations of 11:24 (C-028) and 40:2 (C-030).

items.canon_french: «Alors apparut, chez les chérubins, une forme de main humaine, sous leurs ailes».

reading_quotes.french: sous leurs «ailes», les « chérubins» ont des mains comme les hommes
de même qu’en raison de notre petite taille on nous prend pour des enfants, des chérubins

items.reading_summary: The "cherubim" have human hands under their "wings" (suits with jets); the creators are called cherubs because their small stature makes them look like children.

load_bearing.gloss: the pattern/structure of a human hand
load_bearing.comment: Literal; taḇnîṯ is "built form, model".

load_bearing.gloss: to/on the cherubim
load_bearing.comment: Hebrew kәrûḇîm are the four-faced, four-winged ḥayyôṯ of chapter 1 (10:20: "I knew that they were cherubim"); nothing in the word denotes a child.

load_bearing.gloss: that they were cherubim
load_bearing.comment: The text itself equates the cherubim with the living creatures seen at the Kebar.

items.analysis: Human hands under the wings is the Hebrew text (also 1:8). The explanatory aside at 3:189 — creators taken for children, hence "chérubins" — depends on the modern French/European sense of "chérubin" (a winged infant) and has no basis in Hebrew kәrûḇ, which in this very book names four-faced creatures with wheels.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] That the child sense of "chérubin" derives from European art (putti) rather than from the Hebrew is general knowledge, not from the library.

items.canon_french: «Les chérubins, lorsqu’ils partirent, dressèrent leurs ailes et s’élevèrent de terre, sous mes yeux, et les roues conjointement avec eux».

reading_quotes.french: Autant de voyages pour Ezéchiel dans un des engins volants des créateurs

items.reading_summary: The suited creators take off, the saucers ("wheels") rising with them.

load_bearing.french: s’élevèrent de terre, sous mes yeux
load_bearing.gloss: and they rose from the earth before my eyes
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

load_bearing.gloss: and the wheels alongside them
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

ellipsis.cut: Unmarked: v.19b "and it stood at the entrance of the east gate of the house of YHWH, and the glory of the Elohim of Israel was above them" (וּכְבוֹד אֱלֹהֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל עֲלֵיהֶם מִלְמָעְלָה).
ellipsis.note: The omitted half places the kāḇôḏ above the cherubim-and-wheels group — a spatial arrangement that matches the canon's model (large ship above, small craft below).

items.analysis: Take-off from the ground, witnessed, with the wheels rising alongside, is the Hebrew text; the French is literal. The unquoted second half of the verse adds that the kāḇôḏ was "over them from above", which fits the canon's arrangement better than the half it quotes.

items.canon_french: «L’esprit me souleva et m’emmena (...)».

reading_quotes.french: Autant de voyages pour Ezéchiel dans un des engins volants des créateurs

items.reading_summary: Another journey in a flying craft.

load_bearing.gloss: and (a) rûaḥ lifted me and brought me
load_bearing.comment: Anarthrous rûaḥ again; French supplies the article.

ellipsis.cut: Destination: "to the east gate of the house of YHWH" and the twenty-five men.

items.analysis: Lifting and carrying by rûaḥ is the Hebrew; the craft is the canon's identification. The journey is inside the vision that began at 8:3 "in visions of Elohim" and ends at 11:24 "the vision went up from me".

items.canon_french: «La gloire de Iahvé s’éleva du milieu de la ville et s’arrêta sur la montagne qui est à l’orient de la ville. L’esprit me souleva et m’emmena en Chaldée (...)».

reading_quotes.french: Autant de voyages pour Ezéchiel dans un des engins volants des créateurs
le grand vaisseau appelé respectueusement «gloire de Dieu»

items.reading_summary: The "glory" (the large ship) lifts off from the city and sets down on the mountain to the east; Ezekiel is flown back to Chaldea.

load_bearing.french: La gloire de Iahvé s’éleva du milieu de la ville et s’arrêta sur la montagne
load_bearing.original: וַיַּ֙עַל֙ כְּב֣וֹד יְהוָ֔ה מֵעַ֖ל תּ֣וֹךְ הָעִ֑יר וַֽיַּעֲמֹד֙ עַל־הָהָ֔ר
load_bearing.translit: wayyaʿal kәḇôḏ YHWH mēʿal tôḵ hāʿîr wayyaʿămōḏ ʿal-hāhār
load_bearing.gloss: and the kāḇôḏ of YHWH went up from over the midst of the city and stood on the mountain
load_bearing.comment: kāḇôḏ (root kbd "be heavy") is "weight, substance, splendour"; here it is the grammatical subject of verbs of ascent and standing. "gloire" keeps only the splendour sense.

load_bearing.original: וַתְּבִיאֵ֤נִי כַשְׂדִּ֙ימָה֙ אֶל־הַגּוֹלָ֔ה בַּמַּרְאֶ֖ה בְּר֣וּחַ אֱלֹהִ֑ים
load_bearing.translit: wattәḇîʾēnî ḵaśdîmāh ʾel-haggôlāh bammarʾeh bәrûaḥ ʾĕlōhîm
load_bearing.gloss: and brought me to Chaldea, to the exiles, in the vision, by the rûaḥ of Elohim
load_bearing.comment: The canon's "(...)" begins after "Chaldée"; the next Hebrew words are "in the vision, by the rûaḥ of Elohim".

ellipsis.cut: v.24b: "to the exiles, in the vision, by the rûaḥ of Elohim; and the vision that I had seen went up from me" (וַיַּעַל מֵעָלַי הַמַּרְאֶה אֲשֶׁר רָאִיתִי).
ellipsis.note: The cut clause states that the return to Chaldea took place "in the vision" and that the vision then left him.

items.analysis: The kāḇôḏ behaves in Hebrew as a located object: it "goes up" from over the city and "stands" on a mountain (the etymological sense "heaviness" is, if anything, more object-like than "gloire"). Against the journey reading, the Hebrew of v.24 says the transport was "in the vision" and that "the vision went up from me" — both removed by the ellipsis.
