outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] kbd "be heavy" as the root of kāḇôḏ is a lexicon statement; the library glossary entry for kavod was not opened.

items.canon_french: «(...) Iahvé me fit sortir et me déposa au milieu de la vallée».

reading_quotes.french: Les créateurs vont ressusciter des hommes dont il ne reste que des ossements

items.reading_summary: Ezekiel is set down in the valley where the creators will re-create men from bone remains.

load_bearing.gloss: and he brought me out by/in the rûaḥ of YHWH
load_bearing.comment: In Hebrew YHWH is not the subject noun of this clause: the text is "he brought me out by the rûaḥ of YHWH". The canon's French (after its ellipsis) makes Iahvé the direct agent and drops the rûaḥ.

load_bearing.french: me déposa au milieu de la vallée
load_bearing.gloss: and set me down in the midst of the valley/plain
load_bearing.comment: Literal; hēnîaḥ "set down, deposit".

ellipsis.cut: Before: "The hand of YHWH was upon me". Within: "by the rûaḥ of YHWH". After: "and it was full of bones".
ellipsis.note: The instrument of the transport ("by the rûaḥ of YHWH") is dropped; with it the sentence reads as physical conveyance by Iahvé.

items.analysis: The wording "Iahvé me fit sortir" is not the Hebrew clause: the original has an unnamed subject who brings the prophet out "by/in the rûaḥ of YHWH" under "the hand of YHWH", the book's formula for visionary transport (cf. 8:3; 40:1-2). "Set me down" (hēnîaḥ) is literal.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] Whether the dropping of "par l'esprit de" is Dhorme's or the canon's has not been collated.

items.canon_french: «Fils d’homme, ces ossements peuvent-ils revivre ? (...) il y eut un bruit, et voilà que ce fut un branle-bas (...) il y avait sur (les ossements) des nerfs, de la chair croissait et il étendit sur eux de la peau par-dessus (...) ils prirent vie et se dressèrent sur leurs pieds, armée très, très nombreuse».

reading_quotes.french: Il suffit de placer une de ces particules, pouvant provenir de débris osseux, dans un appareil qui fournit toute la matière vivante nécessaire à la reconstitution de l’être originel
Tout cela est très facile à réaliser et vous le ferez un jour

items.reading_summary: A literal, technical re-creation of dead men from the information in a particle of bone, by a machine supplying living matter.

load_bearing.gloss: will these bones live?
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

load_bearing.gloss: a shaking / rattling
load_bearing.comment: Same noun as "grande rumeur" at 3:12 (C-023): two French words for one Hebrew word.

load_bearing.french: des nerfs, de la chair croissait
load_bearing.gloss: sinews, and flesh came up
load_bearing.comment: gîḏîm are sinews/tendons ("nerfs" in the older French sense). The staged order bone → sinew → flesh → skin is the Hebrew.

load_bearing.french: il étendit sur eux de la peau
load_bearing.gloss: and skin covered over them
load_bearing.comment: In the MT ʿôr "skin" is the subject of an intransitive verb; the French "il étendit" supplies a personal agent (as v.6 does, in the first person: וְקָרַמְתִּי).

load_bearing.gloss: and the rûaḥ came into them and they lived
load_bearing.comment: The canon's "(...)" swallows the clause "the rûaḥ came into them".

load_bearing.gloss: these bones are the whole house of Israel
load_bearing.comment: v.11, not quoted: the text's own decoding of the vision.

ellipsis.cut: v.3b ("Lord YHWH, you know"), vv.4-6 (command to prophesy; "I will put sinews ... and put rûaḥ in you"), v.7a and 7c (the prophesying; "bone to its bone"), v.8b ("but rûaḥ was not in them"), v.9 (the rûaḥ summoned from the four winds to breathe into "these slain"), v.10a; and, after the quotation, vv.11-14 ("these bones are the whole house of Israel ... I will bring you into the land of Israel").
ellipsis.note: The cuts remove (i) the two-stage structure body-then-rûaḥ, (ii) the instrument (prophetic speech), and (iii) the text's explicit statement that the bones are a figure for exiled Israel.

items.french_variance: ETTMTTP-2:72 cites the same passage as "(Ezéchiel, XXVII, 3, 7-8, 10)" (chapter number wrong there; other slice).
items.analysis: The anatomical sequence the canon reads technically (bones, sinews, flesh, skin, standing alive) is the Hebrew text and Dhorme renders it literally. The Hebrew is less favourable in what the ellipses remove: the bodies are complete but lifeless until rûaḥ ("breath/wind") is called from the four winds (v.8b-10) — a second stage with no counterpart in the canon's cell-plus-machine account — and v.11 decodes the whole scene as a figure: "these bones are the whole house of Israel". The agentive "il étendit" is French; the MT has "skin covered them".

items.canon_french: «Il m’emmena (...) et me déposa sur une très haute montagne sur laquelle il y avait comme les constructions d’une ville, au midi (...) (il y avait) un homme dont l’aspect était comme l’aspect de l’airain».

reading_quotes.french: Ezéchiel est encore emmené par un engin volant qui le conduit près d’un homme revêtu d’un scaphandre
Cette ville est une des bases terrestres qu’avaient les créateurs à cette époque, toujours sur de hautes montagnes
L’homme à l’aspect d’airain est bien sûr revêtu d’un scaphandre métallique

items.reading_summary: A flight to one of the creators' mountain bases (the "city"), where a man in a metallic suit meets him.

load_bearing.french: Il m’emmena (...) et me déposa sur une très haute montagne
load_bearing.original: בְּמַרְא֣וֹת אֱלֹהִ֔ים הֱבִיאַ֖נִי אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיְנִיחֵ֗נִי אֶל־הַ֤ר גָּבֹ֙הַּ֙ מְאֹ֔ד
load_bearing.translit: bәmarʾôṯ ʾĕlōhîm hĕḇîʾanî ʾel-ʾereṣ yiśrāʾēl wayәnîḥēnî ʾel-har gāḇōah mәʾōḏ
load_bearing.gloss: in visions of Elohim he brought me to the land of Israel and set me down on a very high mountain
load_bearing.comment: The Hebrew verse BEGINS with "in visions of Elohim"; the canon's quotation begins with the verb and its "(...)" covers "to the land of Israel".

load_bearing.gloss: something like the structure of a city
load_bearing.comment: Literal, hedge included.

load_bearing.french: un homme dont l’aspect était comme l’aspect de l’airain
load_bearing.gloss: a man whose appearance was like the appearance of bronze/copper
load_bearing.comment: Literal: a man (ʾîš) with a metallic look is the Hebrew text; it is his appearance, not his clothing, that is compared.

ellipsis.cut: Opening words "In visions of Elohim" (unmarked); "to the land of Israel"; v.3 "He brought me there, and behold"; and after the quotation "with a cord of flax in his hand and the measuring reed; and he was standing in the gate".
ellipsis.note: Third case (with 8:3 and 11:24) where the phrase "in visions of Elohim / in the vision" falls outside the canon's quotation.

items.analysis: A high mountain with city-like structures and a man of bronze-like appearance are the Hebrew text; the suit and the base are the canon's reading of a simile. As in 8:3 and 11:24, the quotation omits the frame bәmarʾôṯ ʾĕlōhîm, here the very first words of the verse. The measuring line and reed (cut) define the man's function in the Hebrew as a surveyor.

items.canon_french: «Quand les prêtres sortiront, (...) ils laisseront là les vêtements avec lesquels ils officient, car (ces vêtements) sont saints».

reading_quotes.french: avaient des vêtements aseptiques pour faire leur service et ces vêtements devaient rester dans le «temple» pour ne pas risquer de ramener des germes dangereux pour les créateurs
Ils auraient dû écrire «car ces vêtements sont sains» SAINS

items.reading_summary: The priests' service garments were aseptic and stayed inside the "temple" to keep germs from the creators; the text should have read "sains" (healthy/clean) instead of "saints" (holy).

load_bearing.gloss: for they are holiness / a holy thing
load_bearing.comment: The pun sains/saints exists only in French. qōḏeš is "set-apartness"; no Hebrew word for "healthy" or "clean" (ṭāhôr) resembles it.

load_bearing.gloss: when the priests enter
load_bearing.comment: Hebrew has "when they enter" (bwʾ), followed by "they shall not go out"; the French starts from the going-out.

load_bearing.gloss: and there they shall lay down their garments in which they minister
load_bearing.comment: Literal: the garments stay inside.

load_bearing.french: pour ne pas risquer de ramener des germes
load_bearing.gloss: so that they do not sanctify the people by their garments
load_bearing.comment: Unquoted parallel: the stated purpose of the clothing change is to prevent "holiness" passing from the garments to the people — transmission by contact, but in the direction sanctuary → people, the reverse of the canon's (people → creators).

ellipsis.cut: "they shall not go out of the holy place into the outer court"; and after the quotation "they shall put on other garments and approach what belongs to the people".
ellipsis.note: The cut clauses reinforce the containment rule (no exit in service dress; change before contact with the public).

items.analysis: The explicit argument ("they should have written sains") is a French homophone and cannot be stated in Hebrew; on that point the reading is wholly translation-dependent. Separately, the rule the canon describes is in the Hebrew and is stated more fully in the omitted clauses and in 44:19: service garments are confined to the inner area and changed before contact with the people, because qōḏeš is treated as transmissible by contact. In the Hebrew the transmission runs outward (the people must not be "sanctified"), not inward as the germ reading requires.

items.ref_note: No reference; emended re-quotation of the verse cited at TBWTT-3:191.
items.canon_french: «car ces vêtements sont sains»

reading_quotes.french: Subtilité incompréhensible pour des primitifs déifiant tout ce qui leur était dit ou montré

items.reading_summary: The canon corrects the verse: it should read "sains" (healthy) not "saints" (holy).

load_bearing.gloss: holiness, a set-apart thing
load_bearing.comment: The proposed correction is a change of one French letter; the Hebrew noun has no near-homophone meaning "healthy".

items.analysis: A correction stated in French orthography ("Ils auraient dû écrire") about a text written in Hebrew; see C-032. In the canon's own frame (the creators' language "close to ancient Hebrew", TBWTT-7:35) the pun cannot be the original subtlety.

items.canon_french: «Et voici que la gloire du Dieu d’Israël vint de la direction de l’orient avec un bruit comme le bruit des grandes eaux et la terre resplendit de sa gloire».

reading_quotes.french: le grand vaisseau appelé respectueusement «gloire de Dieu» approche

items.reading_summary: The "glory of God" is the respectful name for the large vessel, here approaching from the east with noise and light.

load_bearing.french: la gloire du Dieu d’Israël vint de la direction de l’orient
load_bearing.original: כְּבוֹד֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בָּ֖א מִדֶּ֣רֶךְ הַקָּדִ֑ים
load_bearing.translit: kәḇôḏ ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl bāʾ midderek haqqāḏîm
load_bearing.gloss: the kāḇôḏ of the Elohim of Israel was coming from the way of the east
load_bearing.comment: Hebrew has ʾĕlōhê (construct of Elohim); the French prints "Dieu" here although it keeps "Elohim"/"Iahvé" elsewhere.

load_bearing.french: avec un bruit comme le bruit des grandes eaux
load_bearing.gloss: and its/his sound was like the sound of many waters
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

load_bearing.french: la terre resplendit de sa gloire
load_bearing.gloss: and the earth was lit up from his kāḇôḏ
load_bearing.comment: hēʾîr is "give light": the ground is illuminated by the kāḇôḏ; "resplendit" is literal.

ellipsis.note: v.3 (unquoted) says this was "like the vision I saw by the river Kebar", tying the kāḇôḏ to the chapter-1 apparatus.

items.french_variance: "Dieu d’Israël" here and at 44:2, against the canon's usual retention of "Elohim" (e.g. Ps 8:6, Job 1:6).
items.analysis: The kāḇôḏ arrives from a compass direction, with a roar like great waters, and lights up the ground: all three properties are in the Hebrew, rendered literally. The vessel identification is the canon's, but it attaches to real predicates. The French "Dieu d'Israël" conceals the plural-form ʾĕlōhê that the canon elsewhere insists on.

items.canon_french: «Cette porte restera fermée, elle ne sera pas ouverte et personne n’y entrera, car Iahvé, Dieu d’Israël, y est entré : elle restera fermée».

reading_quotes.french: Ils ne voulaient pas être dérangés

items.reading_summary: The gate stays shut because the creators did not want to be disturbed.

load_bearing.french: car Iahvé, Dieu d’Israël, y est entré
load_bearing.gloss: because YHWH the Elohim of Israel has entered by it
load_bearing.comment: Literal; the stated reason is the entry itself.

ellipsis.cut: Unmarked: the opening "YHWH said to me".

items.analysis: The Hebrew gives its own reason (the gate is closed because YHWH passed through it); "they did not want to be disturbed" is a motive supplied by the canon. No word depends on the French.

items.canon_french: «Quant au prince, en tant que prince il pourra s’y asseoir pour manger son pain devant Iahvé».

reading_quotes.french: Seul le «prince» a le droit de venir s’entretenir avec les créateurs

items.reading_summary: Only the prince may come and confer with the creators.

load_bearing.gloss: the nāśîʾ (chief, "lifted-up one")
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

load_bearing.french: pour manger son pain devant Iahvé
load_bearing.gloss: to eat bread before YHWH
load_bearing.comment: The Hebrew privilege is to eat a (sacral) meal "before YHWH" in the gate; it does not mention speaking. Hebrew has "bread", French "son pain".

ellipsis.note: The verse is split over two quotations (C-035, C-036).

items.analysis: The prince's exclusive access to the closed gate is in the Hebrew; that he comes "to confer" with the creators is added — the text has him eat there.

items.canon_french: «Il viendra par l’itinéraire du vestibule de la porte et sortira par le même chemin».

reading_quotes.french: Mais le prince devait venir par un sas où il était aseptisé grâce à des rayons spéciaux

items.reading_summary: The vestibule of the gate is an airlock where the prince was sterilised by special rays.

load_bearing.french: par l’itinéraire du vestibule de la porte
load_bearing.gloss: by the way of the porch/vestibule of the gate
load_bearing.comment: ʾûlām is the architectural porch of a gatehouse or temple.

items.analysis: An entrance hall through which the prince must both enter and leave is the Hebrew text. Sterilisation and rays have no lexical counterpart in either language.

items.canon_french: «Ce sont eux qui s’approcheront de moi pour me servir et ils se tiendront devant moi pour m’offrir la graisse et le sang (...) ce sont eux qui s’approcheront de ma table pour me servir».

reading_quotes.french: Les «prêtres» lévites sont là pour assurer le service des créateurs

items.reading_summary: The Levite "priests" are the creators' service staff.

load_bearing.gloss: to minister to / attend on me
load_bearing.comment: šrṯ is personal attendance (used of servants and courtiers), not only cult.

load_bearing.gloss: my table
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

load_bearing.gloss: fat and blood
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

ellipsis.cut: v.15a "the priests the Levites, the sons of Zadok, who kept the charge of my sanctuary when the sons of Israel went astray"; v.15 end "declares the Lord YHWH"; v.16a "they shall enter my sanctuary"; v.16 end.

items.analysis: First-person singular speech about personal attendance (šrṯ) and "my table" is the Hebrew; the service reading has a real hook and the French is literal. The speaker is singular.

items.canon_french: «Lorsqu’ils franchiront les portes du parvis intérieur ils revêtiront les habits de lin (...) ils ne se ceindront de rien qui fasse transpirer».

reading_quotes.french: L’odeur de la transpiration des hommes de la Terre leur était très désagréable

items.reading_summary: The rule against sweat-inducing clothing exists because the smell of human sweat was unpleasant to the creators.

load_bearing.french: ils ne se ceindront de rien qui fasse transpirer
load_bearing.gloss: they shall not gird themselves with sweat / in what makes sweat
load_bearing.comment: yāzaʿ "sweat" (hapax) is in the Hebrew.

load_bearing.gloss: garments of linen
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

ellipsis.cut: v.17b "and no wool shall come upon them while they minister"; v.18a linen turbans and breeches.
ellipsis.note: The omitted "no wool" is part of the same anti-sweat rule.

items.analysis: The sweat rule is explicit in Hebrew (bayyāzaʿ) and literally translated; the motive (smell disagreeable to the creators) is supplied — the Hebrew states the rule without a reason.

items.canon_french: «Le meilleur des prémices de tout et (...) le meilleur de vos pâtes, vous le donnerez aux prêtres pour que la bénédiction repose sur vos maisons».

reading_quotes.french: Le ravitaillement des créateurs en produits frais continuait ainsi

items.reading_summary: First-fruits and dough given to the priests were the creators' continuing supply of fresh produce.

load_bearing.french: Le meilleur des prémices de tout
load_bearing.gloss: the first/best of all first-fruits of everything
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

load_bearing.gloss: you shall give to the priest (sg.)
load_bearing.comment: The recipient in Hebrew is "the priest" (and "the priests" earlier in the verse) — human recipients, not the deity.

load_bearing.gloss: on your (sg.) house
load_bearing.comment: Hebrew singular "your house"; French plural.

ellipsis.cut: "and every oblation of everything, of all your oblations, shall belong to the priests".

items.analysis: Delivery of first produce is the Hebrew, but both Hebrew and French name the priests as the recipients; that the food went on to the creators is the canon's inference (it reads the priests as their staff).

items.actual_reference: Dan 3:25 (Aramaic; = 3:92 in Bibles that insert the Greek additions)
items.ref_note: Aramaic/Protestant numbering 3:25; the canon follows it.
items.canon_french: «Ah ! Je vois quatre hommes qui marchent librement au milieu de la fournaise et qui n’ont aucun mal, et l’aspect du quatrième ressemble à celui d’un fils des dieux».

reading_quotes.french: les trois hommes sont sauvés par un des créateurs qui vient à leur secours dans le brasier, et qui, grâce à un rayon refoulant et réfrigérant, refoule la chaleur et les flammes

items.reading_summary: The fourth figure is one of the creators, who protects the three men with a repelling, cooling ray.

load_bearing.gloss: a son of gods (Aramaic plural ʾĕlāhîn)
load_bearing.comment: The Aramaic is a true numerical plural ("gods"); Dhorme's "un fils des dieux" is literal where traditional versions have "the Son of God". Speaker is Nebuchadnezzar.

load_bearing.gloss: four men
load_bearing.comment: The fourth is counted among "men" (guḇrîn) in the Aramaic.

load_bearing.gloss: who sent his messenger/angel
load_bearing.comment: Unquoted v.28: the king himself calls the fourth figure "his [their God's] malʾaḵ" — a sent agent.

ellipsis.note: The canon's paraphrase says "bûcher"; the Aramaic has a furnace (ʾattûn), as the quotation itself says ("fournaise").

items.analysis: The identity hook is in the Aramaic and Dhorme transmits it exactly: a fourth "man" whose look is that of a bar-ʾĕlāhîn, a member of the class of gods (plural), later called a sent malʾaḵ (3:28). The ray and the mechanism are additions. Here the original and the French are equally favourable, and both are more favourable than the traditional singular "Son of God".
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] That Catholic French Bibles number this verse 3:92 (after the Greek Song of the Three) is general knowledge, not from the library.

items.ref_note: Verse number is the Aramaic/Hebrew one (6:23), one higher than English Bibles (6:22).
items.canon_french: «Mon Dieu a envoyé son ange et a fermé la gueule des lions».

reading_quotes.french: Là, rien de très compliqué, seulement un petit rayon paralysant, le temps que l’on sorte Daniel de la fosse

items.reading_summary: The lions were immobilised by a small paralysing ray.

load_bearing.gloss: his messenger
load_bearing.comment: malʾaḵ = "messenger, envoy"; "ange" narrows it to a class of beings.

load_bearing.french: a fermé la gueule des lions
load_bearing.gloss: and shut the mouth of the lions
load_bearing.comment: Literal: the text describes the effect on the mouths only.

load_bearing.gloss: my God (Aramaic singular ʾĕlāh + suffix)
load_bearing.comment: Singular in Aramaic.

ellipsis.cut: Unmarked: "and they have not hurt me, because before him innocence was found in me ...".

items.analysis: A sent agent (malʾaḵ) and closed mouths are the Aramaic; the paralysing ray is supplied. The Aramaic "messenger" is slightly more favourable to a personal-envoy reading than "ange".

items.canon_french: «Je levai les yeux et regardai : voici, un homme (...) Son corps était comme de chrysolite, son visage comme l’aspect de l’éclair, ses yeux comme des lampes de feu, ses bras et ses jambes comme l’apparence de l’airain poli, et le bruit de ses paroles comme le bruit d’une multitude».

reading_quotes.french: vous avez encore une description intéressante d’un créateur

items.reading_summary: A description of one of the creators (in the context of the metallic-suit descriptions of Ezekiel).

load_bearing.gloss: a certain man clothed in linen
load_bearing.comment: The Hebrew states what he wears: linen (baddîm), with a belt of gold. The canon's "(...)" begins immediately after "un homme".

load_bearing.french: ses bras et ses jambes comme l’apparence de l’airain poli
load_bearing.gloss: like the look of burnished bronze
load_bearing.comment: Identical three-word phrase to Ezek 1:7, where the canon's French has "comme le scintillement de l’airain poli": same Hebrew, two French renderings.

load_bearing.french: Son corps était comme de chrysolite
load_bearing.gloss: and his body like tarshish-stone
load_bearing.comment: Same stone as the wheels of Ezek 1:16 ("chrysolite" there too): consistent French, real Hebrew cross-link.

ellipsis.cut: "clothed in linen, and his loins girded with gold of Uphaz" (לָבוּשׁ בַּדִּים וּמָתְנָיו חֲגֻרִים בְּכֶתֶם אוּפָז).
ellipsis.note: The omitted words are the only statement of the figure's clothing.

items.french_variance: kәʿên nәḥōšeṯ qālāl = "le scintillement de l’airain poli" (Ezek 1:7, TBWTT-3:159) vs "l’apparence de l’airain poli" (Dan 10:6, TBWTT-3:212).
items.analysis: A "man" (ʾîš) with a gem-like body, lightning-like face and limbs like burnished bronze is the Hebrew text, and the bronze phrase is verbatim the one used of Ezekiel's creatures — an intertext that is real in Hebrew but blurred by the two French renderings. The ellipsis removes the one clothing detail the text gives (linen and a gold belt), which does not sit easily with a metallic suit.

items.ref_note: No parenthetical reference in the canon; introduced only by "Dans le dixième chapitre de Daniel" two paragraphs earlier. Not in the canon_citations index.
items.canon_french: «Michaël (...) est venu (...) là, auprès des rois de Perse».

reading_quotes.french: les créateurs, pour le punir de son manque de foi, ont placé des hommes à eux, des «anges», parmi ces peuples, afin de leur faire accomplir des progrès techniques
L’ange Michaël était le chef de la délégation chargée d’aider les Perses

items.reading_summary: Michael was head of the creators' delegation placed with the Persians to help them progress technically (as punishment of the Jews).

load_bearing.original: מִֽיכָאֵ֗ל אַחַ֛ד הַשָּׂרִ֥ים הָרִאשֹׁנִ֖ים בָּ֣א לְעָזְרֵ֑נִי
load_bearing.translit: mîḵāʾēl ʾaḥaḏ haśśārîm hāriʾšōnîm bāʾ lәʿozrēnî
load_bearing.gloss: Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me
load_bearing.comment: The first "(...)" removes "one of the chief princes"; the second removes "to help me" — Michael comes to help the speaker AGAINST the prince of Persia.

load_bearing.french: là, auprès des rois de Perse
load_bearing.original: וַאֲנִי֙ נוֹתַ֣רְתִּי שָׁ֔ם אֵ֖צֶל מַלְכֵ֥י פָרָֽס׃
load_bearing.translit: waʾănî nôṯartî šām ʾēṣel malḵê p̄ārās
load_bearing.gloss: and I was left there beside the kings of Persia
load_bearing.comment: In Hebrew the one who is "there beside the kings of Persia" is the speaker ("I"), not Michael; the second "(...)" removes the subject and verb.

load_bearing.gloss: and the prince of the kingdom of Persia was standing against me
load_bearing.comment: Verse opening, not quoted: Persia has its own śar, who is the opponent.

load_bearing.gloss: Michael your prince
load_bearing.comment: Unquoted: Michael is "your [Daniel's people's] prince"; 12:1 "the great prince who stands over the sons of your people". The Hebrew title is śar ("prince, commander"), not malʾāḵ ("ange").

ellipsis.cut: Two "(...)" inside one verse: "one of the chief princes"; "to help me; and I remained". Also the verse opening "the prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood me twenty-one days".
ellipsis.note: The two cuts splice the subject of clause 2 (Michael) onto the locative of clause 3 (whose subject is "I"), reversing who is with the kings of Persia and whom Michael helps.

items.analysis: This is the clearest case in the slice of an ellipsis producing the reading. In Hebrew, Persia has its own śar who opposes the speaker; Michael, "one of the chief princes", comes to help the speaker against him; and it is the speaker who is then "left there beside the kings of Persia". Michael is explicitly Israel's prince (10:21 "your prince"; 12:1). The canon's spliced sentence puts Michael beside the kings of Persia and its commentary makes him the helper of the Persians — the opposite alignment. The Hebrew does support a general idea the canon uses (nations each have a non-human śar), but with Michael on Israel's side. No reference is printed for this quotation.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] Some ancient versions read "I left him there" for the MT "I was left there"; that variant would put Michael with the kings of Persia but still as an opponent of Persia's prince. Not checked in the library.

items.canon_french: «Beaucoup de ceux qui dorment dans la terre de la poussière se réveilleront : ceux-ci pour la vie éternelle, ceux-là pour la honte, pour l’horreur éternelle».

reading_quotes.french: Le «jugement dernier» permettra aux grands hommes de revivre
tous les mauvais hommes auront honte devant leurs juges, mais vivront dans le regret éternel en exemple pour l’humanité

items.reading_summary: The "last judgement" is a future (scientific) re-creation of great men; the good are welcomed, the bad live on in shame as an example.

load_bearing.gloss: and many from among the sleepers of
load_bearing.comment: Partitive "many of", not all: consistent with a selective revival.

load_bearing.gloss: ground of dust
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

load_bearing.gloss: to life of ʿôlām (age-long / everlasting)
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

load_bearing.gloss: to abhorrence of ʿôlām
load_bearing.comment: dērāʾôn is others' abhorrence of them — fits the canon's "en exemple pour l'humanité".

items.analysis: A selective awakening ("many of") of the dead from the ground to two lasting fates is the Hebrew, rendered literally. "Great men" and the technical means are the canon's; dērāʾôn (an object of others' abhorrence) does support its "as an example".

items.canon_french: «Les gens intelligents brilleront comme l’éclat du firmament, et ceux qui ont amené beaucoup à la justice, comme les étoiles (...)».

reading_quotes.french: Les génies seront les plus estimés et les plus récompensés

items.reading_summary: Geniuses will be the most esteemed and rewarded; the just who helped them, also.

load_bearing.gloss: the insightful / those who give insight (hiphil participle of śkl)
load_bearing.comment: maśkîl is "one who has, or imparts, understanding" — a teacher-sage term; "gens intelligents" moves it toward native intelligence, and the canon's "génies" moves it further.

load_bearing.gloss: like the brightness of the rāqîaʿ
load_bearing.comment: rāqîaʿ = "firmament" here, "plateforme" at Ezek 1:22 (C-016).

ellipsis.cut: "for ever and ever" (לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד).

items.analysis: The step maśkîlîm → "gens intelligents" → "génies" is carried by the French: the Hebrew participle denotes the wise who instruct (parallel to "those who turn many to righteousness"), a moral-didactic category rather than high intellect. The shining reward is original.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] The sense "instructors" for maśkîlîm in Daniel 11-12 is a standard scholarly reading not stated in the library note for this verse.

items.canon_french: «Et toi, Daniel, garde secrètes ces paroles et scelle le livre jusqu’au temps de la fin. Beaucoup chercheront çà et là, et la connaissance s’accroîtra».

reading_quotes.french: Ces paroles ne pourront effectivement être comprises que quand l’homme sera parvenu à un niveau de connaissances scientifiques suffisant, c’est-à-dire maintenant

items.reading_summary: The words are sealed until humanity reaches a sufficient scientific level — now.

load_bearing.french: scelle le livre jusqu’au temps de la fin
load_bearing.gloss: and seal the book until the time of the end
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

load_bearing.gloss: and the knowledge will increase
load_bearing.comment: daʿaṯ with the article; rendered "connaissance" here but "science" at Jer 10:14 and Ps 139:6 (same noun).

load_bearing.gloss: many will roam / range to and fro
load_bearing.comment: šwṭ polel "rove about"; "chercheront" (search) is interpretive of a verb of motion; same verb as the "eyes" that range the earth in Zech 4:10.

items.analysis: The reading's two pillars — sealing "until the time of the end" and an increase of knowledge then — are both explicit in the Hebrew; this is one of the strongest textual hooks in the slice and owes nothing to the French. "Scientific" is the canon's specification of daʿaṯ. The French "chercheront" slightly intellectualises a verb of roaming.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] The Old Greek of this verse is reported to read differently (evil/unrighteousness increasing rather than knowledge); not checked in the library.

items.canon_french: «Lorsque s’achèvera l’écrasement de la force du peuple saint».

reading_quotes.french: Lorsque le peuple d’Israël retrouvera son pays après la longue dispersion. L’état d’Israël fut créé voici quelques dizaines d’années

items.reading_summary: The end of the "crushing of the power of the holy people" = Israel regaining its land (1948), coinciding with the scientific explosion.

load_bearing.french: Lorsque s’achèvera l’écrasement de la force du peuple saint
load_bearing.gloss: and at the completing of the shattering of the hand of the holy people
load_bearing.comment: Literal ("force" = yaḏ "hand"). The Hebrew is ambiguous between "when the shattering is over" (canon) and "when the shattering has been carried through to the end".

ellipsis.cut: Unmarked: the man in linen above the river, his oath, "for a time, times and a half", and the apodosis "all these things shall be finished".
ellipsis.note: The time formula is omitted; the canon supplies its own date.

items.analysis: The clause is literally the Hebrew. The canon takes kallôṯ as the cessation of the shattering (hence restoration); the Hebrew equally allows completion of the shattering as the low point. The identification with 1948 is supplied.

items.canon_french: «Va, Daniel, car ces paroles sont secrètes et scellées jusqu’aux temps de la fin».

reading_quotes.french: Tout cela ne pourra être compris qu’à cette époque-là. Maintenant, tout cela peut être compris

items.reading_summary: The sealed words become understandable in the present scientific age.

load_bearing.french: secrètes et scellées jusqu’aux temps de la fin
load_bearing.gloss: the words are shut up and sealed until the time of the end
load_bearing.comment: Literal; Hebrew "time" is singular (French plural "aux temps").

items.french_variance: "jusqu’au temps de la fin" (12:4, TBWTT-3:222) vs "jusqu’aux temps de la fin" (12:9, TBWTT-3:226) for the identical Hebrew ʿaḏ-ʿēṯ qēṣ.
items.analysis: Literal Hebrew; the identification of "the time of the end" with the present is the canon's.

items.ref_note: Hebrew numbering (2:1), as in Dhorme-type scholarly translations; English Bibles number it 1:17. The library note records this.
items.canon_french: «Iahvé commanda à un grand poisson d’avaler Jonas et Jonas fut dans les entrailles du poisson trois jours et trois nuits».

reading_quotes.french: en réalité un sous-marin comme vous les connaissez maintenant
Dans ce sous-marin, les créateurs peuvent s’entretenir avec Jonas et se tenir au courant de l’évolution des événements politiques de l’époque

items.reading_summary: The "great fish" is a submarine in which the creators talk with Jonah.

load_bearing.french: Iahvé commanda à un grand poisson
load_bearing.gloss: and YHWH appointed / assigned / provided a great fish
load_bearing.comment: mnh piel is "appoint, assign, make ready" with the fish as direct object — YHWH provides a fish; he does not address it. "commanda à" turns provision into an order to an agent. (At 2:11 the Hebrew does have speech: wayyōʾmer.)

load_bearing.gloss: in the inward parts of the fish
load_bearing.comment: mēʿîm is "inner parts, belly"; dāḡ is the ordinary word for fish.

load_bearing.gloss: to swallow Jonah
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

ellipsis.note: What happens inside is given in 2:2-10: Jonah prays "from the belly of the fish ... out of the belly of Sheol"; no conversation is narrated.

items.analysis: Nothing in the Hebrew nouns suggests a vessel (dāḡ "fish", mēʿîm "innards", blʿ "swallow"). One verb is more favourable than the French: wayәman means YHWH "appointed/provided" a great fish — language of furnishing a thing for a purpose — where the French "commanda à" treats the fish as a creature taking orders. The canon's account of what took place inside (discussion of politics) replaces the Hebrew's psalm of distress (2:2-10).
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] Whether Dhorme has "commanda" for wayәman has not been collated.

items.ref_note: Hebrew numbering (2:11 = English 2:10).
items.canon_french: «Alors Iahvé commanda au poisson et celui-ci cracha

reading_quotes.french: Le sous-marin s’est approché près du rivage et Jonas est revenu sur la terre ferme

items.reading_summary: The submarine came inshore and put Jonah back on land.

load_bearing.gloss: and YHWH said to the fish
load_bearing.comment: Plain verb of speech; the French uses "commanda" for both this verb and the different verb of 2:1.

load_bearing.gloss: and it vomited Jonah onto the dry land
load_bearing.comment: qyʾ is "vomit", a bodily verb; "cracha" (spat) is milder and less organic.

ellipsis.note: Quotation split over 3:231-232.

items.french_variance: "commanda" renders two different Hebrew verbs (wayәman 2:1; wayyōʾmer 2:11).
items.analysis: Speech addressed to the fish (a hook for "a crew receiving instructions") is in the Hebrew. The disembarkation verb is biological in Hebrew — the fish vomits him — and Dhorme-style "cracha" softens it; the Hebrew is thus slightly less hospitable to the submarine than the French.

items.canon_french: «Je recommençai à lever les yeux et j’eus une vision : et voici un rouleau volant (...) d’une longueur de vingt coudées

reading_quotes.french: Dans Zacharie V, il y a encore la description d’un engin volant

items.reading_summary: The flying scroll, 9 m by 4.5 m, is a flying craft.

load_bearing.gloss: a flying scroll
load_bearing.comment: mәḡillāh is a written scroll (the same word as Ezek 2:9, where the canon accepts it as a book); ʿāp̄āh "flying" is literal.

load_bearing.original: אָרְכָּהּ֙ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים בָּֽאַמָּ֔ה וְרָחְבָּ֖הּ עֶ֥שֶׂר בָּאַמָּֽה׃
load_bearing.translit: ʾorkāh ʿeśrîm bāʾammāh wәroḥbāh ʿeśer bāʾammāh
load_bearing.gloss: its length twenty by the cubit and its breadth ten by the cubit
load_bearing.comment: Dimensions are the Hebrew; the metric equivalents "(9 mètres)", "(4,50 mètres)" are inserted inside the canon's quotation marks.

load_bearing.gloss: this is the curse that goes out over the face of the whole land
load_bearing.comment: Unquoted next verse: the interpreting messenger says what the object is — a curse (ʾālāh) written on both sides against thieves and perjurers.

ellipsis.cut: In v.2 "And he said to me, What do you see? And I said, I see a flying scroll"; the quotation ends before v.3-4, the explanation of the scroll.
ellipsis.note: The explanation in v.3 identifies the object as a written curse.

items.french_variance: mәḡillāh is taken as a real book at Ezek 2:9 (TBWTT-3:170-171) and as a craft here.
items.analysis: A flying object with stated dimensions is the Hebrew (and the 2:1 ratio is real), but the noun is "scroll" — the same mәḡillāh the canon reads as an ordinary book in Ezek 2:9 — and the text explains it in the next verse as a curse-document going out over the land. The reading requires stopping at v.2. The parenthetical metres are the canon's insertion within the quotation.

load_bearing.original: וַתִּשֶּׂ֙אנָה֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֵיפָ֔ה בֵּ֥ין הָאָ֖רֶץ וּבֵ֥ין הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
load_bearing.translit: wattiśśeʾnāh ʾeṯ-hāʾêp̄āh bên hāʾāreṣ ûḇên haššāmāyim
load_bearing.gloss: and they lifted the ephah between the earth and the skies
load_bearing.comment: Unquoted end of the verse: the women carry a container aloft "between earth and sky" — the same phrase as Ezek 8:3.

ellipsis.cut: Before: "Then I lifted up my eyes and saw". After (unmarked): "and they lifted up the ephah between the earth and the skies". Context vv.5-8, 10-11: the ephah holds a woman named "Wickedness" (זֹאת הָרִשְׁעָה), carried to Shinar.
ellipsis.note: The women are transport agents for a symbolic cargo; the cut end of the verse is also the most "aeronautical" clause.

items.analysis: Two winged women in flight are the Hebrew, literally rendered. The original cuts both ways beyond the quotation: the omitted clause has them airlifting a container "between earth and sky" (more favourable than what is quoted), while the surrounding verses make the scene an allegory of Wickedness being removed to Shinar (less favourable). "Companions of the creators" and the suits are supplied.
