items.canon_french: «Tu l’as fait de peu inférieur aux Elohim».

reading_quotes.french: Les hommes sont presque aussi forts, intellectuellement, que leurs créateurs. Ils n’ont pas osé écrire, ceux qui ont recopié, égal aux Elohim comme cela avait été dicté

items.reading_summary: Humans are almost the intellectual equals of their creators; the original dictation said "equal to the Elohim" and the copyists weakened it.

load_bearing.gloss: and you made him lack a little from ʾĕlōhîm
load_bearing.comment: The comparison term is ʾĕlōhîm itself, without article; the French keeps the word and adds a plural article ("aux"). Versions that put "angels" here do not render the Hebrew word.

ellipsis.cut: Unmarked: v.6b "and with glory (kāḇôḏ) and honour you crown him".
ellipsis.note: Note kāḇôḏ in the omitted half.

items.analysis: The comparison of the human with ʾĕlōhîm (not with angels) is the Hebrew wording and Dhorme keeps it; the plural article "aux" is the French's resolution of an anarthrous noun. The claim that the dictated original read "equal" has no support in the Hebrew text or, per the library note, in any manuscript or ancient version; the Hebrew verb ḥsr piel ("cause to lack") states a shortfall. Addressee of "Tu" is YHWH (v.2), a singular who made the human less than ʾĕlōhîm.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] The Septuagint/Vulgate "angels" at this verse is general knowledge; the library note quoted here does not state it.

items.ref_note: Hebrew numbering (19:7 = English 19:6). Verses quoted in reverse order (7, then 5).
items.canon_french: «(...) son point de départ est à un bout des cieux et son orbite à l’autre bout...».

reading_quotes.french: Les créateurs sont venus d’une planète très éloignée de l’orbite terrestre

items.reading_summary: The creators came from a planet very far from Earth's orbit.

load_bearing.french: son point de départ est à un bout des cieux
load_bearing.gloss: from the end of the skies is his going-forth
load_bearing.comment: "his" refers to the sun (šemeš, v.5), compared in v.6 to a bridegroom leaving his chamber. miqṣēh haššāmayim is the phrase of Isa 13:5 ("des confins du ciel").

load_bearing.gloss: and his circuit (turning-round) to their ends
load_bearing.comment: tәqûp̄āh is a "going round, circuit, turn (of the year/day)"; "orbite" is a modern astronomical term, which the commentary picks up ("l'orbite terrestre").

load_bearing.gloss: and he is like a bridegroom coming out of his chamber
load_bearing.comment: v.6 (unquoted): the antecedent of "son" is the sun.

ellipsis.cut: The opening "(...)" hides the subject (the sun, vv.5c-6); the closing "..." drops "and nothing is hidden from his heat" (וְאֵין נִסְתָּר מֵחַמָּתוֹ).
ellipsis.note: Both cuts remove the words that identify the subject as the sun (its tent, its heat).

items.french_variance: miqṣēh haššāmayim = "des confins du ciel" (Isa 13:5) vs "à un bout des cieux" (Ps 19:7).
items.analysis: In Hebrew the sentence describes the sun's daily course from one horizon to the other; the antecedent (v.5c "for the sun", v.6 "he is like a bridegroom") and the closing "nothing is hidden from his heat" are exactly what the two ellipses remove. The astronomical colour comes from the French "orbite" for tәqûp̄āh ("circuit"). The canon quotes v.7 before v.5 and gives each its own reference. The phrase miqṣēh haššāmayim here is identical to the "confins du ciel" of Isa 13:5 that the canon calls "on ne pouvait être plus clair": in Ps 19 it is the point on the horizon where the sun rises.

items.ref_note: Hebrew numbering (19:5 = English 19:4).
items.canon_french: «Pour le soleil, il a dressé une tente sur la mer (...)».

reading_quotes.french: Nouvelle allusion à l’amas de terre qui fut créé quand l’océan recouvrait la Terre et forma le continent originel

items.reading_summary: An allusion to the land-mass raised when ocean covered the Earth (the original continent).

load_bearing.gloss: for the sun he has set a tent in them
load_bearing.comment: MT bāhem "in them" (the skies). "sur la mer" translates a conjectural emendation (bayyām); the word "sea" is not in the Hebrew text.

ellipsis.cut: Unmarked before: v.5ab "Their line has gone out through all the earth, and their words to the end of the world". The "(...)" after covers v.6.
ellipsis.note: With "in them" the tent is in the heavens named in vv.2-5.

items.analysis: The single word the reading rests on — "mer" — is absent from the Masoretic text, which reads bāhem "in them"; the French follows an emendation. This is the purest translation-dependent case in the slice: the reading (a structure on the sea = the first continent) has no foothold in the Hebrew as transmitted. Even in the emended form the "tent" is the sun's.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] That the emendation bayyām is Dhorme's own choice in the Pléiade has not been collated; the library note records only that the canon's French has the emended text.

items.canon_french: «Du haut des cieux Iahvé regarde, il voit tous les fils de l’homme, du lieu de son habitation il observe tous les habitants de la terre (...)».

reading_quotes.french: Les créateurs surveillent de leurs engins volants les agissements de l’humanité comme ils l’ont toujours fait

items.reading_summary: The creators watch humanity from their flying craft.

load_bearing.french: Du haut des cieux Iahvé regarde
load_bearing.gloss: from the skies YHWH looked/looks
load_bearing.comment: Literal ("du haut" is supplied).

load_bearing.french: du lieu de son habitation il observe
load_bearing.gloss: from the fixed place of his sitting/dwelling he gazes
load_bearing.comment: māḵôn is a fixed, established place or base (root kwn "be firm"); it suits a permanent residence better than a mobile craft.

ellipsis.cut: The "(...)" stands where v.15 follows ("he who forms the hearts of them all").

items.analysis: Observation of all humans from the skies, from an established dwelling-place, is the Hebrew and is literally rendered. "Flying craft" is supplied, and the Hebrew noun māḵôn ("fixed site") points to a stationary seat rather than a vehicle.

items.canon_french: «Il advint un jour que les fils d’Elohim vinrent se présenter devant Iahvé et Satan vint aussi parmi eux».

reading_quotes.french: Elohim, cela veut dire littéralement «venus du ciel» en Hébreu. Les fils d’Elohim, donc les créateurs qui surveillent les hommes, font régulièrement des rapports sur leur planète d’origine
Mais l’un d’entre eux nommé Satan, fait partie de ceux qui ont toujours condamné la création d’autres êtres intelligents
le gouvernement triomphe devant l’opposition : «Satan»

items.reading_summary: The "sons of Elohim" are the creators who monitor humans and report periodically to the home planet; "Satan" is one of them, of the party opposed to creating humans; Iahvé is the government, Satan the opposition.

load_bearing.gloss: the sons of THE Elohim (with article)
load_bearing.comment: The Hebrew has the definite article, marking hāʾĕlōhîm as a definite class or body; "sons of" is the idiom for members of a class. The French drops the article.

load_bearing.gloss: and the adversary also came in their midst
load_bearing.comment: haśśāṭān has the article: a title or role ("the adversary/accuser"), not a personal name. French "Satan" (and the canon's "nommé Satan") makes it a name; the canon's own gloss "l'opposition" matches the Hebrew common noun.

load_bearing.gloss: to station themselves before/over-against YHWH
load_bearing.comment: hityaṣṣēḇ ʿal is court language for attendants presenting themselves to a superior: a periodic audience is the Hebrew scene.

load_bearing.french: les créateurs qui surveillent les hommes
load_bearing.gloss: from roaming on the earth and walking about on it
load_bearing.comment: Unquoted v.7: the adversary reports that he has come from ranging over the earth (šwṭ, the verb of the "eyes" in Zech 4:10) — a patrol-and-report detail the canon does not cite.

items.analysis: The scene the canon describes — a plurality of beings of the Elohim class reporting to a presiding YHWH, with an opposition figure among them — is the plain narrative of the Hebrew. Two details of the original are more favourable than the French: the article in bәnê hāʾĕlōhîm (a definite body, "the Elohim") and the article in haśśāṭān (an office, "the adversary", which is the canon's own "l'opposition"); a third, the adversary's roving inspection of the earth (v.7), is unquoted. Less favourable: haśśāṭān is not a name ("nommé Satan"), and the gloss "venus du ciel" is not a lexical meaning of ʾĕlōhîm (core woh-claim-0009). YHWH here is one individual distinct from the sons of the Elohim; "the government" is the canon's reading.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] The court-audience sense of hityaṣṣēḇ ʿal is a standard lexicon/commentary statement, not taken from a library note.

items.canon_french: «Satan répondit à Iahvé et dit : «Est-ce gratuitement que Job craint Elohim ? (...) veuille étendre ta main et frapper tout ce qui est à lui. A coup sûr il maudira ta face ! et Iahvé dit à «Satan»: «Voici que tout ce qui est à lui est à ta discrétion ! Sur lui seulement n’étends pas ta main !».

reading_quotes.french: donne les pleins pouvoirs à Satan afin qu’il ruine Job. on verra bien alors s’il vénère encore ses créateurs. C’est pour cela qu’il ne faut pas le tuer

items.reading_summary: The government gives the opposition full powers to ruin Job as a test of whether he still reveres his creators; he must not be killed.

load_bearing.french: Est-ce gratuitement que Job craint Elohim
load_bearing.gloss: is it for nothing that Job fears Elohim?
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

load_bearing.gloss: in your hand
load_bearing.comment: "à ta discrétion" is an administrative paraphrase of "in your hand"; it suits "pleins pouvoirs".

load_bearing.gloss: to your face he will "bless" you
load_bearing.comment: The Hebrew verb is brk "bless", a scribal euphemism for "curse"; the French translates the intended sense.

load_bearing.french: frapper tout ce qui est à lui
load_bearing.gloss: and touch all that is his
load_bearing.comment: ngʿ "touch"; "frapper" is stronger.

ellipsis.cut: v.10 (the protective "hedge" around Job and his prosperity) and v.12b ("and the adversary went out from before YHWH").

items.french_variance: The quotation marks around «Satan» appear only the second time the name occurs in the quotation.
items.analysis: Delegated authority with a stated limit ("only against him do not put out your hand") is the Hebrew text; the political vocabulary (government, opposition, full powers) is the canon's, assisted by Dhorme's "à ta discrétion" for "in your hand". Nothing technological is read in.

items.canon_french: «Le voici à ta discrétion ! Sauvegarde seulement sa vie !».

reading_quotes.french: Le gouvernement lui donne carte blanche à condition qu’il ne le tue pas

items.reading_summary: The government gives the opposition carte blanche provided Job is not killed.

load_bearing.gloss: behold him in your hand
only guard his nep̄eš (life)
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

ellipsis.cut: Unmarked: "YHWH said to the adversary".

items.analysis: Literal Hebrew; the reading only restates it in political terms.

items.canon_french: «(...) étendras-tu, avec lui, des nuages, solides comme un miroir de métal fondu ?».

reading_quotes.french: Est-ce que l’homme est capable de faire des «nuages solides», des engins volants métalliques en réalité

items.reading_summary: "Solid clouds" like a mirror of cast metal are metallic flying craft, thought impossible for anyone but God.

load_bearing.gloss: will you beat out / hammer flat (hiphil of rqʿ)
load_bearing.comment: rqʿ is the metal-worker's verb ("beat out into a sheet") and the root of rāqîaʿ "firmament/plateforme". "étendras" keeps only the spreading; the Hebrew verb already implies working something solid like metal.

load_bearing.gloss: the šәḥāqîm: clouds / the skies (poetic plural)
load_bearing.comment: šәḥāqîm means both "(fine) clouds" and "the skies"; the canon's English has "the sky", its French "des nuages" (library note: "the canon itself is divided"). As "the skies" the verse describes the firmament itself.

load_bearing.french: solides comme un miroir de métal fondu
load_bearing.gloss: strong/hard as a cast mirror
load_bearing.comment: mûṣāq "cast, poured (metal)" and rәʾî "mirror" are literal; ancient mirrors were cast bronze. "solides" for ḥăzāqîm "strong, hard" is fair.

load_bearing.gloss: with him
load_bearing.comment: "Him" is God (El, 37:14-16); the speaker is Elihu.

ellipsis.cut: The opening "(...)" covers nothing of v.18 (the verse begins with the verb); it stands for the preceding context.

items.french_variance: Canon French "des nuages, solides" vs canon English "the sky, which is strong" (library note).
items.analysis: The metallic hook is stronger in Hebrew than in the French the canon quotes: the verb is rqʿ, "to hammer out (metal)", and the comparison is to a cast-metal mirror, hard (ḥăzāqîm). What the Hebrew leaves open is the object: šәḥāqîm is "clouds" (canon's French, library line) or "the skies" (canon's English), and with the latter the verse is the standard picture of a solid sky-vault spread by God, not of discrete objects. The plural indefinite "des nuages" (some clouds = craft) is a French reading of a Hebrew definite poetic plural (lišḥāqîm, with article).
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] That ancient mirrors were cast bronze is general knowledge.

items.ref_note: Deuterocanonical book; the library holds the Greek. The quotation follows the short Greek text (library note).
items.canon_french: «Tous les jours je me rendais visible pour vous ; je ne mangeais ni ne buvais (...) je remonte vers celui qui m’a envoyé, et écrivez dans un livre tout ce qui s’est accompli».

reading_quotes.french: l’un des robots des créateurs, nommé Raphaël, vient aussi éprouver les réactions des humains face à eux

items.reading_summary: Raphael is one of the creators' robots, sent to test human reactions; he does not eat or drink, and returns to his sender.

load_bearing.french: je ne mangeais ni ne buvais
load_bearing.gloss: I did not eat nor drink
load_bearing.comment: Literal: the non-eating that suggests a "robot" is in the Greek.

load_bearing.french: je me rendais visible pour vous
load_bearing.gloss: I was letting myself be seen by you
load_bearing.comment: Literal middle.

load_bearing.gloss: but you were beholding a vision
load_bearing.comment: The clause removed by the canon's ellipsis: the Greek explains the non-eating as appearance (a "vision"), not as the nature of a machine.

load_bearing.french: je remonte vers celui qui m’a envoyé
load_bearing.gloss: I am going up to the one who sent me
load_bearing.comment: A sent agent returning upward to a singular sender: literal. "re-" is added in French.

ellipsis.cut: "but you were seeing a vision" (12:19c) and "And now give thanks to God, for" (12:20a).
ellipsis.note: The first cut removes the text's own explanation of why he seemed to eat (in the Greek he only appeared to); the second removes "God".

items.analysis: Greek, not Hebrew. The three hooks — a being who neither ate nor drank, who "made himself visible", and who returns upward to "the one who sent me" — are all in the Greek short text and literally rendered. "Robot" is the canon's inference from the non-eating; the Greek gives a different explanation in the very clause the ellipsis removes ("you were seeing a vision"), and calls the figure an angelos (12:15, outside the quotation). The stated purpose "éprouver" is not in the text quoted (library note: nearest is the long-text clause at 12:13).

items.canon_french: «Ce qu’est la Sagesse et comment elle est née, je le ferai savoir ; je ne vous cacherai aucun secret, mais je remonterai jusqu’au début de sa genèse et mettrai en lumière sa connaissance sans passer à côté de la vérité».

reading_quotes.french: la «sagesse», la science qui a permis à tout cela d’exister, sera connue de l’homme en temps voulu

items.reading_summary: "Wisdom" is the science that made the creation possible; it will be made known to humanity in due time.

load_bearing.gloss: wisdom
load_bearing.comment: Literal; no capital in Greek.

load_bearing.gloss: mysteries
load_bearing.comment: Literal sense kept.

load_bearing.original: θήσω εἰς τὸ ἐμφανὲς τὴν γνῶσιν αὐτῆς
load_bearing.translit: thēsō eis to emphanes tēn gnōsin autēs
load_bearing.gloss: I will set the knowledge of her in the open
load_bearing.comment: Literal: a promised disclosure of knowledge.

items.analysis: The promise to disclose the origin of wisdom and hide no mysteries is the Greek; equating sophia with the creators' science, and the speaker's promise (Solomon to his readers) with a future revelation, is the canon's. Nothing depends on the French.

items.canon_french: «Car en partant de la grandeur et de la beauté des créatures on contemple par analogie leur auteur».

reading_quotes.french: Il était pourtant simple de voir la vérité, reconnaître les créateurs en observant la chose créée

items.reading_summary: One could have recognised the creators by observing the created thing.

load_bearing.gloss: their originator / maker of their coming-to-be (singular)
load_bearing.comment: Singular in Greek and in French; the commentary's "les créateurs" is plural.

load_bearing.gloss: of created things
load_bearing.comment: Literal: things explicitly called "made/created".

load_bearing.gloss: proportionately, by analogy
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

items.analysis: Greek. Inference from made things to a maker is exactly the Greek argument (ktismata → genesiourgos). The maker is singular, and the surrounding passage (13:1-9) argues against taking fire, wind, stars or the luminaries of heaven for gods; the plural "créateurs" is the canon's.

items.canon_french: «Ils n’ont pas été capables de connaître d’après les biens visibles. Celui qui est».

reading_quotes.french: reconnaître les créateurs en observant la chose créée

items.reading_summary: Men failed to recognise the creators from visible things.

load_bearing.gloss: the one who is (masc. sg. participle)
load_bearing.comment: Singular; an allusion to the divine self-designation of Exod 3:14 in Greek.

load_bearing.gloss: from the good things that are seen
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

ellipsis.cut: Unmarked: the opening "For vain by nature were all people in whom there was ignorance of God" and the closing "nor, by attending to the works, did they recognize the craftsman" (τὸν τεχνίτην).
ellipsis.note: The omitted last clause has technitēs "craftsman/artificer" — a maker-as-technician word the canon does not quote in French (its English edition does, as "workmaster").

items.french_variance: French quotes clause 2 of the verse; the English edition quotes clause 3 plus "he that is" (library note).
items.analysis: Greek. The quoted clause is literal, though the full stop before "Celui qui est" breaks the syntax (in Greek "him who is" is the object of "know"). The unquoted remainder of the verse calls the maker ho technitēs, "the craftsman", which is closer to the canon's engineer-creators than anything in the French it prints; the canon's English edition quotes that clause instead. Number is singular throughout.

items.canon_french: «En ce jour-là, Iahvé sévira avec sa dure, grande et forte épée contre Léviathan, le serpent fuyard, (...) et il tuera le dragon qui est dans la mer».

reading_quotes.french: Les créateurs bannis du début se cachaient sous les océans
Le gouvernement de la planète voulait à cette époque détruire les créateurs des hommes

items.reading_summary: Leviathan / the dragon in the sea = the banished creators (the "serpent" group) hiding in undersea bases; Iahvé = the home-planet government that wanted to destroy them.

load_bearing.gloss: Leviathan, fleeing serpent
load_bearing.comment: nāḥāš is the word of Gen 3:1; the canon's identification of the sea-creature with the "serpent" faction rests on a lexical identity that is in the Hebrew. "fuyard" for bārîaḥ fits "banished/hiding" slightly better than the Hebrew adjective requires.

load_bearing.french: le dragon qui est dans la mer
load_bearing.gloss: the tannin that is in the sea
load_bearing.comment: tannîn is the word of Gen 1:21 (tannînîm); Dhorme's "dragon" in both places is recorded in core (woh-claim-0073). Singular, with article.

load_bearing.gloss: YHWH will visit / punish
load_bearing.comment: Imperfect (future) "in that day"; the canon narrates it as a past policy ("voulait à cette époque").

ellipsis.cut: "and against Leviathan the twisting serpent" (וְעַל לִוְיָתָן נָחָשׁ עֲקַלָּתוֹן).
ellipsis.note: The second Leviathan epithet; its removal makes one creature of what the Hebrew parallelism names twice (or as two).

items.analysis: The reading's lexical chain is original: nāḥāš (the Eden serpent word) and tannîn (the Gen 1:21 "dragons" word) both stand in the Hebrew verse, the creature is located "in the sea", and YHWH is its enemy. Dhorme's French transmits all three faithfully, so nothing here is translation-dependent. What the Hebrew does not give is plurality (one or two monsters, grammatically singular) or a past tense: the verse is an eschatological future.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] The Ugaritic parallel (ltn bṯn brḥ) is in the library's interpretive note for this verse, not in the canon.

items.canon_french: «(...) on donne l’écrit à quelqu’un qui ne connaît pas l’écriture, en disant : «lis donc ceci» ; mais il dit : «je ne connais pas l’écriture».

reading_quotes.french: ils ne pouvaient pas la comprendre avant de «savoir lire», d’être suffisamment évolués scientifiquement

items.reading_summary: Humanity has long held the truth (the scriptures) but could not "read" it until scientifically advanced.

load_bearing.gloss: I do not know writing / (a) book
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

load_bearing.gloss: and the scroll/book is given
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

ellipsis.cut: The opening "(...)" stands where v.11 would be: "the vision of all this has become for you like the words of a sealed book (הַסֵּפֶר הֶחָתוּם) ... 'I cannot, for it is sealed'".
ellipsis.note: v.11 says explicitly that the image is a simile for an un-understood vision, and that the book is sealed — the motif the canon uses from Dan 12:4, 9.

items.analysis: The illiteracy image is the Hebrew text. The verse the canon skipped (29:11) is more favourable to its reading than the one it quotes: it states in so many words that the prophetic vision has become "like the words of a sealed book" that even a literate man cannot read, which is the canon's thesis (truth held but unreadable) and ties to Daniel's "sealed" (same root ḥtm). The equation reading = scientific maturity is the canon's.

items.canon_french: «Tout homme est abruti, faute de science (...)».

reading_quotes.french: ils ne pouvaient pas la comprendre avant de «savoir lire», d’être suffisamment évolués scientifiquement
Cette science qui a permis aux créateurs de créer et permettra aux hommes d’en faire autant

items.reading_summary: Humanity was dull for lack of "science" — the science by which the creators created and humans will too.

load_bearing.gloss: every human is stupid/brutish — from/without knowledge
load_bearing.comment: middaʿaṯ: min is either privative ("without knowledge", French, library line) or causal ("by [his] knowledge", KJV, canon English). daʿaṯ is "knowledge"; "science" in the French carries that older sense, which the commentary then takes as (technical) science.

ellipsis.cut: "every goldsmith is put to shame by his carved image; for his molten image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them".
ellipsis.note: The rest of the verse shows the "knowledge" lacking is knowledge that idols are lifeless: an anti-idol polemic.

items.french_variance: Canon French "faute de science" (privative) vs canon English "brutish in his knowledge" (library note). daʿaṯ = "science" here, "connaissance" at Dan 12:4.
items.analysis: The move from the verse to "Cette science qui a permis aux créateurs de créer" runs through the French word "science". The Hebrew daʿaṯ is general "knowledge", and the continuation (cut) defines the stupidity as idol-making. The privative construal itself is a legitimate reading of the Hebrew.

items.canon_french: «Iahvé m’a créée, principe de sa voie, antérieurement à ses oeuvres, dès lors, dès l’éternité j’ai été formée, dès le début, antérieurement à la terre (...). Quand il établit les cieux, j’étais là (...) quand il imposa à la mer sa limite pour que les eaux ne franchissent pas son bord (...) j’étais à son côté, comme architecte, et j’étais dans les délices (...) jouant sur le sol de la terre, et mes délices sont avec les fils d’homme».

reading_quotes.french: L’intelligence et la science, c’est grâce à ces deux vertus que les créateurs ont pu créer la «terre ferme», le continent unique et les êtres vivants qu’ils ont mis dessus

items.reading_summary: Wisdom = the intelligence and science by which the creators made the dry land and its living beings, and which now leads humans to repeat the act.

load_bearing.gloss: crux: "master-workman/artisan" or "nursling, one brought up"
load_bearing.comment: The technical sense rests on one of two standing construals of a hapax-like word; the canon's English has the other ("as one brought up with him").

load_bearing.gloss: YHWH acquired / begot / created me
load_bearing.comment: qnh: "acquire, possess" or "create"; French "créée", canon English "possessed".

load_bearing.french: quand il imposa à la mer sa limite
load_bearing.gloss: when he set for the sea its decree/limit
load_bearing.comment: Literal; the sea-boundary motif the canon links with the "terre ferme".

load_bearing.french: jouant sur le sol de la terre
load_bearing.gloss: playing in the inhabited world of his earth
load_bearing.comment: Literal apart from "sol".

ellipsis.cut: vv.24-26, 27b ("when he inscribed a circle on the face of the deep"), 28, 29b ("when he marked out the foundations of the earth"), 30b.
ellipsis.note: The cut 27b and 29b are the most "engineering" clauses (ḥûḡ "circle", ḥqq "inscribe/mark out").

items.french_variance: Canon French "créée" / "architecte" vs canon English "possessed" / "as one brought up with him" (library notes).
items.analysis: That wisdom was present and active at the making of sky, sea-limit and earth is the Hebrew text. The specifically technical word "architecte" is one of two established readings of ʾāmôn, and the canon's two language editions take opposite sides. The maker is singular (YHWH). The omitted half-verses (27b, 29b) contain drafting verbs — "inscribing a circle", "marking out foundations" — that would have served the reading better than some of what is quoted.

items.canon_french: «Ce qui déjà fut est et ce qui doit être a déjà été (...)».

reading_quotes.french: Depuis le début des temps il en est ainsi, les hommes créent d’autres hommes, semblables à eux-mêmes, sur d’autres mondes. Le cycle continue

items.reading_summary: The cycle of creators creating creators: what is to be has already been.

load_bearing.french: Ce qui déjà fut est et ce qui doit être a déjà été
load_bearing.original: מַה־שֶּֽׁהָיָה֙ כְּבָ֣ר ה֔וּא וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר לִהְי֖וֹת כְּבָ֣ר הָיָ֑ה
load_bearing.translit: mah-ššehāyāh kәḇār hûʾ waʾăšer lihyôṯ kәḇār hāyāh
load_bearing.gloss: what has been — already it is; and what is to be already has been
load_bearing.comment: Literal in the word-order construal.

ellipsis.cut: "and the Elohim seeks what has been driven away" (וְהָאֱלֹהִים יְבַקֵּשׁ אֶת־נִרְדָּף).
ellipsis.note: The omitted clause has hāʾĕlōhîm with article and a SINGULAR verb.

items.analysis: Recurrence ("what is to be has already been") is the Hebrew; applying it to successive creations of humanities is the canon's. The omitted clause is an example of hāʾĕlōhîm (with article) governing a singular verb.

items.canon_french: «La supériorité de l’homme sur la bête est nulle, car tout est vanité».

reading_quotes.french: Les animaux eux aussi ont été créés et seront recréés. Tout comme l’homme ni plus, ni moins

items.reading_summary: Animals too were created and will be re-created, exactly like man.

load_bearing.french: La supériorité de l’homme sur la bête est nulle
load_bearing.gloss: and the advantage of the human over the beast is nothing
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

load_bearing.original: כְּמ֥וֹת זֶה֙ כֵּ֣ן מ֣וֹת זֶ֔ה וְר֥וּחַ אֶחָ֖ד לַכֹּ֑ל
load_bearing.translit: kәmôṯ zeh kēn môṯ zeh wәrûaḥ ʾeḥāḏ lakkōl
load_bearing.gloss: as this one dies so dies that one, and all have one rûaḥ
load_bearing.comment: Unquoted first part of the verse: the stated ground of equality is common death and one breath.

ellipsis.cut: Unmarked: v.19a "For the fate of the sons of the human and the fate of the beast is one: as the one dies, so dies the other; they all have one breath".
ellipsis.note: In Hebrew the equality is equality in dying; the canon turns it into equality in being (re)created.

items.analysis: The no-advantage statement is literal Hebrew. Its ground in the same verse (omitted) is shared mortality and a single rûaḥ; re-creation is not in view in either language.

items.canon_french: «Malheur à quiconque récrimine contre Celui qui l’a formé... L’argile dira-t-elle à celui qui la façonne : «que faistu ? ton œuvre n’a pas de valeur!» Malheur à qui dit à son père : «Qu’as-tu engendré ?».

reading_quotes.french: Nous avons peur d’une rancune que nous n’admettrions pas
que vous nous aimiez comme des pères

items.reading_summary: The creators will show themselves only if humanity is grateful for having been made and loves them "as fathers".

load_bearing.gloss: his former/potter (sg. participle of yṣr)
load_bearing.comment: Singular; yṣr is the potter's verb of Gen 2:7. The canon's "créateurs" is plural.

load_bearing.french: ton œuvre n’a pas de valeur
load_bearing.gloss: and your work: "he has no hands"
load_bearing.comment: The French paraphrases a difficult Hebrew clause; not load-bearing for the reading.

load_bearing.gloss: to a father
load_bearing.comment: Hebrew has no possessive ("a father"); the French "son père" personalises it.

ellipsis.cut: The canon's "..." drops "a potsherd among the potsherds of the ground" (חֶרֶשׂ אֶת־חַרְשֵׂי אֲדָמָה); the quotation stops before v.10b "or to a woman: with what are you in labour?" (וּלְאִשָּׁה מַה־תְּחִילִין).
ellipsis.note: The mother half of the parent pair is dropped; the canon keeps only the father.

items.analysis: The maker-as-potter and maker-as-father images are the Hebrew text (yṣr, ʾāḇ), so the hook for "love us as fathers" is original. The former is singular. The Hebrew pairs father with mother (v.10b), which the quotation omits. No technological reading is involved.

items.canon_french: «(...) je t’ai éprouvé dans le creuset du malheur. C’est pour l’amour de moi... que j’ai agi !».

reading_quotes.french: C’est dans la crainte que les hommes n’aiment pas leurs créateurs qu’ils les ont laissé faire tout seuls des progrès scientifiques, presque sans les aider

items.reading_summary: The creators left humans to make scientific progress alone, as a trial, out of fear that humans would not love them.

load_bearing.gloss: I have chosen you (MT)
load_bearing.comment: MT reads bḥr "choose"; "éprouvé" (tested) presupposes bḥn. The library note records the two readings; the canon's English has "chosen". The "trial" sense the commentary needs is in the French, not in the MT wording.

load_bearing.gloss: in the furnace of affliction
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

load_bearing.gloss: for my sake, for my sake
load_bearing.comment: The Hebrew preposition means "for the sake of"; no word for love is present. "pour l'amour de moi" is a French idiom for "for my sake".

load_bearing.gloss: I do / will do (imperfect)
load_bearing.comment: French perfect for a Hebrew imperfect.

ellipsis.cut: v.10a "Behold, I have refined you, but not as silver" (הִנֵּה צְרַפְתִּיךָ וְלֹא בְכָסֶף); the "..." inside v.11 drops the doubled "for my sake"; v.11b "for how should it be profaned? and my glory I will not give to another".

items.french_variance: Canon French "éprouvé" vs canon English "chosen" (library note).
items.analysis: Both words the commentary builds on are French-side. "éprouvé" follows a reading (bḥn) that is not the Masoretic consonantal text printed in the library (bḥr "chosen"), and the "love" of the commentary ("dans la crainte que les hommes n'aiment pas leurs créateurs") echoes "pour l'amour de moi", an idiom rendering ləmaʿănî "for my sake", which has no affective content. The furnace image is original.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] The library note attributes the "tested" reading to 1QIsa-a; whether Dhorme printed "éprouvé" has not been checked.

items.canon_french: «Ne le savez-vous pas, ne l’avez-vous pas entendu, ne vous l’a-t-on pas exposé depuis le commencement ? N’avez-vous pas compris la fondation de la terre ?».

reading_quotes.french: Les origines et le destin des créateurs et des hommes sont semblables et liés

items.reading_summary: An appeal to understand how the Earth was founded (the creation as the creators' work); requoted at TBWTT-5:17.

load_bearing.french: N’avez-vous pas compris la fondation de la terre
load_bearing.gloss: have you not understood (the) foundations of the earth
load_bearing.comment: The MT has no preposition before môsәḏôṯ, so the object construal quoted by the canon is the plain syntax; "from the foundations" (ASV, library line) supplies a preposition. Hebrew noun is plural ("foundations"); French singular "la fondation" makes it an act of founding.

items.analysis: The canon's French takes "the foundations of the earth" as the direct object of "understood", which is what the Masoretic consonants say without supplement; the library's own line supplies "from". On syntax the Hebrew is therefore at least as favourable as the French. The singular "fondation" (an event) for the plural môsәḏôṯ (structures) is a French nuance that helps the "how the earth was founded" reading.

items.canon_french: «... Lui... qui marche sur les hauteurs de la terre».

reading_quotes.french: La trace des bases des créateurs sur les hautes montagnes se trouve dans Amos

items.reading_summary: A trace of the creators' bases on high mountains.

load_bearing.french: qui marche sur les hauteurs de la terre
load_bearing.gloss: and treading upon the heights of (the) earth
load_bearing.comment: Singular participle; bāmŏṯê is the word of Isa 14:14 ("hauteurs de la Nuée").

load_bearing.original: יוֹצֵ֨ר הָרִ֜ים וּבֹרֵ֣א ר֗וּחַ וּמַגִּ֤יד לְאָדָם֙ מַה־שֵּׂח֔וֹ
load_bearing.translit: yôṣēr hārîm ûḇōrēʾ rûaḥ ûmaggîḏ lәʾāḏām mah-śśēḥô
load_bearing.gloss: former of mountains and creator of wind, and declaring to the human what his thought is
load_bearing.comment: Omitted by the canon's "...": includes "declares to man what his (own) thought is" — a mind-reading clause comparable to Ps 139 that the canon does not use.

ellipsis.cut: Everything except one clause: "he who forms the mountains and creates the wind, and declares to man what his thought is; who makes the morning darkness ... YHWH, the God of hosts, is his name".

items.analysis: Treading on the earth's heights is the Hebrew; a single figure walks there, and no installation is mentioned. The omitted clauses of the same verse include one the canon's telepathy theme could have used ("declares to man what his thought is").
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] Whether śēaḥ refers to the human's thought or God's is debated; not in the library note quoted.

items.canon_french: «Quant à ces sept, ce sont les yeux de Iahvé, ceux qui circulent par toute la terre».

reading_quotes.french: Les bases des créateurs étaient au nombre de sept

D’où le chandelier à sept branches dont le sens a été perdu et qui à l’origine était, au Q.G. des créateurs, un central comportant sept témoins lumineux leur permettant de rester en contact avec les autres bases

items.reading_summary: The creators had seven bases; the seven-branched lampstand was originally a console with seven indicator lights linking HQ to the bases and the orbiting ship.

load_bearing.french: ces sept, ce sont les yeux de Iahvé
load_bearing.gloss: these seven are the eyes of YHWH
load_bearing.comment: Literal. "These seven" refers back to the seven lamps of the lampstand in 4:2.

load_bearing.french: ceux qui circulent par toute la terre
load_bearing.gloss: they are ranging to and fro through all the earth
load_bearing.comment: šwṭ polel: mobile, roving observers — same verb as Dan 12:4 "chercheront çà et là" (C-046), rendered differently.

load_bearing.original: מְנוֹרַת֩ זָהָ֨ב כֻּלָּ֜הּ וְגֻלָּ֣הּ עַל־רֹאשָׁ֗הּ וְשִׁבְעָ֤ה נֵרֹתֶ֙יהָ֙ עָלֶ֔יהָ
load_bearing.translit: mәnôraṯ zāhāḇ kullāh wәḡullāh ʿal-rōʾšāh wәšiḇʿāh nērōṯêhā ʿālêhā
load_bearing.gloss: a lampstand all of gold, its bowl on its top, and its seven lamps on it
load_bearing.comment: The lampstand-with-seven-lamps that the "seven eyes" explain is in the same vision (4:2); the canon does not quote it.

ellipsis.cut: Unmarked: v.10a "For who has despised the day of small things? They shall rejoice and see the plummet in the hand of Zerubbabel".

items.french_variance: šwṭ polel = "chercheront çà et là" (Dan 12:4) vs "circulent" (Zech 4:10).
items.analysis: The canon's link between the number seven, YHWH's means of observing the earth, and the lampstand is not its invention: in the Hebrew of this chapter the seven lamps of the golden menorah (4:2) are explained as "the eyes of YHWH ranging through all the earth" (4:10). The canon quotes only the explanation; the unquoted 4:2 makes the lampstand connection explicit. Against "bases": the seven are eyes that rove (mәšôṭәṭîm), not fixed places — the Hebrew supports seven mobile observers or seven lights, not seven sites.

items.ref_note: Hebrew psalm numbering (139 = Greek/Latin 138).
items.canon_french: «Car la parole n’est pas encore sur ma langue, que déjà, Iahvé, tu la connais toute, tu me cernes derrière et devant, puis tu mets la main sur moi. Science trop mystérieuse pour moi, elle est trop haute, je n’y puis atteindre».

reading_quotes.french: En ce qui concerne l’allusion à la télépathie
La télépathie est inimaginable à cette époque «Science trop mystérieuse pour moi»

items.reading_summary: An allusion to telepathy, a "science" unimaginable at the time.

load_bearing.french: la parole n’est pas encore sur ma langue, que déjà, Iahvé, tu la connais toute
load_bearing.original: אֵ֣ין מִ֭לָּה בִּלְשׁוֹנִ֑י הֵ֥ן יְ֝הוָ֗ה יָדַ֥עְתָּ כֻלָּֽהּ׃
load_bearing.translit: ʾên millāh bilšônî hēn YHWH yāḏaʿtā ḵullāh
load_bearing.gloss: there is no word on my tongue — behold, YHWH, you know all of it
load_bearing.comment: The temporal "pas encore ... que déjà" is the French's construal; the Hebrew has "no word on my tongue; behold you know it wholly".

load_bearing.gloss: knowledge (too wonderful) for me
load_bearing.comment: daʿaṯ "knowledge" — here God's knowledge of the psalmist. French "Science" (= knowledge in literary French) is read by the canon as a science/technique. Same noun = "connaissance" in Dan 12:4.

load_bearing.gloss: you discern my thought from afar
load_bearing.comment: Unquoted v.2: knowledge of thought at a distance is stated outright.

ellipsis.cut: None marked; the quotation starts at v.4 and so omits v.2-3.
ellipsis.note: v.2 is the more direct statement.

items.french_variance: daʿaṯ = "Science" (Ps 139:6), "science" (Jer 10:14), "connaissance" (Dan 12:4).
items.analysis: That the addressee knows the psalmist's words unspoken is in the Hebrew of v.4, though the "not yet ... already" sharpening is French. The verse the canon did not quote is stronger for its reading than those it did: v.2 says "you understand my thought from afar" (mērāḥôq). The label "Science" for this knowledge, on which the commentary's closing quotation leans, is a French sense of daʿaṯ "knowledge".

items.ref_note: Hebrew psalm numbering (147:4-5 = Greek/Latin 146:4-5).
items.canon_french: «Il compte le nombre des étoiles, il les appelle toutes par leurs noms. Il est grand, notre Seigneur, et très fort, son intelligence est incalculable».

reading_quotes.french: De même que l’astronomie et les voyages interplanétaires étaient inimaginables eux aussi

items.reading_summary: Astronomy and interplanetary travel, unimaginable then, are attributed to the creators.

load_bearing.french: Il compte le nombre des étoiles
load_bearing.gloss: counting/assigning a number to the stars
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

load_bearing.gloss: to his understanding there is no number
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

load_bearing.gloss: our lord(s) — plural-form ʾăḏōnîm with suffix
load_bearing.comment: A second plural-of-form divine title (like ʾĕlōhîm) that the French renders as a plain singular; the canon does not remark on it.

items.analysis: Counting and naming the stars is the Hebrew; travel between them is not mentioned in either language. Incidentally the Hebrew title ʾăḏônênû is plural in form, a feature invisible in "notre Seigneur".
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] The analysis of ʾăḏônênû as the plural-of-form ʾăḏōnîm + suffix is standard grammar, not from the library note.

items.ref_note: Hebrew psalm numbering (147:15 = Greek/Latin 147:4).
items.canon_french: «Lui qui adresse sa parole à toute la terre, son verbe court à toute vitesse (...)».

reading_quotes.french: La télécommunication non plus ne pouvait pas être comprise à cette époque

items.reading_summary: An allusion to telecommunication.

load_bearing.french: Lui qui adresse sa parole à toute la terre
load_bearing.gloss: who sends his utterance (to) earth
load_bearing.comment: šlḥ "send" (the French "adresse" is weaker); "toute" is not in the Hebrew.

load_bearing.french: son verbe court à toute vitesse
load_bearing.gloss: very swiftly his word runs
load_bearing.comment: Literal: a "sent" word that "runs" at speed.

load_bearing.gloss: he sends his word and melts them
load_bearing.comment: Unquoted vv.16-18: the "word" is the command that brings snow, frost and thaw.

ellipsis.cut: vv.16-18: snow like wool, hoarfrost, ice, "he sends his word and melts them".
ellipsis.note: The continuation makes the swift "word" a command to the weather.

items.analysis: A word that is "sent" to the earth and "runs very swiftly" is the Hebrew image, and šlḥ ("send, dispatch") is if anything closer to transmission than the French "adresse". The following verses (cut) define that word as the command that produces snow and thaw; "à toute la terre" overstates the Hebrew "earth(ward)".

items.ref_note: Hebrew numbering, which the canon follows (library note); English Bibles 5:2-5.
items.canon_french: «(...) Bethléem (...) de toi sortira... celui qui doit être dominateur en Israël et dont les origines sont de toute antiquité, depuis les jours d’antan ! (...). Il sera debout et fera paître par la puissance de Iahvé (...) jusqu’aux confins de la terre, et c’est lui qui sera la Paix».

reading_quotes.french: ils décident d’envoyer un «Messie» qui sera capable de faire en sorte que ce que seul le peuple d’Israël sait, se répande sur toute la Terre
Ils l’annoncent alors

items.reading_summary: The creators announce the Messiah (Jesus) who will spread Israel's knowledge over the whole Earth.

load_bearing.french: dont les origines sont de toute antiquité, depuis les jours d’antan
load_bearing.gloss: and whose goings-forth are from of old, from days of ʿôlām
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

load_bearing.gloss: to the ends of the earth
load_bearing.comment: In Hebrew the subject of this phrase is "he shall be great" (yiḡdal), which the "(...)" removes.

load_bearing.french: c’est lui qui sera la Paix
load_bearing.gloss: and this (one) shall be peace
load_bearing.comment: Capitalised title in French; the Hebrew continues "when Assyria comes into our land".

ellipsis.cut: v.1 "Ephrathah, little to be among the clans of Judah" and "for me"; all of v.2 (given up until she who is in labour has borne); v.3 "in the majesty of the name of YHWH his God; and they shall abide, for now he shall be great"; v.4b the Assyrian invasion and the seven shepherds.
ellipsis.note: The cuts de-historicise the oracle (Assyria) but do not alter the quoted clauses.

items.analysis: A ruler from Bethlehem with ancient origins whose greatness reaches the ends of the earth is the Hebrew. The messianic application is traditional (Matt 2:6); that the creators "announce" a messenger to universalise Israel's knowledge is the canon's framing. No French-only wording is load-bearing.

items.canon_french: «Jubile (...) fille de Jérusalem : voici que ton roi vient vers toi (...) humble et monté sur un âne (...) il dictera la paix aux nations ; son empire s’étendra de la Mer à la Mer».

reading_quotes.french: Ils l’annoncent alors

items.reading_summary: Second announcement of the Messiah.

load_bearing.original: גִּילִ֨י מְאֹ֜ד בַּת־צִיּ֗וֹן הָרִ֙יעִי֙ בַּ֣ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם
load_bearing.translit: gîlî mәʾōḏ baṯ-ṣiyyôn hārîʿî baṯ yәrûšālaim
load_bearing.gloss: rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion; shout, daughter of Jerusalem
load_bearing.comment: The ellipsis joins the first imperative to the second vocative, dropping "Zion".

load_bearing.french: humble et monté sur un âne
load_bearing.gloss: lowly/afflicted and riding on a donkey
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

load_bearing.french: il dictera la paix aux nations
load_bearing.gloss: and he shall speak peace to the nations
load_bearing.comment: "dictera" (dictate) is stronger than dbr "speak".

load_bearing.french: de la Mer à la Mer
load_bearing.gloss: from sea to sea
load_bearing.comment: Literal.

ellipsis.cut: "righteous and saved/victorious is he" (צַדִּיק וְנוֹשָׁע הוּא); "upon a colt, the foal of a donkey"; v.10a "I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim ..."; v.10 end "and from the River to the ends of the earth".
ellipsis.note: The library note records the omission of ṣaddîq wәnôšāʿ.

items.analysis: Traditional messianic proof-text quoted in excerpts; no technological reading and no French-dependent hook.

items.canon_french: «(...) elle se trouva enceinte par l’Esprit saint».

reading_quotes.french: faire naître un enfant issu d’une femme et d’un des leurs

items.reading_summary: The conception is the creators fathering a child with a human woman so that he inherits telepathic faculties.

load_bearing.original: εὑρέθη ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχουσα ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου
load_bearing.translit: heurethē en gastri echousa ek pneumatos hagiou
load_bearing.gloss: was found having in the womb from/out of holy spirit (no article)
load_bearing.comment: French « par » makes the Spirit an agent; Greek ἐκ marks source/origin and is the same preposition the genealogy uses for the mother (1:16 ἐξ ἧς ἐγεννήθη). πνεῦμα is neuter and anarthrous here: 'a holy spirit/breath', not a named person.

ellipsis.cut: The canon's (...) drops 1:18a (betrothal to Joseph, 'before they came together').
ellipsis.note: Context only.

items.french_variance: Spelling « Mathieu » here and at TBWTT-4:19, « Matthieu » elsewhere. Library notes do not identify the French NT the canon follows (Dhorme is OT only).
items.analysis: Greek and French agree that the pregnancy has a non-human source named pneuma hagion. The identification of that source with 'one of theirs' (a male individual) is supplied by the canon: πνεῦμα is neuter and unarticled, and nothing in the wording individuates a father. The Greek ἐκ ('out of', the genealogical preposition of 1:3–16) is marginally closer to a parentage statement than the French agentive « par », but it does not carry the reading.

load_bearing.comment: Two differences. (1) ἀνήχθη is 'led/brought up' (ἀνά-), which French « emmené » flattens. (2) The canon's (...) sits exactly where the Greek names the agent, ὑπὸ τοῦ πνεύματος 'by the Spirit'; the canon's commentary supplies 'par les créateurs' instead.

load_bearing.comment: πειράζω = put to the test; French « mis à l'épreuve » is the literal sense (library line: 'tempted'). διάβολος = 'slanderer/accuser', a title, which suits the canon's 'sceptic' reading at least as well as « diable ».

load_bearing.comment: French middle « s'ouvrirent »; Greek passive.

ellipsis.cut: 3:16a (the baptism, coming up from the water) and, in 4:1, the agent phrase 'by the Spirit' (ὑπὸ τοῦ πνεύματος).
ellipsis.note: The second (...) removes the only stated agent of the 'taking'. The reading replaces it with the creators; the same book identifies the 'Spirit' with the creators' activity elsewhere, so the cut does not hide a contradiction, but the reader of the excerpt cannot see that the text names an agent. The baptism by John (3:13–15), the occasion of the scene, is also absent.

items.french_variance: Reference printed « IV-I » (letter I for 1). The appositional « mon fils, l'aimé » is a legitimate construal (library note at 3:17). Library notes do not identify the French NT the canon follows (Dhorme is OT only).
items.analysis: The passive 'was led up … to be tested' is in the Greek, and two Greek words are closer to the canon's reading than the quoted French: ἀνήχθη is 'led up' (not merely 'taken'), and διάβολος/πειρασθῆναι are literally 'the accuser' and 'to be tested'. Against that, the Greek states the agent of the leading — the Spirit — in the words the canon's ellipsis removes, and the 'presentation to his Father … initiation in scientific techniques' corresponds to nothing in 3:16–4:1 beyond the voice from the skies.

items.reading_summary: A translation claim: the usual 'poor in spirit' is a mistranslation; the original sense is 'the poor, if they have spirit/intelligence, will be happy'.

load_bearing.gloss: the poor in/with respect to the spirit (dative)
load_bearing.comment: The dative τῷ πνεύματι is attached directly to οἱ πτωχοί: it specifies the poverty ('poor as to spirit'). French « par l'esprit » reads the dative as instrumental. Neither is a conditional clause.

load_bearing.gloss: happy, fortunate, blessed (nominal sentence, no verb)
load_bearing.comment: « Magnifiques » is an idiosyncratic rendering; the canon's own gloss returns to « heureux ».

load_bearing.original: ὅτι αὐτῶν ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν
load_bearing.translit: hoti autōn estin hē basileia tōn ouranōn
load_bearing.gloss: because theirs is the kingdom of the heavens
load_bearing.comment: Second half of the verse, not quoted.

ellipsis.cut: 5:3b 'for theirs is the kingdom of the heavens' is not quoted.

items.french_variance: The canon contrasts the French it quotes (« par l'esprit ») with the common French (« pauvres d'esprit ») and with its own claimed original. Library notes do not identify the French NT the canon follows (Dhorme is OT only).
items.analysis: This is one of the few places where the canon makes an explicit claim about the original wording. The Greek does not have it: there is no conditional ('if they have'), no verb of having, and no future 'will be'; τῷ πνεύματι is a dative of respect limiting 'poor'. The Greek does exclude the colloquial French sense 'simple-minded' (pauvres d'esprit), so the complaint about that reception is fair, but the proposed 'original sense' is not a possible construal of οἱ πτωχοὶ τῷ πνεύματι. The quoted French (« par l'esprit », instrumental) is a step toward the canon's sense that the Greek does not require.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] The canon's words 'sens originel' could refer to a lost Aramaic saying rather than Matthew's Greek; no such source is extant, so the claim cannot be checked beyond the Greek.

items.canon_french: «D’autres sont tombées parmi la rocaille, où elles n’avaient pas beaucoup de terre ; (...) mais au lever du soleil elles ont été brûlées (...)».

reading_quotes.french: La deuxième tentative fut faite sur une planète située trop près d’un soleil trop chaud et dont les radiations nocives détruisirent la création.

load_bearing.french: au lever du soleil elles ont été brûlées
load_bearing.gloss: when the sun rose it was scorched
load_bearing.comment: The sun is the destroying agent in the Greek; so in French.

load_bearing.original: διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν ῥίζαν ἐξηράνθη
load_bearing.translit: dia to mē echein rhizan exēranthē
load_bearing.gloss: because it had no root it withered
load_bearing.comment: Cut: the Greek's stated cause is lack of root, not excess of sun.

ellipsis.cut: 13:5b 'immediately they sprang up because they had no depth of soil'; 13:6b 'because they had no root they withered'.
ellipsis.note: Both cuts remove the parable's stated cause (shallow soil / no root). With them gone the sun alone looks like the cause, which is what the 'too hot a sun' reading needs.

items.french_variance: Library notes do not identify the French NT the canon follows (Dhorme is OT only).
items.analysis: The sun's scorching is in the Greek, but as a secondary agent: the Greek twice gives the cause as lack of depth and root, and both clauses fall inside the canon's ellipses. The reading therefore rests on the excerpt as cut rather than on the full verse.

items.analysis: Plants choking the crop is the Greek image; the planetary application and humidity are added.

items.canon_french: «D’autres sont tombées dans la bonne terre et ont donné du fruit, celle-ci cent, celle-là soixante, celle-là trente. Entende qui a des oreilles !».

reading_quotes.french: Enfin la quatrième tentative fut un succès, «dans la bonne terre». Et chose importante, il y a eu trois succès, ce qui veut dire que sur deux autres planètes relativement proches il y a des êtres semblables aux hommes
«Entende qui a des oreilles !» : comprenne qui pourra.

items.reading_summary: Fourth attempt succeeds; the three yields = three successful worlds, so two other nearby planets carry humans made by the same creators.

load_bearing.french: celle-ci cent, celle-là soixante, celle-là trente
load_bearing.original: ὃ μὲν ἑκατὸν ὃ δὲ ἑξήκοντα ὃ δὲ τριάκοντα
load_bearing.translit: ho men hekaton ho de hexēkonta ho de triakonta
load_bearing.gloss: one a hundred, one sixty, one thirty
load_bearing.comment: Three distinct yields from the good soil — the numeral three the canon uses is really in the Greek (as three grades of yield).

load_bearing.gloss: upon the good earth/soil
load_bearing.comment: γῆ is both 'soil' and 'earth/land'. French « la bonne terre » keeps the same double sense; English 'good soil' (library line) loses it.

items.french_variance: Library notes do not identify the French NT the canon follows (Dhorme is OT only).
items.analysis: The structural hooks — three failures followed by a success that comes in three grades — are in the Greek, and γῆ ('earth' as well as 'soil') permits the 'world' sense as readily as French « terre ». That the grades are planets is added; within the canon's own reading 'three successes' sits awkwardly with 'the fourth attempt was a success' (one sowing, three yields in the Greek).

items.canon_french: «(...) à vous il a été donné de connaître les mystères du règne des cieux...».

reading_quotes.french: Les trois planètes où la vie a été créée ont été mises en compétition.

items.reading_summary: The 'mysteries of the reign of the heavens' concern the competition among the three created worlds for the creators' inheritance.

load_bearing.french: les mystères du règne des cieux
load_bearing.original: τὰ μυστήρια τῆς βασιλείας τῶν οὐρανῶν
load_bearing.translit: ta mystēria tēs basileias tōn ouranōn
load_bearing.gloss: the secrets of the kingdom/reign of the heavens
load_bearing.comment: Exact; plural 'heavens' in both.

ellipsis.cut: 13:11b 'but to them it has not been given' (the canon's '...').
ellipsis.note: The canon paraphrases the contrast itself at TBWTT-4:50.

items.french_variance: Library notes do not identify the French NT the canon follows (Dhorme is OT only).
items.analysis: Wording identical in substance. βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν with a genuine plural is rendered « règne des cieux », which the canon can read as 'reign of the skies'; the three-planet competition is added.

items.actual_reference: 'Last judgement' (Matthean judgement scenes, e.g. Matt 13:49; 25:19-30); no verse cited
items.canon_french: elle recevra alors cet héritage au jour du «jugement dernier». Jour où un niveau suffisant de connaissances aura été acquis.

reading_quotes.french: un grand conseil des éternels se réunit pour juger, en un «jugement dernier», quels sont ceux qui, morts durant l’année, méritent de vivre une autre vie

items.reading_summary: The 'last judgement' is (a) the day a world has reached sufficient knowledge and inherits, and (b) on the creators' planet, the annual council session deciding who is re-created.

load_bearing.gloss: at the completion of the age
load_bearing.comment: The phrase 'last judgement' is not a biblical expression in the passages the canon quotes; the nearest quoted Greek is 'the completion of the age'.

items.french_variance: The term is used in two different senses (TBWTT-4:55 a single future day for a planet; TBWTT-7:31 a yearly sitting).
items.analysis: A church-tradition term in scare quotes, not a quotation; no verse to compare. Recorded because the canon uses it with two distinct referents.

items.canon_french: «(...) la plus petite de toutes les semences, mais quand elle croît, c’est le plus grand des légumes, elle devient un arbre et les oiseaux du ciel viennent nicher dans ses branches».

reading_quotes.french: Le génie humain c’est
Les «oiseaux du ciel» : les créateurs viendront «nicher» dans ses branches, apporteront leur savoir aux hommes quand ils s’en seront montrés dignes.

items.reading_summary: The mustard seed is human genius; the 'birds of the sky' are the creators who will come and bring their knowledge.

load_bearing.gloss: the flying things of the sky (singular)
load_bearing.comment: πετεινά is literally 'winged/flying things'; a fixed biblical phrase for birds.

load_bearing.translit: (elthein … kai) kataskēnoun en tois kladois autou
load_bearing.gloss: come and pitch tent / settle
load_bearing.comment: κατασκηνόω is 'encamp, take up quarters' (from σκηνή 'tent'), a verb of persons dwelling, used of birds roosting. French « nicher » is bird-specific.

load_bearing.original: Ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν κόκκῳ σινάπεως
load_bearing.translit: Homoia estin hē basileia tōn ouranōn kokkō sinapeōs
load_bearing.gloss: the kingdom of the heavens is like a mustard seed
load_bearing.comment: The Greek subject of the comparison is the kingdom of the heavens, replaced in the canon's lead-in by 'human genius'.

ellipsis.cut: 13:31 and the subject of the simile ('the kingdom of the heavens is like a mustard seed which a man sowed in his field').
ellipsis.note: The canon substitutes its own subject (« Le génie humain c'est ») for the Greek one (the kingdom of the heavens).

items.french_variance: « oiseaux » = opponents at 13:4 (TBWTT-4:49), creators here. Library notes do not identify the French NT the canon follows (Dhorme is OT only).
items.analysis: For the detail the reading uses, the Greek is slightly more open than the French: κατασκηνοῦν is 'to encamp, settle' — a word for people taking up residence — where « nicher » can only be said of birds, and πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ is 'flying things of the sky'. Against the reading, the Greek subject of the simile is the kingdom of the heavens, not human genius, and the canon reads the same 'birds' as destroyers eleven lines earlier.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] κατασκηνόω echoes LXX Dan 4 / Ezek 17:23 / Ps 103(104):12, where birds lodging in a great tree picture nations sheltering under an empire; this conventional background is not in the library note for this verse.

items.canon_french: «Le règne des cieux est pareil à la levure qu’une femme a (...) cachée dans trois mesures de farine jusqu’à ce que tout ait levé».

reading_quotes.french: Nouvelle allusion aux trois mondes où les créateurs attendent l’éclosion scientifique.

items.reading_summary: Three measures = the three worlds awaiting scientific flowering.

load_bearing.gloss: three sata of flour
load_bearing.comment: The numeral three is in the Greek. σάτον is a specific dry measure (Aramaic seʾah), so 'three sata' is a concrete quantity.

load_bearing.gloss: hid in
load_bearing.comment: Exact.

ellipsis.cut: 'took' (λαβοῦσα).

items.french_variance: Library notes do not identify the French NT the canon follows (Dhorme is OT only).
items.analysis: The numeral is real and the French keeps it. Its application to worlds is added; in the Greek the three measures are one batch into which one leaven is hidden 'until the whole was leavened', i.e. the image stresses one whole, not three separate units.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] Three seahs is commonly noted as the quantity of Gen 18:6 (Sarah's baking), i.e. an idiomatic 'large batch'; not in the library note.

items.canon_french: «(...) je clamerai ce qui a été caché depuis la fondation du monde».

reading_quotes.french: Car c’est là une des choses les plus importantes, les planètes ont une vie et ne sont un jour plus habitables.

items.reading_summary: What was hidden 'since the foundation of the world' concerns the finite life of planets and the need to create successor humanities.

load_bearing.gloss: things hidden from (the) foundation
load_bearing.comment: The library's Greek text ends at καταβολῆς; κόσμου 'of the world' is absent (library line: 'hidden from the foundation'). The canon's French has « du monde ».

load_bearing.gloss: I will utter/belch forth

ellipsis.cut: 13:35a 'so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled: I will open my mouth in parables' (Ps 78:2).
ellipsis.note: The cut removes the statement that this is a citation of 'the prophet' and that the medium is parables.

items.french_variance: The canon's French follows a Greek text with κόσμου; the library follows the shorter reading. Library notes do not identify the French NT the canon follows (Dhorme is OT only).
items.analysis: The canon's comment turns on 'the world' (planets have a life-span). In the Greek text the library prints, the phrase is only 'from (the) foundation' — the word 'world' is a textual plus carried by the French the canon quotes. The longer reading is widely attested, so this is a text-critical dependence rather than a translation error; either way the planetary doctrine is not in the wording.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] That many manuscripts read ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου and that NA28 brackets κόσμου is from general knowledge of the apparatus, not from the library note.

items.canon_french: «(...) à la fin des âges : les anges sortiront, ils sépareront les mauvais du milieu des justes (...)».

reading_quotes.french: Afin que l’héritage ne soit pas perdu, les créateurs ont mis la vie sur trois mondes, et le meilleur seulement aura droit à l’héritage

items.reading_summary: At the end of the ages the 'angels' (creators) will sort the worlds; only the best inherits.

load_bearing.gloss: at the completion of the age (singular)
load_bearing.comment: Greek αἰών is 'age', singular; French has the plural « des âges ». Both avoid the traditional « fin du monde ».

load_bearing.gloss: the messengers will go out
load_bearing.comment: ἄγγελοι = messengers.

load_bearing.french: les mauvais du milieu des justes
load_bearing.original: τοὺς πονηροὺς ἐκ μέσου τῶν δικαίων
load_bearing.translit: tous ponērous ek mesou tōn dikaiōn
load_bearing.gloss: the wicked out of the midst of the righteous
load_bearing.comment: Individuals (masculine plural persons), not worlds.

load_bearing.original: βαλοῦσιν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν κάμινον τοῦ πυρός
load_bearing.translit: balousin autous eis tēn kaminon tou pyros
load_bearing.gloss: they will throw them into the furnace of fire
load_bearing.comment: Cut after the quotation.

ellipsis.cut: 13:49a 'So it shall be'; 13:50 the furnace of fire, weeping and gnashing of teeth.
ellipsis.note: The canon elsewhere (TBWTT-4:88) says the losing world is 'anéanti', so the cut does not reverse the sense.

items.french_variance: Library notes do not identify the French NT the canon follows (Dhorme is OT only).
items.analysis: αἰών 'age' is the Greek word, and the French the canon quotes already renders it as age rather than 'world' — a point where the original supports the canon's age-vocabulary against the common French Bibles, though the Greek is singular ('the age'), not plural. The sorting in the Greek is of persons within one net/field, not of planets.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] That Segond/Crampon-type French Bibles print « fin du monde » here is from memory.

items.canon_french: Le passage de la multiplication des pains a déjà été expliqué précédemment. Il s’agit d’aliments concentrés sous forme de grosses pilules

reading_quotes.french: D’où les «hosties» et leurs formes rappelant celle d’une pilule.

items.reading_summary: The loaves are concentrated food in large pill form, like astronauts' rations (refers back to the 2 Kings 4:42-44 explanation, TBWTT-3:137).

load_bearing.original: τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους καὶ τοὺς δύο ἰχθύας
load_bearing.translit: tous pente artous kai tous dyo ichthyas
load_bearing.gloss: the five loaves and the two fish
load_bearing.comment: Ordinary bread loaves and fish; broken (κλάσας) and distributed.

load_bearing.original: τὸ περισσεῦον τῶν κλασμάτων δώδεκα κοφίνους πλήρεις
load_bearing.translit: to perisseuon tōn klasmatōn dōdeka kophinous plēreis
load_bearing.gloss: the surplus of the broken pieces, twelve baskets full
load_bearing.comment: Leftover fragments exceed the starting quantity.

items.analysis: Unreferenced allusion. The Greek speaks of five loaves and two fish, broken, with twelve baskets of fragments left over. Nothing in the vocabulary suggests concentrates; the fish and the surplus of 'broken pieces' are not addressed by the pill reading.

items.canon_french: «(...) il vint vers eux, marchant sur la mer».

reading_quotes.french: les créateurs le soutiennent par un rayon antigravitationnel qui annule en un point précis les effets de la pesanteur

items.reading_summary: Jesus is held up by an anti-gravity ray.

load_bearing.gloss: walking upon/over the sea (accusative)
load_bearing.comment: Exact.

ellipsis.cut: 'in the fourth watch of the night'.

items.french_variance: Library notes do not identify the French NT the canon follows (Dhorme is OT only).
items.analysis: The Greek reports the fact without mechanism; the ray is added.

items.canon_french: «(...) mais en voyant le vent (Pierre) fut effrayé et (...) comme ils montaient dans le bateau, le vent tomba».

reading_quotes.french: Cela crée d’ailleurs une turbulence qui est décrite
Le «vent tomba» quand ils montèrent dans le bateau, car l’émission du rayon fut interrompue quand Jésus fut dans le bateau.

items.reading_summary: The wind is turbulence produced by the anti-gravity ray; it stops when the ray is switched off as Jesus boards.

load_bearing.gloss: the wind grew weary / abated
load_bearing.comment: Exact.

load_bearing.french: comme ils montaient dans le bateau
load_bearing.gloss: when they had gone up into the boat (aorist participle)
load_bearing.comment: Greek aorist = boarding completed; French imperfect « comme ils montaient » = while boarding. The canon's own comment ('quand Jésus fut dans le bateau') matches the Greek aspect better than the French it quotes.

load_bearing.gloss: seeing the strong wind
load_bearing.comment: Library text has ἰσχυρόν 'strong'; canon's French follows the shorter text.

load_bearing.gloss: for the wind was contrary
load_bearing.comment: Not quoted: the wind is already blowing against the boat before Jesus sets out across the water (14:24, before 14:25).

ellipsis.cut: 14:30b–31 (Peter sinks, cries out, is caught by the hand); and, upstream, 14:24.
ellipsis.note: The quoted verses alone make the wind coincide with the walking. 14:24 has the head-wind battering the boat before the fourth-watch walk begins, so in the Greek narrative the wind is not produced by the event the canon assigns it to.

items.french_variance: Library notes do not identify the French NT the canon follows (Dhorme is OT only).
items.analysis: The cessation of wind on boarding is in the Greek (and the aorist participle fits the canon's 'once he was in the boat' better than the French imperfect). But the causal claim — the ray creates the turbulence — conflicts with the narrative order of the Greek: 14:24 states the contrary wind as the boat's condition before Jesus comes (14:25). The canon quotes 14:25, 30, 32 and not 14:24.

items.canon_french: «(...) sur une haute montagne, à l’écart (...) (Jésus) fut transfiguré devant (Pierre, Jacques et Jean), sa face brilla comme le soleil, ses vêtements devinrent blancs comme la lumière. Et voilà qu’ils virent Moïse et Elie parler avec lui (...) voilà qu’une nuée lumineuse les couvrit et que, de la nuée, une voix dit : Celui-ci est mon fils, (...) écoutez-le».

reading_quotes.french: Cette scène se déroule de nuit et les apôtres sont tous effrayés de voir Jésus éclairé par les puissants projecteurs de l’engin volant d’où sortent Moïse et Elie toujours en vie grâce à «l’arbre de vie»

items.reading_summary: A night scene: Jesus lit by the searchlights of a flying craft, out of which come Moses and Elijah, kept alive by the 'tree of life'.

load_bearing.gloss: a luminous cloud overshadowed them
load_bearing.comment: φωτεινή = 'full of light, shining'; ἐπισκιάζω = 'cast a shadow over'. French « couvrit » drops the shadow image; the Greek has the paradox of a bright thing that overshadows from above.

load_bearing.gloss: a voice out of the cloud
load_bearing.comment: Exact: the voice issues from inside the cloud.

load_bearing.french: sa face brilla comme le soleil
load_bearing.original: ἔλαμψεν τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ὡς ὁ ἥλιος
load_bearing.translit: elampsen to prosōpon autou hōs ho hēlios
load_bearing.gloss: his face shone like the sun
load_bearing.comment: Greek: the face itself shines (active ἔλαμψεν), and he 'was transformed' (μετεμορφώθη) — light from him, not onto him.

load_bearing.gloss: Moses and Elijah appeared / were seen by them
load_bearing.comment: Greek passive 'appeared to them' (singular verb); French makes the disciples the subject.

load_bearing.gloss: they were exceedingly afraid
load_bearing.comment: Fear is in 17:6 — on hearing the voice, not on seeing the light.

load_bearing.french: Cette scène se déroule de nuit
load_bearing.gloss: tell no one the vision
load_bearing.comment: Matthew has no time-of-day notice; and in 17:9 Jesus himself calls the event τὸ ὅραμα 'the vision'.

ellipsis.cut: 17:1a 'after six days'; 17:4 (Peter's offer of three tents); 17:5a 'while he was still speaking'; in the voice, 'the beloved, in whom I am well pleased'.
ellipsis.note: The cuts shorten; the insertions in brackets are identifications. The sense-affecting elements are in the commentary, not the cuts.

items.french_variance: The voice is quoted in full at TBWTT-4:19 (« l'aimé dont je suis content ») and truncated here although the Greek of 17:5 repeats 3:17 verbatim. Library notes do not identify the French NT the canon follows (Dhorme is OT only).
items.analysis: The luminous cloud that comes over the group and the voice from inside it are the Greek wording (νεφέλη φωτεινή, ἐκ τῆς νεφέλης), and ἐπεσκίασεν 'overshadowed' is slightly more spatial than « couvrit ». Three elements of the reading are not in the Greek or run against it: (1) 'at night' — Matthew gives no time; (2) Moses and Elijah come 'out of the craft' — in the Greek they appear (17:3) before the cloud arrives (17:5); (3) Jesus 'lit by searchlights' — the Greek has his face itself shining and him 'transformed'. The disciples' fear is real but is attached to the voice (17:6).
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] Luke 9:32 ('heavy with sleep') and 9:37 ('the next day') are the usual basis for a night setting; Luke 9 is not in the library and the canon cites Matthew.

items.ref_note: Proverbial wording; « d'après » acknowledged by the canon.
items.canon_french: «Les premiers seront les derniers et les derniers seront les premiers»

reading_quotes.french: veut dire que les créés seront créateurs comme les créateurs ont été créés

load_bearing.original: πολλοὶ δὲ ἔσονται πρῶτοι ἔσχατοι καὶ ἔσχατοι πρῶτοι
load_bearing.translit: polloi de esontai prōtoi eschatoi kai eschatoi prōtoi
load_bearing.gloss: but many (who are) first will be last, and last first
load_bearing.comment: Greek has πολλοί 'many' and no articles: 'many firsts will be lasts'. The canon's proverbial form is universal ('the first').

ellipsis.cut: 'many' (πολλοί).
ellipsis.note: The universal form supports a general law (created → creators); the Greek limits the reversal to 'many'.

items.french_variance: Canon flags the looseness itself with « d'après ». The reference sits in TBWTT-4:76, the saying in 4:77. Library notes do not identify the French NT the canon follows (Dhorme is OT only).
items.analysis: A reversal of rank is the Greek sense; the cyclical 'created become creators' is added, and the Greek's 'many' is less general than the canon's wording. Library note already records that the wording is closer to 20:16 (not in the library).

ellipsis.cut: 25:16–27 summarised in the canon's own words (TBWTT-4:80–86, presented inside opening guillemets); 25:30 (the useless slave thrown into outer darkness) not quoted; 25:29 'παντί' (everyone) not rendered.
ellipsis.note: The paraphrase is faithful in outline. In the Greek two of three slaves are commended equally (25:21, 23); the canon's 'the world that has made the most progress will receive the inheritance' singles out one.

items.french_variance: TBWTT-4:80–86 mix paraphrase and quotation inside one set of guillemets; only 4:87 is verbatim scripture. Library notes do not identify the French NT the canon follows (Dhorme is OT only).
items.analysis: The triad the canon builds on is in the Greek (three slaves, three allotments, a reckoning on the master's return). The canon's French puts the numeral 'three' into what is typographically a quotation; the Greek has it only implicitly. The winner-takes-the-inheritance rule fits 25:28 (the ten-talent slave receives the extra talent) but not 25:21–23, where the two-talent slave gets the same commendation.

items.french_variance: Library notes do not identify the French NT the canon follows (Dhorme is OT only).
items.analysis: The descent from the sky, the shaking and the lightning-like figure are the Greek wording. On the central point the Greek is, if anything, more favourable than the French the canon uses: where the canon writes « ressuscite » in scare quotes and says the creators 'revive' him, Matthew's own verb (28:6, unquoted) is the passive ἠγέρθη — 'he was roused/raised' by an unnamed agent. In the Greek, however, the single messenger opens an already-vacated tomb and announces; no treatment or reanimation is narrated, and only one figure appears, not 'creators'.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] The agentless passive is conventionally explained as a 'divine passive' (God as implied agent); so the library note at 17:2 for μετεμορφώθη.

items.analysis: The universal mission (πάντα τὰ ἔθνη) is Greek. What is to be transmitted is redefined by the canon's bracket and ellipsis: the Greek specifies baptism into the name of Father, Son and Holy Spirit and observance of Jesus' commands; the excerpt replaces the first with « dire tout cela ». Text-critically the verse belongs to the longer ending of Mark, absent from Vaticanus and Sinaiticus (library note) — the canon's 'last sentence, so important' stands in a passage the library marks as secondary.

items.analysis: The reading as a date-marker depends on the bracketed lead-in, which is neither in the French Bible nor in the Greek. In the Greek the sentence continues 16:17: these are signs that accompany believers 'in my name', alongside exorcism and new tongues — immunity as a sign, not acquired medical capability, and not tied to an epoch. Like 16:19 the verse stands in the longer ending (library note).

items.analysis: Every observable the reading uses is in the Greek: a sudden noise from the sky filling the house, a fire-like something distributed onto each individual, immediate speech in other languages. The French follows closely, similes included. The mechanism (telepathic waves, electroshock, memory imprint) is supplied; the Greek's own account of the agency — the Spirit continuously 'giving' the utterance — falls in the canon's trailing ellipsis.

items.analysis: γένος is a kinship word — 'stock, race' — and the French « race » renders it literally where many versions weaken it to 'offspring'; the Greek gives the canon's literal-kinship reading a real lexical footing. load_bearing.gloss: from the gate of the fishes
load_bearing.comment: Plural 'fishes' with article — the Hebrew is literally 'Gate of the Fishes', as in French. Hebrew has 'from' (min); French « du côté de ».

load_bearing.comment: ṣəʿāqâ is a cry of distress (paired with 'wailing' in the next clause), not a proclamation.

load_bearing.comment: The rest of the verse, not quoted: two further named localities of Jerusalem in parallel.

ellipsis.cut: 'oracle of YHWH' (nəʾum-YHWH) inside the quoted half; and the second half of the verse (Second Quarter, the hills).
ellipsis.note: The unquoted parallel members (ha-Mišneh, the hills; 1:11 'the Mortar') show the Fish Gate as one of a series of Jerusalem localities struck on the day of YHWH. Quoted alone, the gate is free to become a symbol.

items.french_variance: Quotation split across TBWTT-5:5–6. The OT French here is presumably Dhorme (woh-claim-0066); not collated.
items.analysis: The lexical hook is real and not a French artefact: שַׁעַר הַדָּגִים is 'the gate of the fishes', plural, exactly as « Porte des Poissons ». The zodiacal application is added, and the Hebrew context is less hospitable than the excerpt: the cry is a ṣəʿāqâ, an outcry of disaster, and the gate is the first of three or four named city districts in a judgement oracle on Jerusalem, all cut.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] The Hebrew name of the constellation Pisces is Dagim (the same plural), which would make the pun available in Hebrew; from general knowledge, not in the library note.
