load_bearing.comment: literal

items.analysis: The French follows the Greek closely (and has the 'third of the earth' clause that the canon's English lost). The text says things were burned up by fire thrown down (katakaiō); 'radioactivity' and 'no longer grow' are supplied. The library note already records the French/English divergence.

items.canon_french: Le deuxième ange a trompeté et une sorte de grande montagne de feu ardent s'est jetée dans la mer, et le tiers de la mer a été du sang,

reading_quotes.french: L'explosion atomique a produit une énorme éruption de lave qui s'est écoulée dans les océans et a tué le tiers des animaux marins et détruit le tiers des navires.

items.reading_summary: The atomic explosion produces an enormous lava eruption flowing into the oceans.

load_bearing.french: une sorte de grande montagne de feu ardent s'est jetée dans la mer
load_bearing.original: ὡς ὄρος μέγα πυρὶ καιόμενον ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν
load_bearing.translit: hōs oros mega pyri kaiomenon eblēthē eis tēn thalassan
load_bearing.gloss: something like a great mountain burning with fire was thrown into the sea
load_bearing.comment: Greek passive 'was thrown' (same verb as hail and fire in 8:7); French reflexive 's'est jetée' ('flung itself') is nearer to a flow that moves of itself

load_bearing.french: le tiers des créatures qui vivent dans la mer
load_bearing.original: τῶν κτισμάτων τῶν ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ, τὰ ἔχοντα ψυχάς
load_bearing.translit: tōn ktismatōn tōn en tē thalassē, ta echonta psychas
load_bearing.gloss: the creatures in the sea, those having psychai (lives)
load_bearing.comment: French 'qui vivent' renders 'having psychai' — sea animals have psychē here, in line with the argument of LWTE-1:69

items.analysis: A weak dependence: 'lava that flows into the oceans' sits more easily on the French reflexive 's'est jetée' than on eblēthē, 'was thrown/hurled' — one burning mass cast in from outside, by the same verb used for the hail and fire of the first trumpet. Otherwise the reading (eruption caused by an explosion) is supplied. Side note: ta echonta psychas is another place where the Greek gives animals psychē, which would have served LWTE-1:69 and is flattened in the French.

items.canon_french: Le troisième ange a trompeté, et une grande étoile ardente comme une torche est tombée du ciel. Elle est tombée sur le tiers des fleuves et sur les sources des eaux.

reading_quotes.french: Les explosions atomiques se succèdent en riposte aux premières attaques, des missiles, de «grandes étoiles ardentes» tombent un peu partout, et les eaux potables sont pour une grande partie polluées et tuent beaucoup d'hommes qui en boivent.

items.reading_summary: The burning star(s) = missiles falling in retaliation; drinking water is polluted and kills.

load_bearing.french: une grande étoile ardente comme une torche est tombée du ciel
load_bearing.original: ἔπεσεν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἀστὴρ μέγας καιόμενος ὡς λαμπάς
load_bearing.translit: epesen ek tou ouranou astēr megas kaiomenos hōs lampas
load_bearing.gloss: there fell from the sky a great star burning like a torch
load_bearing.comment: singular in Greek and in the canon's quotation; the canon's commentary then cites it in the plural inside guillemets

load_bearing.original: ἀπέθανον ἐκ τῶν ὑδάτων, ὅτι ἐπικράνθησαν
load_bearing.translit: apethanon ek tōn hydatōn, hoti epikranthēsan
load_bearing.gloss: died from the waters, because they had been made bitter
load_bearing.comment: literal: people die from drinking contaminated water

items.french_variance: Quotation: «une grande étoile ardente» (singular) — commentary quoting it back: «grandes étoiles ardentes» (plural).
items.analysis: The image (one flaming object falling from the sky, water made deadly) is the same in Greek and French; 'missile' is supplied. The commentary's «grandes étoiles ardentes» (plural, in quotation marks) is not what the verse it has just quoted says — one star, with a name (ho Apsinthos).

items.canon_french: Ils ont été obscurcis d'un tiers et le jour a brillé un tiers en moins et la nuit de même.

reading_quotes.french: Les poussières et les cendres soulevées par les explosions nucléaires successives sont tellement nombreuses qu'elles obscurcissent le ciel, cachent le soleil, la lune et les étoiles et donnent l'impression que le jour et la nuit sont plus courts.

items.reading_summary: Dust and ash from repeated nuclear explosions hide sun, moon and stars and make day and night seem shorter.

load_bearing.french: le jour a brillé un tiers en moins
load_bearing.original: ἡ ἡμέρα μὴ φάνῃ τὸ τρίτον αὐτῆς
load_bearing.translit: hē hēmera mē phanē to triton autēs
load_bearing.gloss: (so that) the day should not shine for the third of it
load_bearing.comment: Greek: a third OF THE DAY gives no light — a loss of duration. French 'un tiers en moins' can be heard as a third less bright.

load_bearing.gloss: was struck
load_bearing.comment: the luminaries themselves are 'struck'; the canon reads an obscuring medium between them and the observer

items.analysis: The canon's gloss — day and night seem shorter — matches the Greek construction (the day not shining for a third of itself) better than the French it quotes, whose 'a brillé un tiers en moins' reads more naturally as dimming. On the other side, eplēgē has the sun, moon and stars themselves struck, not veiled; 'dust' is an inference.

items.canon_french: Le cinquième ange a trompeté, et j'ai vu une étoile qui était tombée du ciel sur la terre. On lui a donné la clé du puits de l'abîme.

reading_quotes.french: Description de la chute d'un missile et du champignon qu'il produit.

items.reading_summary: The fallen star = a missile; the smoke from the pit = the mushroom cloud.

load_bearing.french: une étoile qui était tombée du ciel sur la terre
load_bearing.original: ἀστέρα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ πεπτωκότα εἰς τὴν γῆν
load_bearing.translit: astera ek tou ouranou peptōkota eis tēn gēn
load_bearing.gloss: a star fallen (perfect) from the sky to the earth
load_bearing.comment: literal

load_bearing.french: On lui a donné la clé du puits de l'abîme
load_bearing.original: ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ἡ κλεὶς τοῦ φρέατος τῆς ἀβύσσου
load_bearing.translit: edothē autō hē kleis tou phreatos tēs abyssou
load_bearing.gloss: the key of the shaft of the abyss was given to him/it
load_bearing.comment: the star is an agent that receives a key and (9:2) opens the shaft — library EN 'to him'

load_bearing.french: une fumée est montée du puits comme une fumée de grande fournaise
load_bearing.original: ἀνέβη καπνὸς ἐκ τοῦ φρέατος ὡς καπνὸς καμίνου μεγάλης
load_bearing.translit: anebē kapnos ek tou phreatos hōs kapnos kaminou megalēs
load_bearing.gloss: smoke went up out of the shaft like the smoke of a great furnace
load_bearing.comment: literal: the smoke rises from an opened shaft in the ground, and darkens sun and air

items.analysis: Falling luminous object followed by a rising column of furnace-like smoke that darkens the sun: the sequence is in the Greek as in the French, and the missile/mushroom identification is supplied. What the wording does not suggest is an impact: the star is given a key and opens a shaft, and the smoke comes out of the abyss beneath. French and Greek do not differ here.

items.canon_french: On leur a donné non de les tuer mais de les tourmenter cinq mois et ce tourment est comme un tourment de scorpion quand il pique un homme.

reading_quotes.french: Les sauterelles sont des avions chargés de bombes atomiques qui vont tomber sur les grandes cités et infliger aux hommes qui ne mourront pas de l'explosion, des souffrances épouvantables dues à l'exposition à la radioactivité. Ils seront empoisonnés par les radiations comme on peut l'être par la piqûre d'un scorpion.

items.reading_summary: Locusts = aircraft carrying atomic bombs; the scorpion torment = radiation sickness in those who survive the blast.

load_bearing.french: De cette fumée sont sorties des sauterelles
load_bearing.gloss: out of the smoke came locusts
load_bearing.comment: literal

load_bearing.french: non de les tuer mais de les tourmenter cinq mois
load_bearing.original: ἵνα μὴ ἀποκτείνωσιν αὐτούς, ἀλλʼ ἵνα βασανισθήσονται μῆνας πέντε
load_bearing.translit: hina mē apokteinōsin autous, all' hina basanisthēsontai mēnas pente
load_bearing.gloss: that they should not kill them but that they be tormented five months
load_bearing.comment: the locusts are expressly denied the power to kill

load_bearing.french: ne pas nuire à l'herbe de la terre ni à aucune verdure ni à aucun arbre
load_bearing.original: ἵνα μὴ ἀδικήσουσιν τὸν χόρτον τῆς γῆς οὐδὲ πᾶν χλωρὸν οὐδὲ πᾶν δένδρον
load_bearing.translit: hina mē adikēsousin ton chorton tēs gēs oude pan chlōron oude pan dendron
load_bearing.gloss: that they not harm the grass of the earth nor any green thing nor any tree
load_bearing.comment: the locusts are forbidden to damage vegetation

items.analysis: French and Greek agree, and both resist the reading at two points the canon quotes without comment: the locusts may not kill (the canon confines the torment to 'those who will not die of the explosion', conceding deaths the text excludes) and may not harm any vegetation (whereas the canon's own reading of 8:7 has trees and grass destroyed by radioactivity). The scorpion-sting / radiation-poisoning analogy is supplied. The locusts also come out of the smoke of the pit, i.e. after the 'mushroom', not before it.

items.canon_french: Elles avaient des thorax comme des thorax de fer et le bruit de leurs ailes était comme bruit de chars et de chevaux qui courent à la guerre.

reading_quotes.french: Ces «sauterelles » métalliques, recouvertes de métal pour un primitif, comme un cheval qui part pour la guerre, ont un cockpit à l'intérieur duquel l'on voit le visage d'un homme, «leurs faces pareilles à des faces d'hommes », et en volant très haut dans le ciel elles laissent une traînée blanche que Jean appelle des cheveux, leurs «dents» ce sont les missiles accrochés sous leurs ailes, le «thorax de fer» c'est le fuselage, le bruit, c'est celui des tuyères des réacteurs

items.reading_summary: The locusts are metal aircraft: human faces = pilot seen in the cockpit; women's hair = condensation trails; lion's teeth = missiles under the wings; iron thorax = fuselage; noise of wings = jet nozzles; power in the tails = radiation from the missiles.

load_bearing.french: des thorax comme des thorax de fer
load_bearing.gloss: breastplates like iron breastplates
load_bearing.comment: thōrax = cuirass, piece of armour (library EN 'breastplates'). The canon's French keeps the Greek word in its anatomical French sense, 'thorax' = trunk of the body; 'fuselage' is read off that. The same Greek word at 9:17 is rendered «cuirasses» in the canon's own quotation (LWTE-2:194).

load_bearing.gloss: breastplates of fire
load_bearing.comment: same noun, here translated 'cuirasses' by the same French version

load_bearing.gloss: the sound of their wings
load_bearing.comment: winged, flying, loud: in the Greek

load_bearing.french: leurs faces comme des faces d'hommes
load_bearing.original: τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν ὡς πρόσωπα ἀνθρώπων
load_bearing.translit: ta prosōpa autōn hōs prosōpa anthrōpōn
load_bearing.gloss: their faces like faces of humans
load_bearing.comment: literal; the commentary requotes it as «pareilles à des faces d'hommes»

load_bearing.french: pareil à des chevaux prêts pour la guerre
load_bearing.gloss: like horses made ready for war
load_bearing.comment: 'covered in metal' is inferred from 'prepared for war'

load_bearing.french: dans leurs queues est leur pouvoir de nuire aux hommes cinq mois
load_bearing.original: ἐν ταῖς οὐραῖς αὐτῶν ἡ ἐξουσία αὐτῶν ἀδικῆσαι τοὺς ἀνθρώπους μῆνας πέντε
load_bearing.translit: en tais ourais autōn hē exousia autōn adikēsai tous anthrōpous mēnas pente
load_bearing.gloss: in their tails is their power to harm humans five months
load_bearing.comment: literal

items.french_variance: Same Greek noun: «thorax» at LWTE-2:187 (Rev 9:9), «cuirasses» at LWTE-2:194 (Rev 9:17). Quotation «leurs faces comme des faces d'hommes» (2:185) — requoted in the commentary as «leurs faces pareilles à des faces d'hommes» (2:190).
items.analysis: The clearest case in the slice of a reading resting on a French word. 'Thorax de fer' → fuselage works only because the French version transliterates thōrax, which in French means the body-trunk; in this Greek it is armour — and the same French version renders the same word 'cuirasses' eight verses later. With 'iron breastplates' the locusts are armoured like the war-horses of 9:7, and the body/fuselage step disappears. Conversely the Greek does give winged, loud, armoured, human-faced flyers, and every feature is flagged as comparison (hōs/homoios, as the library note stresses), which is the canon's own premise (a primitive describing by likeness). The golden crowns (9:7) get no gloss. The library note records the thorax point.

items.canon_french: Le sixième ange a trompeté et j'ai entendu une voix sortir des quatre cornes de l'autel d'or qui est devant Dieu.

reading_quotes.french: Jean décrit là les quatre haut-parleurs situés devant moi lorsque je lui faisais assister à tout cela.

items.reading_summary: The four horns of the golden altar = four loudspeakers placed in front of Yahweh while he showed John the scenes.

load_bearing.french: une voix sortir des quatre cornes de l'autel d'or
load_bearing.original: φωνὴν μίαν ἐκ τῶν κεράτων τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου τοῦ χρυσοῦ
load_bearing.translit: phōnēn mian ek tōn keratōn tou thysiastēriou tou chrysou
load_bearing.gloss: one voice out of the horns of the golden altar
load_bearing.comment: the library's base text (SBLGNT) has no 'four'; the numeral is a variant reading that the canon's French (and the KJV) carry. A voice issuing from horn-shaped projections is in both forms of the text.

load_bearing.gloss: which is before God
load_bearing.comment: 'situés devant moi' follows from identifying the throne-figure as Yahweh

items.analysis: The count 'four' in «quatre haut-parleurs» depends on a textual variant: the Greek text the library translates reads 'from the horns of the golden altar' with no numeral, while the French the canon quotes has 'des quatre cornes'. The qualitative hook — a single voice coming out of horns standing before the throne — survives in either text; the number does not. The library note mentions that the canon quotes 'the four horns' and that its own line follows the SBLGNT, without drawing the consequence for the reading.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] tessarōn ('four') is read by the Textus Receptus and many manuscripts and omitted by others (hence bracketed or dropped in critical editions); an altar with four horns is in any case the standard Israelite altar form (Exod 27:2; 30:2-3).

items.canon_french: car le pouvoir des chevaux est dans leurs bouches et dans leurs queues, car leurs queues pareilles à des serpents ont des têtes par lesquelles ils nuisent.

reading_quotes.french: la «tête des chevaux» c'est en fait la sortie des réacteurs, d'où sortent des flammes et de la fumée, et les queues qui ont «des têtes par lesquelles elles nuisent» sont en fait des missiles nucléaires, et vous savez très bien que l'on parle de la «tête » des missiles, qu'ils soient ou non à tête chercheuse

items.reading_summary: More aircraft: the horses' heads = jet exhausts emitting flame and smoke; the tails with heads = nuclear missiles ('heads' as in warheads / homing heads).

load_bearing.french: leurs queues pareilles à des serpents ont des têtes par lesquelles ils nuisent
load_bearing.original: αἱ γὰρ οὐραὶ αὐτῶν ὅμοιαι ὄφεσιν, ἔχουσαι κεφαλάς, καὶ ἐν αὐταῖς ἀδικοῦσιν
load_bearing.translit: hai gar ourai autōn homoiai ophesin, echousai kephalas, kai en autais adikousin
load_bearing.gloss: for their tails are like serpents, having heads, and with them they do harm
load_bearing.comment: kephalē 'head' is the same word in Greek and French, but the appeal to «la tête des missiles» is to modern French (and English) usage

load_bearing.french: de leurs bouches sortent du feu, de la fumée et du soufre
load_bearing.original: ἐκ τῶν στομάτων αὐτῶν ἐκπορεύεται πῦρ καὶ καπνὸς καὶ θεῖον
load_bearing.translit: ek tōn stomatōn autōn ekporeuetai pyr kai kapnos kai theion
load_bearing.gloss: out of their mouths comes fire and smoke and sulfur
load_bearing.comment: fire and smoke issue from the MOUTHS of lion-like heads, i.e. the front; the canon makes the head the exhaust (rear) of a jet

load_bearing.french: Et voici comme j'ai vu les chevaux dans ma vision
load_bearing.gloss: in the vision
load_bearing.comment: the only place the book says outright 'in the vision' (library note)

ellipsis.cut: 9:14-16 (release of the four angels at the Euphrates; the number of the cavalry) and 9:20-21 skipped silently

items.french_variance: Quotation: «par lesquelles ils nuisent» — commentary: «par lesquelles elles nuisent».
items.analysis: The French is literal; the reading is an identification by resemblance, reinforced by a modern-language pun on 'tête'. Two details of the wording pull the other way: flame and smoke come out of the mouths of heads 'like lions' heads' (a forward end), and the riders with their coloured breastplates and the stated number of the cavalry (9:16, twice ten thousand times ten thousand, not quoted) are left without referent. The commentary misquotes the pronoun of its own quotation.

items.canon_french: Et quand les sept tonnerres ont parlé, j'allais écrire et j'ai entendu une voix du ciel me dire : Scelle ce dont parlent les sept tonnerres, ne l'écris pas.

reading_quotes.french: Là, nous avons clairement dit à Jean qu'il n'y avait pas de dieu, et que nous étions des hommes comme lui, mais cela risquant de créer une confusion encore plus grande

items.reading_summary: What the seven thunders said and John was forbidden to write was that there is no god and that the speakers were men like him.

load_bearing.french: Scelle ce dont parlent les sept tonnerres, ne l'écris pas
load_bearing.original: Σφράγισον ἃ ἐλάλησαν αἱ ἑπτὰ βρονταί, καὶ μὴ αὐτὰ γράψῃς
load_bearing.translit: sphragison ha elalēsan hai hepta brontai, kai mē auta grapsēs
load_bearing.gloss: seal what the seven thunders spoke, and do not write it
load_bearing.comment: literal; the content is by definition absent from the text

items.analysis: The verse records only that something was said and suppressed; any statement of its content is outside what Greek or French can support or contradict. The canon fills the gap in the first person.

items.canon_french: aux jours de la voix du septième ange quand il va trompeter, le mystère de Dieu aussi sera fini comme il en a avisé ses esclaves les prophètes.

reading_quotes.french: Nous lui avons clairement expliqué que lorsque le temps sera venu, les hommes comprendront qu'il n'y a pas de dieu, et comprendront que nous sommes leurs créateurs.

items.reading_summary: 'The mystery of God will be finished' = when the time comes, men will understand that there is no god and that the Elohim are their creators.

load_bearing.french: le mystère de Dieu aussi sera fini
load_bearing.gloss: the mystery of God is completed / brought to its end
load_bearing.comment: teleō = bring to completion, accomplish, finish. French 'sera fini' leans to 'will be over'; the Greek leans to 'will be accomplished'.

load_bearing.french: comme il en a avisé ses esclaves les prophètes
load_bearing.original: ὡς εὐηγγέλισεν τοὺς ἑαυτοῦ δούλους τοὺς προφήτας
load_bearing.translit: hōs euēngelisen tous heautou doulous tous prophētas
load_bearing.gloss: as he announced-as-good-news to his own slaves the prophets
load_bearing.comment: euangelizō, the 'good news' verb, flattened to 'avisé' in the French

ellipsis.cut: opening 'mais' (all') replaced by '...'; 10:5-6 (the angel's oath 'there will be no more delay') skipped

items.analysis: A mild dependence on the French: 'le mystère de Dieu … sera fini' can be heard as 'the God-mystery will be over', which is how the canon reads it (the idea of god ends). The Greek etelesthē is the verb of fulfilment — the mystery reaches its goal, as announced as good news to the prophets — not of abolition, though 'finish' is within its range. The reading therefore has a narrower base in Greek than in the French.

items.ref_note: second half of 12:12 only; quotation opens with '...'
items.canon_french: le diable est descendu chez vous avec grande fureur sachant qu'il a peu d'instants.

reading_quotes.french: constitue la dernière possibilité pour Satan de prouver qu'il avait raison de dire que l'humanité était mauvaise
La «bête » qui est décrite plus loin, c'est tout simplement l'utilisation de l'énergie nucléaire à des fins meurtrières.
Pour le commun des mortels, le diable, Satan, Lucifer ou le démon, ce ne sont que des noms différents pour désigner une seule et même personne

items.reading_summary: The devil's 'short time' = humanity's final test (self-destruction or golden age) as Satan's last chance to prove humanity bad. 'The beast' = the murderous use of nuclear energy.

load_bearing.french: le diable est descendu chez vous avec grande fureur
load_bearing.original: κατέβη ὁ διάβολος πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἔχων θυμὸν μέγαν
load_bearing.translit: katebē ho diabolos pros hymas, echōn thymon megan
load_bearing.gloss: the slanderer/devil has come down to you, having great rage
load_bearing.comment: literal

load_bearing.gloss: knowing that he has little time
load_bearing.comment: literal

load_bearing.original: ὁ ὄφις ὁ ἀρχαῖος, ὁ καλούμενος Διάβολος καὶ ὁ Σατανᾶς
load_bearing.translit: ho ophis ho archaios, ho kaloumenos Diabolos kai ho Satanas
load_bearing.gloss: the ancient serpent, the one called Slanderer/Devil and the Satan
load_bearing.comment: three verses before the one quoted, the same chapter identifies the serpent, the Devil and Satan as one figure

ellipsis.cut: 12:12a ('Therefore rejoice, O heavens … Woe to the earth and the sea, for'); all of chapters 11 and 12:1-11, including 12:7-9 (war in heaven; the dragon = the ancient serpent = Devil = Satan cast down)
ellipsis.note: The omitted context identifies as one the figures the canon separates, and makes the descent an expulsion.

items.analysis: The half-verse quoted supports 'limited time' and 'rage' and nothing more specific. Its immediate context is unfavourable to LWTE's framework rather than to this one gloss: Rev 12:9, unquoted, says the dragon is 'the ancient serpent, the one called Devil and Satan' — precisely the identification of serpent, devil and Satan as one person that LWTE-2:4 calls the error of 'le commun des mortels' and that the chapter's taxonomy (Satan the opponent ≠ Lucifer's group, the 'serpent') denies. The canon quotes Revelation 12 as dictated by the Elohim while the chapter contradicts its own distinction; LWTE-2:106's general claim of copyist distortion is the only available reconciliation, and it is not invoked here. In 12:9-12 the devil has been thrown down after losing a war; the canon makes him a participant in an authorised test.

items.canon_french: Que l'intelligent calcule le chiffre de la bête, car c'est un chiffre d'homme et ce chiffre est six cent soixante-six.

reading_quotes.french: Six cent soixante-six, c'est le nombre de générations humaines qui se sont succédé sur terre depuis la création des premiers hommes dans les laboratoires originels.

Il n'y avait encore une fois pas besoin d'interpréter pour comprendre. Il suffisait de lire ce qui était écrit. Six cent soixante-six était effectivement un «chiffre d'homme », un nombre d'hommes qui se sont enfantés depuis le commencement

items.reading_summary: 666 = the number of human generations since the first humans were made (about 13,000 years ago; 666 × 20 years = 13,320), the 666th being the generation born in 1945; 'a number of man' = a number of men, i.e. of generations.

load_bearing.french: ce chiffre est six cent soixante-six
load_bearing.original: ὁ ἀριθμὸς αὐτοῦ ἑξακόσιοι ἑξήκοντα ἕξ
load_bearing.translit: ho arithmos autou hexakosioi hexēkonta hex
load_bearing.gloss: its/his number is six hundred sixty-six
load_bearing.comment: the library note records the variant 616 (P115, Ephraemi Rescriptus, copies known to Irenaeus); the generational computation exists only for the 666 reading

load_bearing.gloss: for it is (the) number of a man / a human number
load_bearing.comment: singular, anarthrous: 'of a man' or 'human'; the French keeps the ambiguity. 'Un nombre d'hommes' (plural, a count of people) is a third sense not carried by the genitive singular.

load_bearing.french: Que l'intelligent calcule le chiffre de la bête
load_bearing.original: ὁ ἔχων νοῦν ψηφισάτω τὸν ἀριθμὸν τοῦ θηρίου
load_bearing.translit: ho echōn noun psēphisatō ton arithmon tou thēriou
load_bearing.gloss: let the one having understanding reckon the number of the beast
load_bearing.comment: the text requires a calculation (psēphizō) and says the number is the beast's

ellipsis.cut: all of chapter 13 before v.18 (the two beasts) and the verse's opening 'Here is wisdom'
ellipsis.note: The description of the beast that the number belongs to is not quoted.

items.analysis: The French is faithful; the Greek adds two constraints that the French reader does not see. First, the manuscript tradition is divided between 666 and 616 (library note), and the canon's arithmetic (666 × 20 = 13,320) has no counterpart for 616. Second, the verse says the number belongs to the beast (ton arithmon tou thēriou) and must be computed (psēphisatō); the canon assigns the number to humanity's generations — while identifying the beast as nuclear weaponry — and says no interpretation is needed, only reading. 'Chiffre d'homme' → 'nombre d'hommes' turns a genitive singular into a head-count. The twenty-year generation is an external parameter.

items.canon_french: Et ç'a été des éclairs, des voix, des tonnerres, et ç’a été une grande secousse telle qu'il n'a pas été de pareille secousse, aussi grande, depuis que l'homme a été sur la terre.

reading_quotes.french: La secousse due aux explosions atomiques est énorme, et devient encore plus forte si elle déclenche une réaction en chaîne.

items.reading_summary: The unprecedented shaking = the shock of atomic explosions, greater still if a chain reaction starts.

load_bearing.gloss: a great shaking/earthquake occurred
load_bearing.comment: French 'secousse' keeps the general sense of seismos

load_bearing.french: depuis que l'homme a été sur la terre
load_bearing.original: ἀφʼ οὗ ἄνθρωποι ἐγένοντο ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς
load_bearing.translit: aph' hou anthrōpoi egenonto epi tēs gēs
load_bearing.gloss: since humans came to be on the earth
load_bearing.comment: library base text plural, French singular generic — no difference in sense (library note records the variant)

items.analysis: Literal French; 'secousse' rather than 'tremblement de terre' leaves room for a non-geological cause, and so does seismos. The atomic cause is supplied.

items.canon_french: Et toute île s'est enfuie, et on n'a plus trouvé de montagne.

reading_quotes.french: Cette monstrueuse explosion due à la réaction en chaîne fait dériver brutalement les continents, engloutit les îles et balaie les montagnes comme fétu de paille.

items.reading_summary: The chain-reaction explosion makes the continents drift abruptly, swallows islands and sweeps away mountains.

load_bearing.gloss: every island fled
load_bearing.comment: literal: islands 'fled' (moved away), which the canon reads as engulfed, and continents are not mentioned

load_bearing.french: on n'a plus trouvé de montagne
load_bearing.gloss: mountains were not found
load_bearing.comment: literal

items.analysis: Literal French. 'Continental drift' is added (the verse has islands and mountains). Compare TBWTT's separate claim about continental break-up at the Flood (core: continental-breakup-at-the-flood) — here the same mechanism is projected forward.

items.ref_note: first clause of 16:21 only; the canon marks the cut with '...'
items.canon_french: Une grande grêle comme des lingots descend du ciel sur les hommes...

reading_quotes.french: Dans les parties n'ayant pas souffert de l'explosion, des roches tombent du ciel à des milliers de kilomètres des points de chute des bombes.

items.reading_summary: The hail = rocks falling from the sky thousands of kilometres from the impact points.

load_bearing.french: Une grande grêle comme des lingots
load_bearing.gloss: great hail, as of a talent's weight
load_bearing.comment: talantiaios is a measure of weight (library note: roughly 25-40 kg); French 'lingots' gives a shape/material (a cast block), from which 'roches' is a short step. The Greek noun stays 'hail'.

ellipsis.cut: 16:21b: 'and the people blasphemed God because of the plague of the hail, for its plague is exceedingly great'; also 16:19 (the great city split, Babylon remembered) between vv.18 and 20

items.analysis: Slight dependence: the Greek says hailstones weighing about a talent — heavy ice; the French 'comme des lingots' substitutes a solid cast object for a unit of weight, which eases the move to 'rocks'. The canon's own English edition reverts to the weight (KJV), as the library note observes.

items.canon_french: Et j'ai vu un nouveau ciel et une nouvelle terre, car le premier ciel et la première terre s'en sont allés et la mer n'est plus.

reading_quotes.french: Jean a pu voir là ce que l'on pourrait voir d'une fusée qui s'éloigne de la terre. L'on a l'impression que c'est la terre qui s'éloigne alors que c'est le vaisseau dans lequel on est qui s'éloigne.

items.reading_summary: John saw what one sees from a rocket leaving Earth: the Earth seems to go away; then an unfamiliar starry sky ('new heaven') and the approach to another planet ('new earth').

load_bearing.french: le premier ciel et la première terre s'en sont allés
load_bearing.original: ὁ γὰρ πρῶτος οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ πρώτη γῆ ἀπῆλθαν
load_bearing.translit: ho gar prōtos ouranos kai hē prōtē gē apēlthan
load_bearing.gloss: for the first heaven and the first earth went away / departed
load_bearing.comment: aperchomai is literally 'go away, depart'; the canon's French keeps the motion sense that 'passed away' (and library EN) turns into disappearance

load_bearing.french: un nouveau ciel et une nouvelle terre
load_bearing.gloss: a new heaven/sky and a new earth/land
load_bearing.comment: literal

load_bearing.gloss: the sea is no longer
load_bearing.comment: no gloss in the canon; LWTE-2:81 describes the Eternals' planet as having a sea

ellipsis.cut: chapters 17-20 entire (Babylon, the rider on the white horse, the thousand years, the judgment) skipped between 16:21 and 21:1

items.analysis: The verb that carries the reading — the first sky and earth 'went away' — is in the Greek (apēlthan) with the same literal motion sense as the French 's'en sont allés'; standard translations obscure it, the canon's French does not. The reading is thus as available from the Greek as from the French. 'The sea is no more' is left unexplained and sits oddly beside the canon's own description of the destination planet's sea (LWTE-2:81).

items.canon_french: Et j'ai vu la ville sainte, la nouvelle Jérusalem, descendre du ciel, d'auprès de Dieu, prête comme une épouse parée pour son homme.

reading_quotes.french: Vu du vaisseau le primitif a l'impression que la ville vers laquelle le vaisseau va atterrir «descend du ciel» alors que c'est bien évidemment l'engin spatial qui s'en rapproche.

items.reading_summary: The city 'coming down from the sky' is an illusion of relative motion: the craft is approaching the city where it will land.

load_bearing.french: descendre du ciel, d'auprès de Dieu
load_bearing.original: καταβαίνουσαν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ
load_bearing.translit: katabainousan ek tou ouranou apo tou theou
load_bearing.gloss: coming down out of the heaven, from God
load_bearing.comment: the city moves, downward, away from God, toward where humans are

items.analysis: The French is exact. The reading does not rest on the wording but inverts it: the text has the city descend 'from God' to mankind (and 21:3, 'the dwelling of God is with humans'), the canon has the observer travel to a city on the Elohim's planet. The inversion is explained as a primitive's perspective error.

items.ref_note: 21:3a ('I heard a loud voice from the throne saying') omitted
items.canon_french: Voici l'abri de Dieu avec les hommes. Il s'abritera avec eux et eux seront ses peuples, et lui sera le Dieu avec eux.

reading_quotes.french: C'est là la description de la planète des Eternels où tous les hommes que nous sauverons de la catastrophe vivront avec nous éternellement en attendant d'être réimplantés sur la terre

items.reading_summary: The passage describes the planet of the Eternals, where those saved from the catastrophe will live with the Elohim until Earth is habitable again.

load_bearing.french: l'abri de Dieu avec les hommes
load_bearing.original: ἡ σκηνὴ τοῦ θεοῦ μετὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων
load_bearing.translit: hē skēnē tou theou meta tōn anthrōpōn
load_bearing.gloss: the tent/tabernacle of God (is) with humans
load_bearing.comment: skēnē = tent; 'abri' is a free but fair rendering

load_bearing.french: car le premier univers s'en est allé
load_bearing.gloss: the first things went away
load_bearing.comment: Greek neuter plural 'the first things' (former state of affairs); French 'le premier univers' makes it a world — closer to 'the first planet is gone'. The library's base text has no 'car' (hoti is a variant).

load_bearing.gloss: death will be no longer
load_bearing.comment: literal — hook for 'vivront … éternellement'

items.analysis: 'No more death' is a real hook for eternal life. The planetary reading is helped by the French 'le premier univers s'en est allé' (a first world left behind), where the Greek has only ta prōta, 'the former things'. The direction of the tent is again reversed: God's tent is with humans (he 'will tent with them'), i.e. he comes to them; the canon sends them to his planet. The library note records 'le premier univers' and the English edition's 'Yahweh'/'Elohim' substitutions.

items.canon_french: Elohim a été injustement traduit par «dieu», alors qu'il signifiait «ceux qui sont venus du ciel» en hébreu

reading_quotes.french: le mot «dieu » n'est qu'une mauvaise traduction de Elohim signifiant «ceux qui sont venus du ciel»
Dans la Bible originelle, écrite en hébreu, on parle des Elohim, signifiant littéralement «ceux qui sont venus du ciel»

items.reading_summary: Elohim 'meant in Hebrew' / 'literally' means 'those who came from the sky'; 'God' is a mistranslation. Repeated by Raël (3:6, 3:10) and, with 'littéralement', by a testimonial writer (4:87).

load_bearing.gloss: gods / God (plural in form)
load_bearing.comment: the word contains no element meaning 'sky' or 'come'; in Gen 1:1 it stands beside a separate word for the skies (haššāmayim) and governs a singular verb

items.french_variance: TBWTT-3:251: «Elohim, cela veut dire littéralement «venus du ciel» en Hébreu» — LWTE-3:6: «ceux qui sont venus du ciel». TBWTT-2:5 has the longer form.
items.analysis: As a statement about what the Hebrew word means, the gloss has no lexical basis: core woh-claim-0009 already rules that 'those who came from the sky' is a canonical rendering and 'not the consensus lexical derivation' (which runs through Eloah/El), and that presenting it as etymology misexpresses the record. LWTE is where the canon states it most strongly as a meaning ('signifiait … en hébreu', 'littéralement'), inside a chapter that rests its method on dictionary etymologies (3:5-3:26). What the Hebrew does support is only the plural form.

items.canon_french: Ange vient du grec «angelos » qui signifie «messager».

reading_quotes.french: L'on peut donc lire «un messager du ciel m'a contacté». Le surnaturel devient compréhensible.

items.reading_summary: 'Angel' is Greek angelos, 'messenger'.

load_bearing.gloss: messengers
load_bearing.comment: correct lexical sense; library glossary keeps 'angels' by convention and records 'messenger' as the etymology

items.analysis: Correct, and confirmed by the library's glossary entries on angelos. The same holds for Hebrew malʾāḵ (outside this slice).

items.canon_french: il vient de l'araméen «meschîhâ» qui veut dire «oint par le seigneur», ou «sacré, choisi par le seigneur»

reading_quotes.french: l'on peut donc dire que «messie» signifie en définitive «choisi par ceux qui sont venus du ciel»
L'on découvre que «seigneur» vient du latin «senior», qui signifie «le plus âgé ».

items.reading_summary: 'Messiah' = 'anointed/chosen by the lord' → 'chosen by God' → 'chosen by those who came from the sky'; 'seigneur' from Latin senior, 'the eldest'.

load_bearing.gloss: anointed (one)
load_bearing.comment: the Hebrew word means 'anointed' and nothing more; 'par le seigneur' and 'choisi' are added in the dictionary gloss the canon quotes, and the chain to 'ceux qui sont venus du ciel' depends on the Elohim gloss (E-046)

items.analysis: The core sense 'anointed' is right. The rest is a chain of substitutions performed on French dictionary definitions: anointed → 'by the lord' → 'chosen by God' → Elohim-gloss. None of the added links is in the Hebrew/Aramaic word, and the final step inherits the unsupported gloss of Elohim. In the library's Daniel the word is an indefinite 'an anointed one', said of a prince.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] Aramaic məšîḥā is the determined form behind Greek Messias; French 'seigneur' does derive from Latin senior.

items.canon_french: Prophète » vient du grec «prophêtês» qui signifie «celui qui révèle ».

reading_quotes.french: N'oubliez pas quelle est la signification du mot «prophète», son étymologie. Il signifie rappelons-le «celui qui révèle».

items.reading_summary: 'Prophet' = 'he who reveals'. (Same chapter: évangile = good news, église = assembly, religion = that which links, pape/pontife, athée, culte, foi.)

load_bearing.gloss: the prophets (those who speak forth / on behalf of)
load_bearing.comment: pro-phēmi 'speak forth/for'; 'celui qui révèle' is a gloss of function, and aligns the word with 'apocalypse = révélation'

items.analysis: Loose but not wrong in function; the Greek word is 'spokesman', not 'revealer'. The other church-vocabulary etymologies of LWTE-3:13-3:31 (euaggelion 'bonne nouvelle', ekklêsia 'assemblée', katholikos 'universel', religio 'ce qui relie', pontifex/'pont', athéos, cultus, fides) concern French ecclesiastical terms rather than scripture and are not checkable against the library; euangelion and ekklēsia are standard, religio < religare is one of two ancient derivations.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] religio from religare ('bind') is Lactantius' derivation; Cicero derives it from relegere.

items.canon_french: Mais les grands prêtres et les anciens persuadèrent les foules de demander Barabbas et de perdre Jésus.

reading_quotes.french: Les grands prêtres des religions officielles et de la grande presse persuadent les foules que les religions ne sont tolérables que si elles ont quelques millénaires d'ancienneté

items.reading_summary: Analogy: today's 'high priests' of official religion and the press persuade the crowds that only ancient religions are tolerable.

load_bearing.gloss: persuaded the crowds
load_bearing.comment: literal

items.analysis: Rhetorical analogy only; quotation literal.

items.canon_french: Alléluia, qui signifie en hébreu: «loué soit Yahvé».

reading_quotes.french: Oui, loué soit Yahvé de m'avoir donné la force d'accomplir ma mission jusqu'au bout.

items.reading_summary: Alleluia means 'praised be Yahweh' — addressed by Raël to Yahweh as his father.

load_bearing.gloss: praise (plural imperative) Yah
load_bearing.comment: an order to a group — 'praise Yah!' — with the short form of the name; 'loué soit Yahvé' turns it into a passive wish but keeps both elements

items.analysis: Substantially right: verb 'praise' plus the divine name (short form Yah). The grammatical mood differs (plural imperative, not passive optative). In Ps 147:1 the same verse parallels Yah with 'our Elohim' and singular predicates.

items.canon_french: Amen! Ce qui signifie en hébreu : qu'il en soit ainsi!

reading_quotes.french: Mon dernier mot sera encore une démystification étymologique.

items.reading_summary: Amen means 'so be it' in Hebrew.

load_bearing.gloss: amen (Hebrew ʾāmēn: 'firm, sure; truly')
load_bearing.comment: transliterated Hebrew; 'qu'il en soit ainsi' is the liturgical paraphrase (Septuagint genoito), not the root sense 'sure/true'

items.analysis: A conventional paraphrase rather than an etymology: the Hebrew root is 'firm, reliable', and 'so be it' is the usage-gloss. Harmless, but it shows that the chapter's 'étymologies' are dictionary definitions of French words, not analyses of the Hebrew.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] Root ʾmn 'be firm'; LXX often renders ʾāmēn by genoito 'may it be'.

items.ref_note: three verses cited, two words used
items.canon_french: on ne peut continuer à rechercher en même temps la «paix» et la «sécurité» comme nous y invitait Paul de Tarse

reading_quotes.french: l'abolition du service militaire et la mise au service de la paix des militaires de carrière

items.reading_summary: A testimonial writer (a former priest, not Raël or Yahweh) cites Paul for the idea that 'peace' and 'security' cannot both be pursued, in support of abolishing military service.

load_bearing.original: ὅταν λέγωσιν· Εἰρήνη καὶ ἀσφάλεια, τότε αἰφνίδιος αὐτοῖς ἐφίσταται ὄλεθρος
load_bearing.translit: hotan legōsin: Eirēnē kai asphaleia, tote aiphnidios autois ephistatai olethros
load_bearing.gloss: when they say 'Peace and security', then sudden destruction comes upon them
load_bearing.comment: the two nouns are a slogan in the mouths of 'them'; Paul neither recommends nor opposes the pair

items.analysis: Only two words are taken from the passage. In the Greek 'peace and security' is what people say just before sudden destruction; the verse does not set the two aims against each other, and Paul 'invites' nothing concerning them. Fully covered by the library note at 5:3.

items.stated_reference: l'Ecclésiaste, -VII, 10 (inline, not in the citation index)
items.canon_french: Ne dis pas : " Comment se fait-il que le passé fût meilleur que le présent, car ce n'est pas la sagesse qui te fait poser cette question ".

reading_quotes.french: c'est le culte de la tradition et les habitudes séculaires qui ont rendu les gens aveugles

items.reading_summary: A testimonial writer quotes Ecclesiastes against the cult of tradition. No technological reading.
items.analysis: The library holds Ecclesiastes 3 only in Hebrew (ecclesiastes-woh); chapter 7 is not available, so the wording cannot be compared. The citation is by a guest author and absent from the citation index.

items.canon_french: ce qui a été tenu caché depuis la fondation du monde

reading_quotes.french: Quiconque fait une recherche dans la Bible en particulier et confronte les prédictions de la Bible avec les réussites de notre ère scientifique ne fait que dévoiler, constater et comprendre

items.reading_summary: A testimonial writer: science now unveils 'what has been kept hidden since the foundation of the world' — the original mystery (creation of life) — and lists biblical 'signs' with modern fulfilments.

load_bearing.french: ce qui a été tenu caché depuis la fondation du monde
load_bearing.gloss: things hidden from (the) foundation
load_bearing.comment: the library's Greek text has no 'of the world' (kosmou is a variant); the French follows the longer text. TBWTT-4:60 cites the same verse.

items.analysis: The phrase is quoted as a slogan. In the library's base text the Greek stops at 'from the foundation'; 'du monde' reflects the longer reading. Nothing technological hangs on the difference. The accompanying list of 'signs' (blind see, voice to the four corners, healing by laying on of hands = surgery, etc.) cites no verses and is not checkable.
outside_knowledge: [outside knowledge — unverified, needs source] kosmou is absent from some early witnesses and bracketed in critical editions of Matt 13:35.
